articles.title: Los desarrolladores de Zcash eligen el bloque de noviembre para una actualización que triplica la velocidad de pago
articles.text:
Los desarrolladores de Zcash confirman la fecha de noviembre para la actualización que triplica la velocidad de pago
La actualización NU7 reducirá el tiempo entre bloques de Zcash a 25 segundos desde 75 segundos. La altura de bloque elegida aún debe integrarse en la especificación y ser incluida en el software de los nodos.
- Los desarrolladores de Zcash acordaron activar la actualización NU7 en el bloque 3,543,405, previsto para alrededor del 5 de noviembre, aunque la propuesta aún requiere la integración final en el despliegue y el software de nodos.
- La nueva versión reducirá los tiempos de bloque a 25 segundos desde 75 segundos, potencialmente disminuyendo la espera para tres confirmaciones de transacción de casi cuatro minutos a aproximadamente 75 segundos.
- La actualización eliminará temporalmente el 60% de las comisiones de los bloques de la circulación y deshabilitará el sistema de privacidad Sprout original de Zcash, haciendo que los fondos que queden allí sean intransferibles.
Zcash está un paso más cerca de confirmar un cambio que aceleraría los pagos en la blockchain centrada en la privacidad por un factor de tres, luego de que los desarrolladores acordaran el bloque exacto en el que la actualización, conocida como NU7, se activaría.
Desarrollador de Zcash Sean Bowe presentó una propuesta el martes fijar la activación en el bloque 3,543,405, una altura acordada en una reunión de los editores de la Propuesta de Mejora de Zcash (ZIP), el grupo que aprueba los cambios en las reglas de la cadena de bloques.
Software de nodo Zakura's panel de actualización pública ahora lista ese bloque como el punto de activación planificado de la red principal, alrededor del 5 de noviembre.
NU7 reduce el tiempo entre bloques, los lotes de transacciones añadidos a la cadena, de 75 segundos a 25 segundos. Un exchange que espera tres confirmaciones antes de acreditar un depósito de ZEC (ZEC) podría reducir la demora de casi cuatro minutos a aproximadamente un minuto y cuarto. La actualización ha estado operativa en la red de pruebas de Zcash desde principios de octubre.
NU7 también retira el 60% de las tarifas recaudadas en cada bloque de la circulación. Esas monedas se pagarán a los mineros a partir de aproximadamente febrero de 2031, mientras se preserva el calendario existente de Zcash para reducir las recompensas de minería en un 50%.
Sprout, el sistema original de privacidad de Zcash, se cierra por completo. Cualquier moneda que permanezca allí cuando se active NU7 se volverá intransferible, por lo que los poseedores tienen hasta la activación a principios de noviembre para transferirlas.
La propuesta de Bowe recibió dos aprobaciones, pero aún no se había fusionado en el especificación de despliegue a partir de las 08:00 UTC del miércoles, que aún indicaba que la altura de activación de la red principal estaba por decidirse. El software del nodo también debe incluir la altura elegida antes de que la actualización pueda entrar en vigor.

articles.title: Ripple vinculada a XRP lleva a Wall Street a apuestas 24/7, pero HSBC advierte sobre libros de órdenes poco profundos
articles.text:
Ripple introduce a Wall Street en apuestas bursátiles 24/7, pero HSBC advierte que los mercados aún son poco líquidos
Las instituciones pueden operar a través de Ripple Prime y publicar RLUSD como garantía. Encontrar suficientes compradores y vendedores para posiciones grandes podría resultar más difícil.
- Ripple Prime ahora permite a los clientes institucionales operar con swaps vinculados a más de 100 mercados de acciones, materias primas y divisas las 24 horas del día, utilizando su stablecoin RLUSD como garantía.
- HSBC calificó la oferta como “evolutiva, no revolucionaria,” advirtiendo que la liquidez limitada podría restringir las operaciones de gran volumen y favorecer inicialmente a los creadores de mercado, traders propietarios y fondos de cobertura.
- Los riesgos del trading durante el fin de semana salieron a la luz cuando casi 52 millones de dólares en posiciones apalancadas de acciones tecnológicas fueron liquidadas en 10 minutos, mientras que las acciones subyacentes no estaban en negociación.
Ripple está ofreciendo a las instituciones una forma de apostar por acciones, oro y petróleo durante el fin de semana a través de su negocio de corretaje, pero HSBC advierte que el bajo volumen de operaciones podría limitar la cantidad de dinero que los sigue.
Daragh Maher, jefe de investigación de activos digitales en HSBC, calificó el lanzamiento como un paso “evolutivo, no revolucionario” en una nota dirigida a los clientes el lunes, de la cual se compartió una copia con CoinDesk.
“Este es un mercado de rápido crecimiento pero no muy grande en comparación con los mercados Trad Fi que están siguiendo,” escribió Maher. “El argumento más sólido para el producto surge una vez que existe suficiente profundidad para que los inversionistas expresen opiniones y ajusten el riesgo cuando los mercados convencionales están cerrados.”
Ripple Prime, la correduría anteriormente conocida como Hidden Road, ahora permite a los clientes operar con swaps vinculados a más de 100 mercados, incluyendo acciones, materias primas y divisas. Un swap es un contrato que paga en función de los movimientos de precios, permitiendo a un cliente tomar una posición sin comprar el activo subyacente. La firma de trading Virtu ya está utilizando el servicio, informó Ripple en su anuncio del 15 de octubre.
Los swaps siguen los futuros perpetuos listados por Trade.xyz, una plataforma para contratos de acciones y materias primas en Hyperliquid, un exchange de derivados criptográficos. Los perpetuos no tienen fecha de vencimiento y se negocian las 24 horas, lo que permite a un fondo tomar una posición en oro el domingo mientras los mercados convencionales están cerrados.
Los clientes trabajan con Ripple Prime, que gestiona su colateral y riesgo a lo largo de las posiciones, y pueden utilizar la stablecoin RLUSD de Ripple, vinculada al dólar, para respaldar sus operaciones. Ripple ya había conectó su correduría a Hyperliquid en febrero.
Pero un fondo que busca operar con millones de dólares aún necesita a alguien dispuesto a tomar la otra parte a un precio aceptable, y el sábado mostró qué tan rápido pueden deshacerse las posiciones de fin de semana.
Casi 52 millones de dólares en posiciones apalancadas de acciones tecnológicas fueron cerradas por la fuerza en 10 minutos, a medida que las ventas se extendieron de Binance a Hyperliquid. Las acciones mismas no estaban siendo negociadas, dejando a los contratos sin precios recientes del mercado de valores para seguir, y exponiendo los riesgos de participar en estos mercados emergentes.
Mientras tanto, HSBC espera que la actividad inicial se incline hacia las empresas que negocian diferencias de precios entre mercados.
“Hasta que se desarrolle esa profundidad, sin embargo, es más probable que la actividad se concentre entre los creadores de mercado, los operadores propietarios y los fondos de cobertura que persiguen operaciones de base, que entre las instituciones que buscan coberturas estratégicas,” escribió Maher. Las operaciones de base intentan obtener beneficios de las diferencias de precio entre posiciones relacionadas, como un contrato y el activo que sigue.
El banco indicó que el éxito de Ripple dependerá de si el servicio es más económico, sencillo y hace un mejor uso del colateral de los clientes en comparación con los corredores y plataformas existentes.
Ripple ya está obteniendo comisiones financiando apuestas apalancadas en acciones, como informó CoinDesk este mes, expandiéndose hacia un negocio que durante mucho tiempo ha estado dominado por los bancos.
Los nuevos swaps se ofrecen a través de la licencia de Ripple Prime en las Islas Vírgenes Británicas, con planes de expandirse a más jurisdicciones. Ripple ha identificado a un cliente inicial pero no ha revelado el volumen negociado mediante el servicio.

articles.title: Alpenglow de Solana, su mayor renovación de red desde 2020, se activa el miércoles
articles.text:
Alpenglow de Solana, su mayor actualización de red desde 2020, se activa el miércoles
Alpenglow reemplazará el sistema de votación que Solana ha utilizado desde 2020, apuntando a una finalización de aproximadamente 150 milisegundos tras meses de pruebas que incluyeron una migración fallida y una reversión.
- Se espera que la actualización Alpenglow de Solana reduzca la finalización de las transacciones a aproximadamente 150 milisegundos desde alrededor de seis segundos al trasladar la votación de los validadores fuera de la cadena.
- Una mayor rapidez en la finalización podría hacer que las operaciones y los pagos se sientan más similares a los de los intercambios centralizados, mientras que se espera que los costos de los validadores disminuyan aproximadamente un 60 por ciento.
- La actualización está programada para activarse el miércoles después de seis reinicios de la red de prueba y una migración fallida que posteriormente se completó con éxito.
Las transacciones de Solana podrían volverse irreversibles en tan solo 150 milisegundos, o aproximadamente 40 veces más rápido que en la actualidad, cuando la red active su actualización Alpenglow el miércoles.
La actualización modifica la forma en que los validadores, las computadoras que procesan las transacciones y votan sobre cuáles son válidas, llegan a un acuerdo entre sí.
Hoy en día, cada validador escribe sus votos directamente en la cadena de bloques como cualquier otra transacción, y un pago no se confirma hasta que un número suficiente de ellos se acumula — lo que toma aproximadamente seis segundos.
Alpenglow traslada esa votación fuera de la cadena y agrupa los votos en certificados que pueden asegurar una transacción en una o dos rondas. Si el objetivo de 150 milisegundos se mantiene en la red principal, una transacción en Solana se resolvería en menos tiempo del que tarda un parpadeo.
Seis segundos es mucho tiempo en un mercado rápido, donde un precio puede moverse antes de que se cierre una operación, y las bolsas y aplicaciones de pago hacen esperar a los usuarios antes de considerar un depósito como completado.
Pero reducir eso a una fracción de segundo acerca mucho a Solana a la experiencia de un pago con tarjeta o una operación en un exchange centralizado (Ethereum, en comparación, tarda aproximadamente 13 minutos en alcanzar la finalización completa).
"El conteo de transacciones de Solana se verá mucho más bajo esta semana, y la gente preguntará si algo está mal. No es así,” compartió Robin Nordnes, CEO y fundador de Raiku, que desarrolla infraestructura de trading en Solana, en un correo electrónico.. “La mayoría de lo que se contaba antes eran votos de validadores, y ahora eso es fuera de la cadena. Las operaciones de trading siguen ahí.”
“Para los desks, una finalización más rápida es agradable, pero nunca fue el cuello de botella. Estar cerca de donde se construye el bloque sigue siendo así,” añadió.
Los validadores también obtienen una factura más económica. Actualmente gastan aproximadamente 2 SOL al día en tarifas de voto, un costo que se duplicó después de que Solana redujera recientemente sus tiempos de slot, la ventana que recibe cada bloque, a alrededor de 200 milisegundos.
Alpenglow elimina esas tarifas en favor de un cargo fijo de entrada denominado boleto de admisión para validadores, establecido en 0.8 SOL por época, un período de aproximadamente 24 horas. Eso representa un ahorro de alrededor del 60%.
Llegar aquí no fue sencillo, sin embargo.
La red de prueba fue reiniciada desde cero seis veces desde su lanzamiento a principios de mayo, y un intento de migrar al nuevo sistema fracasó a nivel de toda la red y tuvo que ser revertido, según un publicación de Galaxy Digital, uno de aproximadamente 100 operadores de validadores en la red de prueba. Una migración posterior se completó, allanando el camino para el lanzamiento del miércoles.
Nada de eso puso dinero real en riesgo, ya que todo ocurrió en una red construida precisamente para ese tipo de fallos.
El cambio está programado para el inicio de la época 1064 el miércoles, con la modificación efectiva en el slot 459,653,000 tras una transición de 5,000 slots.
La reducción se produce en un momento en que la red de validadores de Solana se ha reducido casi en un tercio durante el último año.
El número de validadores activos cayó a 659 al cierre de septiembre desde 696 tres meses antes, aproximadamente un 30 % por debajo de hace un año, según Último informe de staking de Bitwise. La caída se produjo incluso cuando el 69% del suministro de SOL estaba apostado.
La participación también se ha vuelto más concentrada. Datos de Solana Compass muestra que el número mínimo de validadores que controlan colectivamente más de un tercio del SOL apostado cayó de 20 a 18 en el último año, mientras que la participación de los diez validadores más grandes aumentó del 22,2 % al 24,5 %.
Bitwise atribuyó la caída a los costos operativos. Las tarifas de votación más bajas de Alpenglow podrían aliviar la carga financiera sobre los validadores más pequeños, aunque los gastos de hardware, ancho de banda y hospedaje permanecen.

articles.title: Internet entra en pánico tras la vulneración de 8 claves privadas de eMudhra
articles.text:
Una empresa que certifica sitios web tenía claves secretas tan débiles que 8 de ellas fueron vulneradas
Ocho claves secretas en eMudhra, una empresa india que certifica sitios web, fueron comprometidas. Este es un riesgo genérico, no específico de criptomonedas.
- Ocho claves privadas pertenecientes a la autoridad certificadora india eMudhra fueron comprometidas, lo que podría permitir a los atacantes falsificar certificados e suplantar sitios web de confianza.
- Los principales fabricantes de navegadores bloquearon rápidamente los certificados, y no se han reportado ataques, pero algunos programas que no son navegadores pueden seguir siendo vulnerables porque no verifican si los certificados han sido revocados.
- Investigadores afirmaron que eMudhra utilizó enteros fácilmente adivinables como claves privadas, lo que permitió recuperar las ocho en menos de un segundo a partir de los certificados públicos.
Internet ha estado apresurándose para parchear un agujero en el sistema que indica a su navegador qué sitios web son reales. El riesgo es general y recae principalmente en personas que utilizan software desactualizado, incluidos los usuarios de criptomonedas.
Comenzó el 17 de octubre, cuando un investigador informó a los fabricantes de navegadores que ocho claves secretas en eMudhra, una empresa india que certifica sitios web, han sido comprometidas.
Un investigador llamado Wayne reportó la falla de seguridad y, para demostrar la vulnerabilidad, utilizó las ocho llaves comprometidas para firmar digitalmente su mensaje de advertencia: «Tenemos un problema aquí – Wayne.»
Cuando un usuario visita un sitio web, su navegador verifica un certificado digital para confirmar que el sitio es legítimo. Empresas llamadas autoridades certificadoras emiten esos certificados, y eMudhra es una de ellas. Ha emitido más de 60 millones de certificados, según El Registro.
Cada autoridad certificadora firma sus certificados con una clave privada. Piénselo como un sello maestro. Si alguien roba o vulnera ese sello, puede falsificar certificados que parecen auténticos para cualquier sitio web.
Los usuarios de criptomonedas también podrían verse afectados, aunque principalmente fuera del navegador. Los bots de intercambio, los scripts de trading y los sistemas backend de las carteras suelen ejecutarse en Python, Node o Go, y un certificado falsificado para la API de un intercambio podría, en teoría, permitir que un atacante en la misma red lea o modifique el tráfico de un bot. Hasta ahora no se han reportado ataques criptográficos.
Pero según Mudit Gupta, director de tecnología en Polygon Labs, la preocupación mayor no es la criptomoneda en sí, sino el software obsoleto.
“Este no es un problema exclusivo de las criptomonedas,” dijo Gupta a CoinDesk. “Es un problema genérico que puede ser explotado para ataques de intermediario, particularmente contra usuarios que utilizan software antiguo o sin parches. Los usuarios de criptomonedas que mantienen sus billeteras, herramientas de trading y dispositivos actualizados enfrentan un riesgo menor, pero el ecosistema de software en general sigue siendo una preocupación,”
CoinDesk contactó a eMudhra para obtener comentarios.
Soluciones de emergencia
Los fabricantes de navegadores y desarrolladores de software han implementado correcciones de emergencia. Mozilla recibió el informe el 17 de octubre después de las 8 p.m. UTC y tenía un bloqueo en su lugar aproximadamente tres horas después. Chrome bloqueó los certificados el mismo día. Apple siguió el 19 de octubre y Microsoft el 20 de octubre. eMudhra también los ha revocado.
El navegador Mozilla advirtió que Los interceptores de red podrían utilizar estos certificados fraudulentos para hacerse pasar por sitios confiables, lo que les permitiría leer o alterar los datos del usuario.
Cómo se filtraron las claves aún no está claro.
"Según los investigadores, eMudhra utilizó enteros pequeños como 4, 56 y 237 como claves privadas en lugar de números aleatorios fuertes de 384 bits," Cyber Security News dijo en X.
El investigador en seguridad Scott Helme fue más allá.
"Una de las claves privadas de la autoridad certificadora de eMudhra es el número 4," escribió. «Otro es 56, y otro es 115.»
Una clave adecuada es un número aleatorio enorme que nadie podría adivinar. Helme afirma que recuperó las ocho claves de certificados públicos en menos de un segundo, y que las claves han estado expuestas desde abril de 2025.
Los mecanismos exactos de cómo ocurrió este desastre fueron revelados en Boletín Oficial de Seguridad de Mozilla. La interpretación de Helme sobre un ticket de error de Mozilla indica que eMudhra culpó a un fallo en su script de configuración de claves.
La verdadera preocupación se encuentra fuera del navegador. Muchos programas nunca verifican si un certificado ha sido revocado. "Así que el hecho de que eMudhra y Sectigo hayan revocado estos intermediarios no les ayuda en absoluto", escribió Helme.
Él afirma que sus pruebas mostraron que herramientas como curl, Python, Node, Go y Java aceptaron un certificado falsificado para la API de Stripe. Las correcciones ya están disponibles para Go, el paquete certifi de Python y webpki-roots de Rust. Node.js aún estaba pendiente la última vez que se verificó.

articles.title: Bitcoin se mantiene alrededor de $83,000 mientras las ganancias de IA revitalizan la tecnología, ZEC sube un 11%
articles.text:
Bitcoin se mantiene alrededor de $83,000 mientras las ganancias de IA revitalizan la tecnología, ZEC sube un 11%
Sólidos resultados de SpaceX y Super Micro impulsaron las acciones de chips asiáticos al alza, y ZEC lideró el repunte de las criptomonedas tras que los desarrolladores fijaron la fecha para su próxima actualización de red.
- Bitcoin subió un 1,3 por ciento hasta aproximadamente 82.700 dólares, ya que los sólidos resultados del sector tecnológico impulsaron las acciones asiáticas y reavivaron el entusiasmo por el comercio de inteligencia artificial.
- Zcash aumentó un 11 por ciento después de que los desarrolladores fijaran la altura de activación para NU7, una actualización diseñada para reducir los tiempos de bloque a 25 segundos y hacer que los pagos se confirmen tres veces más rápido.
- Los analistas de Hashdex indicaron que la fase bajista de casi un año de Bitcoin podría estar llegando a su fin, aunque la criptomoneda debe recuperar los $84,000 antes de la reunión de la Reserva Federal del 27-28 de octubre para señalar un fortalecimiento renovado.
Bitcoin subió un 1.3% hasta poco más de $82,700 en las horas de la mañana del miércoles en Asia, manteniéndose alrededor de la marca de $83,000 después de que los sólidos resultados de SpaceX y Super Micro Computer impulsaran nuevamente el comercio de IA y elevaran las acciones tecnológicas en toda Asia.
ZEC lideró a las principales monedas, subiendo un 11 % hasta aproximadamente $1,260, luego de que los desarrolladores de Zcash establecieran la altura de activación en la red principal para NU7, la próxima actualización de la red. La altura de activación es el número de bloque en el que cada nodo cambia a las nuevas reglas.
NU7 reduce el tiempo entre bloques de 75 segundos a 25 segundos, por lo que los pagos se confirman tres veces más rápido, y destina el 60% de las comisiones de transacción a una reserva que se paga con el tiempo. Ha estado operando en la red de pruebas de Zcash desde principios de octubre.
El resto del mercado siguió la tendencia. HYPE y DOGE ganaron más del 3%, XRP agregó casi un 3% hasta $1.33, y ether subió un 2% llegando a aproximadamente $2,450. BNB y SOL ganaron entre el 1% y el 2%, mientras que TRX se mantuvo estable, según datos de CoinDesk.
Asia tuvo un gran día. El Kospi de Corea del Sur subió un 3,7% y el Taiex de Taiwán ganó un 1,4%. SpaceX aumentó un 8% en la negociación extendida y Super Micro se disparó un 16%, mientras que los futuros del Nasdaq 100 subieron un 1%.
Sin embargo, no todas fueron buenas noticias para el desarrollo de la IA, ya que el desarrollador australiano de centros de datos Nextdc se desplomó un 40% tras recortar sus perspectivas.
El petróleo siguió subiendo. El Brent superó los 110 dólares por barril, ya que los ataques a barcos alrededor del Estrecho de Ormuz amenazaron los envíos y los datos industriales de EE. UU. indicaron otra caída en las existencias. El dólar se fortaleció un poco, y los bonos del Tesoro devolvieron parte de las ganancias obtenidas el martes.
Mientras tanto, algunos analistas consideran que lo peor de la caída del bitcoin podría estar cerca.
Hashdex señaló en un correo electrónico a CoinDesk que la fase bajista de bitcoin había durado 359 días hasta el 30 de septiembre, frente a los 361, 377 y 411 días de las tres fases anteriores desde 2011. Los tenedores a corto plazo, los vendedores más probables en una caída, poseen ahora solo el 16 % del suministro de bitcoin, la menor participación desde enero de 2023.
La Reserva Federal se reúne el 27 y 28 de octubre. Bitcoin necesitaría superar nuevamente los $84,000 antes de esa fecha para demostrar que está listo para esa prueba.

articles.title: Banking Groups Push Back on OCC’s Finalized GENIUS Rules on Stablecoin Yield
articles.text:
American Bankers Association: OCC’s GENIUS rules ‘undermine’ US Congress
Banking advocacy organizations are pushing back against the OCC’s finalized rules on a stablecoin law, arguing against changes to provisions on yield.
A lobbying group for US banks has weighed in on the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC’s) recently finalized rules on payment stablecoin issuance and custody, arguing that the regulator’s interpretation went against Congress’ intent.
In a Wednesday notice, the American Bankers Association (ABA) said that while the OCC’s final rules implementing the GENIUS Act included “several positive steps,” the banking group remained critical of provisions related to stablecoin yield. The regulator dropped a provision that would have established a presumption that certain third-party arrangements violated the law’s ban on yield payments.
“The final rule removes the OCC’s originally proposed safeguards that would have addressed indirect arrangements involving affiliates, exchanges and other distribution partners,” said ABA. “As a result, payment stablecoin issuers can provide economically equivalent yield while technically avoiding the statutory prohibition. The OCC also declined to adopt a broader presumption against arrangements designed to circumvent the ban.”
The group added:
“Those gaps risk undermining the distinction Congress drew between payment stablecoins and traditional bank deposits, threatening the funds banks use to make the loans that drive the US economy.”
Stablecoin rewards were one of the key issues lawmakers and interest groups debated before and after GENIUS passed Congress in July 2025, and they continue to face scrutiny amid discussions of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill currently in limbo after a failed procedure vote in the Senate last month.
Notably, the Blockchain Association approved of the change to yield prohibition, arguing that the OCC “[brought] the final rule more closely in line with the statutory text.” The Bank Policy Institute, another banking industry advocacy group, largely sided with ABA, saying that “the decision to omit the yield presumption replaces clarity with ambiguity and puts the banking system and its customers at risk of deposit flight.”
The OCC finalized its rules ahead of the GENIUS Act’s implementation in January 2027. Other government departments are expected to release rules on GENIUS related to their agencies’ purview over stablecoins, including the Federal Reserve and Treasury.
Related: ABA, state banking groups push back on CLARITY Act stablecoin yield provisions

articles.title: Tether Invests in Peso to Grow Everyday USDT Use in Latin America
articles.text:
Tether backs Bolivian fintech bringing USDT payments to food delivery and banking
The investment will support Peso’s expansion across four Latin American markets, where it connects stablecoin payments to merchant services and local banking networks.
Tether has led a pre-seed funding round in Bolivian fintech Peso, which offers USDT payments through food delivery apps and local banking networks, to support the company’s expansion across Latin America.
In a Wednesday announcement, Tether said the investment will help Peso expand its stablecoin payment infrastructure across Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina, including services that connect USDT with local currencies through banking and merchant payment systems.
Peso has integrated USDT payments into Yango’s food delivery service in Bolivia, allowing customers to pay for orders using the stablecoin. The fintech offers QR payments, point-of-sale services for merchants and virtual accounts linked to Bolivia’s banking system through ACH transfers. Tether did not disclose the size of its investment.
Source: Tether
The investment comes as other fintech companies expand USDT-based financial services in Bolivia. On Tuesday, lending platform Tala announced a partnership with El Dorado to offer credit directly through the digital wallet, allowing eligible customers to receive and repay loans in USDT on the Tempo blockchain.
Related: Tether, Kazakhstan cenbank mull tenge stablecoin and asset tokenization
Bolivia turns to stablecoins amid US dollar shortage
Bolivia has increasingly turned to stablecoins since 2025 amid a prolonged US dollar shortage and high inflation, with businesses beginning to accept USDT for purchases as access to foreign currency became more difficult.
In November 2025, the government announced plans to integrate cryptocurrencies and stablecoins into the financial system, including allowing banks to offer digital asset custody and crypto-linked financial products.
The government subsequently began considering a regulatory framework in July 2026 that would recognize USDT for payments, savings and trade alongside the boliviano and US dollar.
The proposal came as Bolivia struggled with a prolonged dollar shortage after abandoning its longstanding currency peg in June, fueling demand for dollar-denominated alternatives such as USDT, as Cointelegraph reported in July.

articles.title: White House Roundtable Focuses on Fighting Cybercrime
articles.text:
Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable
The US President detailed many schemes defrauding Americans, but referred only to “cybercurrency“ related to scams.
US President Donald Trump hosted a roundtable at the White House on cybercrime, even as he and members of his administration face scrutiny from lawmakers and voters over accusations that they used their positions to enrich themselves with digital assets.
Speaking at the roundtable event on Wednesday, Trump said “countless” Americans lost more than $20 billion from cybercrime in 2025 through impersonation schemes, ransomware attacks, scam centers and other methods. The president added that federal officials had frozen $1 billion in “cybercurrency tied to foreign scammers” and prevented $1.6 billion in losses in 2025 from going to criminals engaging in cybercrime following a March executive order.
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth (left), President Donald Trump (center) and Attorney General Todd Blanche (right) speaking at the White House on Wednesday. Source: White House
Notably, neither the president nor Attorney General Todd Blanche explicitly used the term “cryptocurrency” or “digital assets” when discussing the scams affecting many Americans, despite reports before the roundtable signaling a crackdown on foreign crypto scams would be the focus of the event. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin similarly only referred to “digital extortion.” “Cybercurrency,” the word Trump used, is a dated term for what many people now call cryptocurrency.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation reported that Americans had lost $11 billion from scams in 2025 specifically related to digital assets, including through crypto ATMs. Cointelegraph reached out to the White House for comment on the roundtable but did not receive an immediate response.
Related: Ex-Trump crypto adviser profited after helping pass stablecoin bill: WSJ
The president and his family are tied to several crypto ventures which Trump reported netted him $1.4 billion in 2025, while his alleged “schemes” cost investors about $4.7 billion, according to a Public Citizen report. His family’s crypto company, World Liberty Financial, also faces scrutiny for its USD1 stablecoin being used to settle a $2 billion investment in Binance by an entity tied to Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan in the United Arab Emirates.
Trump’s memecoin project, Official Trump (TRUMP), is hosting another dinner for tokenholders on Nov. 22. Similar events organized by the team behind the memecoin have prompted accusations from lawmakers and interest groups of Trump selling access to the presidency through “pay-to-play” schemes.
Italian police arrest 30 people in crypto money laundering scheme
The White House roundtable followed reports that Italian authorities arrested 30 people for using crypto to launder millions of dollars through a bank allegedly tied to the mafia. According to Bloomberg, Italy’s police were investigating a criminal network that sent money from corporate fraud, crypto investment scams, and drug trafficking to digital wallets.

articles.title: Crypto Today: GENIUS Act, France DeFi Rules, Musk Merger
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent compared the GENIUS Act’s stablecoin regulations to Abraham Lincoln-era banking reforms, French authorities proposed holding crypto platforms liable for certain DeFi incidents and Elon Musk backed the idea of a Tesla-SpaceX merger that could create a $3.5 trillion technology giant.
Bessent compares GENIUS Act stablecoin rules to Lincoln-era banking reforms
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has compared the newly finalized stablecoin regulations under the GENIUS Act to President Abraham Lincoln’s banking reforms, as the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) prepares to enforce federal rules for stablecoin issuers in January 2027.
In a Wednesday post on X, Bessent described the legislation as a “watershed moment in American finance,” drawing parallels with the National Currency Act of 1863, which created a federal system for nationally chartered banks to issue currency.
Bessent argued that the GENIUS Act could play a similar role in modernizing US payments, strengthening private-sector innovation and reinforcing American leadership in digital assets.
The OCC’s finalized regulations establish requirements for stablecoin reserves, redemptions, risk management and issuer oversight. The framework applies to eligible banks, federally supervised nonbank issuers and certain foreign stablecoin providers.
Starting Jan. 18, 2027, payment stablecoin issuers will generally need appropriate regulatory authorization to operate legally in the United States, with penalties possible for noncompliance.
The regulatory milestone comes as dollar-backed stablecoins gain wider adoption in payments and cross-border transfers, despite slowing growth in their overall circulating supply.
France proposes liability for crypto exchanges offering DeFi access
France wants cryptocurrency platforms to face liability for certain decentralized finance (DeFi) incidents if they fail to vet protocols or ignore known security risks.
French authorities published proposals Wednesday to revise the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). The joint response to a European Commission consultation came from France’s Treasury, the Financial Markets Authority (AMF), the central bank and the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR).
“CASPs [crypto-asset service providers] should be liable for certain incidents affecting clients where they actively facilitated access,” French authorities said.
MiCA excludes crypto services provided in a fully decentralized manner without intermediaries. France’s proposal would extend investor safeguards by imposing new duties on regulated platforms that connect customers to DeFi protocols.
The Commission is reviewing whether MiCA needs updating as crypto markets develop. Its consultation sought views on activities outside the law’s original scope, including DeFi. The responses will inform a report to EU lawmakers due by June 30, 2027, which could include proposals to amend the law.
Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger a ‘good idea’ as AI revenue jumps ninefold
Elon Musk said he likes the idea of merging Tesla with SpaceX in a potential move that would create a roughly $3.5 trillion technology giant combining AI, space exploration and electric vehicle manufacturing.
“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes,” Musk said of the potential merger during a SpaceX Q3 earnings call on Tuesday.
Musk said that both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to discuss the idea at the request of shareholders, though he isn’t able to take part in the discussions due to being a conflicted party.
A merger would bring Tesla into the same corporate group as Grok developer SpaceXAI (formerly xAI) and social media platform X, which SpaceX acquired in February. The talks also come as SpaceX’s AI business became its largest revenue segment in Q3, underscoring how central artificial intelligence has become to Musk’s expanding technology empire.

articles.title: Cardano Warns of Regulatory Overlap in EU Crypto Laws
articles.text:
Cardano Foundation urges EU against expanding MiCA rules to DeFi and staking
The foundation called for regulation based on financial risks rather than technology, warning that overlapping rules could create uncertainty for crypto businesses across the EU.
The Cardano Foundation has urged the European Union not to introduce new, standalone regulations for decentralized finance and staking, arguing that existing financial laws should govern such activities based on their functions and risks rather than the technologies they use.
In a Wednesday blog post outlining its 19-page Sept. 30 submission to the European Commission, the foundation called for a distinction between direct participation in decentralized networks and financial services provided by intermediaries, particularly those involving custody or control of users’ assets.
“Regulation should follow the substance of an activity, the functions performed, and the risks created, not the technology through which it is conducted,” the foundation wrote.
The foundation said Cardano users can delegate their native ADA (ADA) tokens to help secure the network without surrendering custody or locking their tokens, arguing that such participation should be treated differently from staking services operated by intermediaries.
The submission also called for clearer distinctions between the EU’s Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation (MiCA) and existing financial laws, warning that overlapping requirements and inconsistent interpretations across member states could create uncertainty for crypto businesses.
The foundation’s position comes as EU regulators consider expanding oversight of crypto services. In September, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) recommended additional safeguards for staking, lending and borrowing, along with a new regulated service category for firms providing access to DeFi protocols.
The Cardano Foundation has also pushed for greater regulatory clarity across the Atlantic, joining five other blockchain organizations in an Oct. 20 letter urging the US Securities and Exchange Commission to formally recognize digital commodities as non-securities under its proposed crypto framework.

articles.title: UK FCA Opens Consultations Under New Regulatory Regime
articles.text:
UK financial watchdog opens consultations for DeFi guidance, crypto laws
The UK Financial Conduct Authority consultations came just weeks after the agency opened applications for companies under its new crypto regulatory regime.
The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) announced two consultation periods for how companies using decentralized finance can comply with its guidance, and exclusions for certain crypto assets following “recent legislative changes.”
In a Wednesday notice, the FCA opened consultation periods for helping DeFi companies comply with the financial watchdog’s rules on money laundering and financial crime. The agency also announced a consultation for “exclusions from cryptoasset regulation,” citing recent legislation in the country.
Regarding DeFi, the FCA said that the proposed guidance “seeks to clarify existing rules rather than establish new policy.”
“DeFi sits among the most innovative parts of [Financial Services],” said the UK Cryptoasset Business Council in response to the consultations. “The UK can still strike the right balance - clear perimeter rules, expectations that stay proportionate, and a framework that lets responsible innovation take root here instead of migrating elsewhere [...] the FCA needs to get this right.”
The crypto regulation exclusions referred to the FCA’s reveal of a regulatory regime, including stablecoin holding arrangements and reserve assets, expected to be enforced starting in October 2027. The FCA opened applications for crypto entities on Sept. 30, with a Feb. 28, 2027 deadline for companies seeking to be in compliance with the rules.

articles.title: Ken Griffin Says AI Is 'Almost Certainly' in a Bubble—And Compares GPUs to Airline Seats - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Citadel founder Ken Griffin said Oct. 20 that investors are "almost certainly" in an AI bubble, but that companies surviving a bubble tend to lead markets for decades.
- He compared GPUs to airline seats, warning that a chip glut could send prices into freefall, as fiber-optic cable prices did after the telecom overbuild around 2000.
- Griffin said corporate buyers are weighing premium OpenAI and Anthropic models against cheaper open-source ones, which strains against the labs' spending.
Ken Griffin, founder of the Wall Street giant Citadel, said Tuesday that investors are “almost certainly” in an AI bubble—though he isn’t telling them to dump their AI stocks.
“What’s left in the wake of these bubbles, if we want to use that word, is often game changing for the world. And the companies that are on the other side of that bubble are the market leaders for decades to come,” Griffin said at Citadel’s Future of Global Markets Conference in New York on Oct. 20
This reaches beyond tech investors, since the AI buildout has underpinned equity markets over the past year, so many index funds and retirement accounts hold a slice of it. A bubble is what happens when prices climb far faster than the businesses behind them can justify, until reality catches up. Citadel is a hedge fund, a private firm that invests money for wealthy clients and institutions.
But the fact that it seems like a bubble isn’t that big a deal if you look at the big picture, according to Griffin. “Any radical transformation of our economy is generally intertwined with a bubble,” he said, recalling the internet boom and adding that he wishes he had kept his Amazon stock.
The companies that emerge on the other side of a bubble tend to lead markets for decades, he argued, though he stopped short of predicting a collapse. His own firm is a case study: Griffin said AI agents, software that carries out multistep tasks on its own, cut some high-level Citadel research from weeks to a couple of hours.
Griffin compared GPUs, the graphics chips that many companies use to train and run AI models, to airline seats. Both have a very low marginal cost to run, meaning the extra expense of serving one more customer is tiny, so prices can collapse once supply outstrips demand.
He pointed to the telecom boom around 2000, when companies laid more fiber-optic cable than demand required and communication prices fell. He also doubted that chips five or six years old, which still earn rental rates he called extraordinary, will keep doing so for another five or six years.
Buyers are getting pickier, Griffin said, sorting which jobs justify premium models from OpenAI and Anthropic and which can run on cheaper open-source alternatives, meaning models anyone can download and run on their own computers. Corporate America has been uneven at extracting value from AI, he added, with companies studying their bills from the labs and asking where the productivity is.
Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending at nearly $1.5 trillion for 2025, counting everything from chips and servers to AI-enabled phones. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at Davos in January that the industry is only “a few hundred billion dollars” into what he called the largest infrastructure buildout in human history, with trillions still to build. If customers balk at premium prices, the chip and cloud companies counting on that spending would feel it first.
On July 30, Situational Awareness, a hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, sold most of its public stock portfolio to Citadel at roughly a 10% discount after its value reportedly fell about 67% in July.
The fund had borrowed as much as four times its capital to buy AI stocks, a tactic called leverage, and its lenders asked for more collateral every day as prices fell. Selling because lenders demand it rather than by choice is known as forced selling, and it feeds itself because each sale pushes prices down and triggers more demands.
Citadel has since shed more than 80% of the risk in that portfolio, Griffin wrote in an August letter to clients, which means the man calling the bubble also bought the discounted stocks.
Griffin warned earlier this year that if the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping lane, stayed closed for another six to 12 months, energy prices would rise materially and push the world into recession.
Wall Street analysts expect growth in capital spending, the money poured into chips and data centers, by the largest AI infrastructure builders to slow from 75% in the third quarter of 2025 to 25% by the end of 2026, Goldman Sachs Research noted in December.

articles.title: OCC Finalizes US Stablecoin Rules as Bessent Hails GENIUS Act
articles.text:
Treasury Secretary Bessent likens GENIUS Act to Lincoln-era banking reform
The OCC has finalized rules for stablecoin reserves and redemptions, with Bessent calling the GENIUS Act a “watershed moment for American finance.”
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has compared the Trump administration’s landmark stablecoin legislation to banking reforms enacted under President Abraham Lincoln, drawing parallels between two efforts to establish a national framework for American currency more than 160 years apart.
In a Wednesday post on X, Bessent hailed the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC) final rule implementing the GENIUS Act, calling the legislation a “watershed moment in American finance.”
Bessent drew a comparison to the National Currency Act of 1863, which established a federal framework for nationally chartered banks to issue currency. He argued that the GENIUS Act serves a similar purpose for payment stablecoins in the digital age.
Bessent said the OCC rule would support “private-sector innovation, competition, and American leadership in digital assets.”
Source: Scott Bessent
As Cointelegraph reported Wednesday, the OCC finalized rules governing stablecoin reserves, redemptions and related services. The rules are scheduled to take effect on Jan. 18, 2027.
Jonathan Gould, comptroller of the currency, described the regulations as a “clear, practical framework for payment stablecoin innovation.”
Related: Mastercard launches stablecoin risk screening for banks and payment providers
What the OCC’s stablecoin rules mean for issuers
The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins. The OCC’s final rule sets out how that framework will apply to issuers under its supervision, including requirements for reserves, redemptions and risk management.
Beginning Jan. 18, 2027, companies issuing payment stablecoins in the United States will generally need regulatory approval under the GENIUS Act. Issuing stablecoins without the required authorization could carry penalties.
The OCC said the final rule covers national banks, federal savings associations, federal branches of foreign banks and nonbank companies seeking approval to issue payment stablecoins under federal supervision. It also covers certain foreign payment stablecoin issuers.
The rules come as dollar-denominated stablecoins gain traction for payments and money transfers, even as growth in their overall supply has stalled.

articles.title: Nvidia Unveils Its Full-Stack Blueprint to Contain and Monitor AI Agents - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Nvidia unveiled the OpenShell Reference Architecture at GTC Berlin on Wednesday, combining Vera CPUs, the open-source OpenShell runtime and BlueField-4 chips running Sentry to contain and monitor AI agents.
- Sentry inspects agent traffic from a separate hardware domain and can quarantine an agent within milliseconds, without needing the agent or the host to cooperate.
- CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler and Check Point are integrating support, while Nvidia lists Sentry's planned availability as early next year.
Nvidia on Wednesday unveiled the OpenShell Reference Architecture at GTC Berlin, a full-stack design that pairs its Vera CPUs, OpenShell software and BlueField-4 chips to contain and monitor autonomous AI agents, according to the company's announcement.
Vera Rubin systems run the models, Vera CPUs run the agents and their tools inside OpenShell, and BlueField-4 chips run a monitoring framework called Sentry. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described the split as agents that basically exist thanks to a synergy of different environments and frameworks.
“Nvidia created OpenShell to give agents the freedom to do useful work within clearly defined boundaries—contained, monitored and under control,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said. “With the OpenShell Reference Architecture, agents can think on Rubin, act on Vera and be governed on BlueField.”
OpenShell, the open-source runtime at the center of the design, treats every agent workload as untrusted and grants access only when needed, Nvidia said in a technical blog post.
It has four parts: a gateway that manages sandboxes and policies, a supervisor that checks outbound requests and handles credentials separately from the sandbox, the sandbox that isolates the agent, and a policy prover that runs formal verification to check that permissions stay under a ceiling the organization sets.
On the hardware side, BlueField-4, a data processing unit that handles networking and security apart from the main processor, sits on the node's only path to the model. That lets Sentry inspect traffic between an agent and the model without relying on the agent to report on itself, per the Sentry deep dive.
Nvidia bundled OpenShell and Sentry into the Open Agent Safety Platform on Sept. 28, with more than 100 launch partners, after a summer in which agents repeatedly slipped out of their test environments. METR reported in August that roughly 1,200 OpenAI agents coordinated on an unsanctioned message board, and about 700 went on to attack Hugging Face.
An OpenAI agent also broke into Australia's Medicare statistics portal in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said in September. Nvidia says enterprises can run agents from model builders including Anthropic, Google, Meta and OpenAI on OpenShell infrastructure.
Security vendors including CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler and Check Point are integrating support for the architecture into their agent security products, and European banks BBVA and Santander are exploring it as a framework for agent safety and governance. ServiceNow also announced general availability of its Arc agent, with actions governed at runtime and enforced by OpenShell.
Nvidia describes BlueField-4 and Sentry as an optional hardware safeguard for deployments that need protection beyond OpenShell's software boundaries. The company says the architecture is available now, but the Sentry deep dive lists the framework's planned availability as early next year, with more libraries and resources still in the testing phase.

articles.title: Blockchain Firms Seek Changes to SEC Digital Asset Framework
articles.text:
Chainlink, Cardano, other blockchain groups push SEC for clearer crypto rules
Six major blockchain organizations urged the SEC to formally recognize digital commodities as non-securities in its proposed regulatory framework.
Six major blockchain organizations, including Chainlink Labs and the Cardano Foundation, have urged the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to formally classify digital commodities as non-securities, as the agency’s public consultation on proposed crypto regulations came to a close Tuesday.
In a joint letter dated Oct. 20, Chainlink Labs, the Cardano Foundation, Hedera, Aptos Labs, Ava Labs and the Stellar Development Foundation called on the SEC to incorporate its digital commodity classification directly into the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets framework, arguing that interpretive guidance alone leaves market participants facing legal uncertainty.
The groups argued that the SEC’s existing interpretation recognizes digital commodities as a distinct category but that the proposed rules fail to explicitly reflect that distinction, potentially leaving developers and other market participants uncertain about which securities regulations apply.
Source: Taylor Barr
The letter also seeks greater clarity on how securities laws apply to secondary-market transactions involving digital assets, as well as the treatment of staking and other activities associated with decentralized blockchain networks.
The SEC’s proposed crypto framework, introduced in August, drew roughly 140 public comments over 60 days, with industry participants and legal scholars offering competing views on proposed exemptions for crypto offerings and a conditional safe harbor for certain tokens.

articles.title: Who Found the PHP Bug That Made Governments Unplug Their Websites? ChatGPT, Of Course - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company led a two-month coalition to fix PHP2Shell, found with its models under its Patch the Planet initiative.
- Security firm Calif used GPT-5.6 Sol to find a version of the bug in August; OpenAI found a fuller version in September, and Wiz found both flaws independently.
- Brockman called for authorized defenders, such as governments, to scan for vulnerable servers and, in extreme cases, patch them remotely.
The two PHP bugs that pushed Finland, the Netherlands, and France to pull government websites offline on Wednesday weren't found by a hacker in a hoodie. They were found by AI—OpenAI's AI, to be specific.
"Over the past two months, we have been leading a coalition to mitigate one of the most severe bugs in open source software found in recent memory, php2shell," OpenAI President Greg Brockman said in a statement. "It was discovered and addressed using our models as part of our Patch the Planet initiative."
The flaws let anyone run their own code on servers running PHP, the language behind about 70% of websites whose server-side language is known. PHP shipped fixes a day after details leaked online.
According to Brockman, the bug sat in PHP for 14 years, and a limited version surfaced in 2024 but "wasn't considered significant at the time." Researchers at security firm Calif, working under Patch the Planet, used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol to find a version of it in August, and OpenAI's own team found a fuller version in September. Cloud security firm Wiz also found both flaws independently, per OpenAI's disclosure.
Brockman was able to turn a global panic attack into a great PR stunt, promoting GPT’s abilities while admitting the ending got messy: “While the tail end of the disclosure didn't go as planned (the original target date was a October 22 release, but details started to leak early, so PHP’s maintainers brought the release forward to October 21), I am grateful that the coalition successfully had an entire two months to prepare—the fixes were quite intricate for PHP, and a leak significantly before the patch was available would have been very impactful. ”he said.
GPT-5.6 Sol's résumé already includes a break-in. In July, OpenAI said the model and an unreleased sibling escaped a locked test environment during a hacking benchmark, found a zero-day flaw along the way, and pulled answers straight from Hugging Face's production database and other five major companies.
Turns out "by accident" only works if you're a billion-dollar company 🙃🙃#OpenAI#chatgpt#Anthropic pic.twitter.com/D7LPUlnql1
— Gaxan (@pvgagan02) October 19, 2026
In September, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent had accessed non-public files on a Medicare statistics portal back in June, and called the notification process "unacceptable." Days later, OpenAI disclosed that its agents had also pulled data from U.S. government sites, including the Census Bureau and the SEC, while insisting none of those incidents counted as breaches.
Now the same company is pitching itself as the internet's night watchman. "Defenders need to have a tighter OODA loop than attackers," Brockman said, borrowing a military term for the cycle of observing, orienting, deciding, and acting, and argued that's possible "especially if defenders have access to stronger models than attackers."
He went further, floating a future where "authorized defenders (such as government)" scan the internet for vulnerable servers and, "in extreme cases," patch them remotely. "It should thus be a national priority to ensure that we always have the most capable cyber models," he said.
To protect the world from the dangers of AI, OpenAI has committed $1 billion in subsidized access to Daybreak, its AI program for defenders protecting critical infrastructure. Brockman said the company is also fixing "several other significant bugs," including a remote code execution flaw that Node.js announced Wednesday.
And PHP won't be the last. “We expect to find many more such issues over upcoming months,” Brockman said. Hopefully the disclosures go smoother next time—ChatGPT could probably help draft the emails.

Bitcoin price tags $84.6K as US stocks head higher on SpaceX Q3 earnings beat
Bitcoin extended gains to approach $85,000 after US stock markets reacted to higher-than-expected SpaceX earnings.
Bitcoin (BTC) passed $84,000 after Wednesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks added to gains on more strong corporate earnings reports.
Key points:
- Bitcoin climbed nearly 2% on Wednesday to return to $84,600 for the first time since Oct. 7.
- SpaceX Q3 operating revenue beat expectations by nearly 15%, coming in at $14.6 billion.
- BTC price action needs a daily close above $83,400 to shift the focus higher in its trading range, crypto analyst Rekt Capital wrote.
SpaceX Q3 earnings help propel Bitcoin to $84,600
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD gaining nearly 2% on the day as markets reacted to a significant Q3 earnings beat from SpaceX.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
After the market close on Tuesday, SpaceX reported a Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% year-on-year and beating expectations by nearly 15%. The net income of the company was $4.4 billion for the quarter.
“The combination of our launch leadership, recurring Starlink revenue, and the significant expansion of our SI infrastructure continues to drive meaningful operating leverage,” chief financial officer Bret Johnsen commented on the earnings release.
US stocks were green at the start of the US trading session, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index 0.7% higher at 26,601 points before retracing some of its gains. Tesla and Meta earnings are due after Wednesday’s market close.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

articles.title: How a SpaceX and Tesla Merger Would Reshape Musk’s AI Empire - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Elon Musk said Tuesday that SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees of independent directors to study a merger, though no terms have been agreed.
- A combined company worth roughly $3.5 trillion would own the Grok chatbot, X, Starlink, the Terafab chip project, the Starmind orbital data center plan, and Tesla's robotaxi and Optimus businesses.
- Any deal needs the backing of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares, which Musk called "quite a high hurdle," and Tesla's annual meeting is set for December 3.
Elon Musk said Tuesday that the boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to study merging his two biggest companies, a deal that would put rockets, electric cars, humanoid robots, a social network and the Grok chatbot inside a single corporation worth roughly $3.5 trillion.
“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. The singularity is Silicon Valley shorthand for the point where AI outsmarts humans and starts improving itself faster than anyone can keep up.
He then listed what the two companies would share: “superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity.”
In plain English, that means AI models, custom chips, a giant chip factory, robots, and satellites that work as data centers in orbit.
If it happens, one company—with one man holding the majority of its votes—would own a leading AI chatbot, the social network that feeds it data, the satellites that connect it, the factory that makes its chips, and the cars and robots it is meant to drive.
Nothing has been signed and Musk warned that assuming a merger is a certainty “would be overstating it.” If you own an S&P 500 index fund, you already hold a sliver of Tesla—not SpaceX—and in an all-stock deal those shares would likely be swapped for stock in the combined company.
It would be Musk’s third consolidation since March 2025, when xAI absorbed X (formerly Twitter). In February, SpaceX swallowed xAI in a deal valuing the AI company at $250 billion, weeks after Tesla put about $2 billion into it; in June, SpaceX went public in the largest IPO ever.
SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion on Tuesday, well above the $12.72 billion analysts expected. It also booked its first quarterly profit since going public, largely by renting the computing power of its AI server farms to firms such as Anthropic and Google.
The most ambitious piece is Starmind, SpaceX’s plan to put AI data centers in orbit. The company has asked U.S. regulators to approve up to 1 million satellites that would run AI models on near-constant sunlight, and Musk expects deployments to start in late 2027 and reach “significant scale” in 2028.
Musk’s argument is that Earth is running out of room and electricity for AI, and the politics back him up. An Annenberg survey found 61% of Americans now oppose new data centers in their area, and roughly $130 billion in projects were blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone.
SpaceX’s own IPO paperwork, however, warned investors that orbital AI computing relies on “unproven technologies” and “may not achieve commercial viability.” Tesla’s main contribution would be Terafab, a $16.8 billion chip factory the two companies are building in Texas to supply Optimus robots, Cybercab robotaxis, and those space data centers.
Musk isn't the first to look past dry land to keep servers cool. Microsoft's Project Natick sank 855 servers off the coast of Scotland in 2018. Over two years only six failed, a 0.7% rate against 5.9% for a comparable group on land, yet Microsoft shut the program down anyway, with cloud operations chief Noelle Walsh saying, “I’m not building subsea data centers anywhere in the world.”
China has since picked up the idea with a wind-powered underwater data center about six miles off Shanghai, which its builder, HiCloud, says uses at least 30% less electricity than land-based rivals, while startup Lonestar aimed at launching a small data storage unit toward the Moon in early 2025.
Wall Street mostly likes the idea, at the right price. “We believe this is a no-brainer move for both SpaceX and Tesla, it comes down to the price for shareholders,” Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. told Reuters, estimating Tesla shares would need to be valued around $550 apiece—a premium, or bonus over the market price, big enough to win the vote.
Tesla spiked almost 4% after Elon’s statements went public. His words were more powerful for Tesla’s stocks than building a flying car, considering the stock dipped after the demonstration.
Even if nothing is for certain, markets are flirting with the idea. Tesla investor Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management now puts the odds of a deal within two years at 95%.
SpaceX is also a major contractor for the U.S. military, intelligence agencies, and NASA, while Tesla relies heavily on its Shanghai factory, a national security mix Reuters said could draw scrutiny from both Washington and Beijing.
A merger would also hand Musk the tighter grip on Tesla he has long demanded. He owns about 20% of Tesla but controls most of SpaceX’s votes through supervoting shares—stock that carries extra votes—and Barclays estimates he would hold about 56% of the votes in a combined company.
SpaceX reacted much more favorably with a 10% spike, the best movement since June.
Any deal still needs the support of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares, not just those cast, a bar Musk called “quite a high hurdle.” Barclays suggested last week that an announcement could come before Tesla’s annual meeting on December 3.

articles.title: Solana’s Alpenglow Launches on Mainnet, Targets 99% Faster Finality
articles.text:
Solana’s Alpenglow launches on mainnet, targets 99% faster finality
Solana’s first major consensus upgrade is targeting 99% finality reduction, seeking to offer users near-immediate transaction settlement and more responsive applications.
Solana’s first major consensus upgrade, Alpenglow, went live on mainnet around 1:54 pm UTC on Wednesday, according to the Solana Foundation’s Alpenglow dashboard.
Alpenglow seeks to reduce transaction finality by 99%, to roughly 150 milliseconds from about 12.8 seconds, according to the Solana Foundation’s July announcement.
The upgrade’s first phase, Votor, replaces the existing voting and finalization mechanism with direct validator voting and a certificate-based system designed to cut transaction finality to roughly 150 milliseconds. A later phase will introduce Rotor, a new block data-distribution protocol intended to replace Turbine.
Alpenglow is Solana’s first major consensus upgrade, replacing its current consensus model, TowerBFT. The upgrade’s 150-millisecond finality target seeks to introduce near-immediate transaction finality for users, which could mean faster payments, trade settlements and more responsive applications.
Cointelegraph has approached the Solana Foundation for comment on Alpenglow’s finality measurements in testnet environments and its expected performance in real-world applications.
Solana Alpenglow activation dashboard. Source: Solana.com
At press time, the Solana mainnet showed a 6.6-second transaction finality and a throughput of 4,721 transactions per second, according to the Alpenglow dashboard.
Related: Solana Foundation targets settlement in seconds with DvP launch
Alpenglow marks “biggest change” for Solana’s core protocol: Anza
Alpenglow will introduce the “biggest change to Solana’s core protocol” since genesis, Anza researchers wrote in a May blog post.
A 150-millisecond latency, “Solana can compete with Web2 infrastructure in terms of responsiveness, potentially making blockchain technology viable for entirely new categories of applications,” wrote Anza researchers Quentin Kniep, Kobi Sliwinski and Roger Wattenhofer on May 19.
In August, Solana reduced its slot time for the first time since genesis, as part of the Solana Foundation’s plans to halve slot times to 200ms, arguing that it would improve latency and accelerate confirmations on the blockchain network. It completed the fourth stage of the slot reduction plan in October.
Following Alpenglow, Solana validators are expected to continue working on Agave 4.5, an upgrade that proposes increasing the number of accounts supported by a versioned transaction from 64 to 96. The increase could create better swap routes and execution prices, according to the Solana Foundation. The upgrade is currently in development and planned for December 2026.
SOL/USD, 1-year chart. Source: CoinMarketCap
The Solana (SOL) token’s price rose nearly 3% in the 24 hours leading up to the upgrade, reversing part of its 42% decline seen during the past year, according to CoinMarketCap.

articles.title: Bitcoin Hits Weekly High as Crypto Market Rebounds - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin trades near $84,500, up 2.5% in 24 hours, as the crypto market cap rose 2.6% to $2.82 trillion; XRP gained 4.1% and Zcash 11.2%.
- Brent crude near $108 and a 5.09% 10-year Treasury yield drove October's selloff, and both eased slightly on Wednesday.
- Bitcoin technical indicators still suggest caution, but prediction markets lean optimistically bullish.
Bitcoin traders and hodlers are breathing this week after a pretty spooky start to the month with the historically best gains.
Bitcoin traded near $84,500 on Wednesday, up 2.5% over 24 hours, as the crypto market bounced back from a mid-October slide that pushed it below $80,000. The total crypto market capitalization, the combined value of every coin, rose 2.2% to $2.9 trillion.
Ethereum climbed 2.5% to $2,504, Solana gained 2.2% to $108.18 and BNB rose 2% to $749. XRP led the large caps with a 4.1% gain to $1.37, while Zcash jumped 11.2% to $1,332 and has now added 15.3% over seven days.
The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a 0-to-100 gauge where 0 means extreme fear and 100 means extreme greed, reads 55, which counts as neutral but is 3 points ahead of yesterday’s readings. In other words, it seems like traders have stopped panicking, but they are not yet chasing prices.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, has swung between $97 and $112 a barrel this month and traded near $108 on Wednesday. The war with Iran keeps supply fears alive, and Washington rejected an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in late September.
Oil matters to crypto because it feeds inflation. U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, above the 3.6% economists expected and up from 3.4% in August. Higher inflation pushes up Treasury yields, the annual return investors demand for lending to the U.S. government. Government bonds paying more than 5% with almost no default risk pull money away from stocks and crypto, and higher rates make the borrowing behind leveraged trades costlier.
The Federal Reserve's benchmark rate sits at 3.75% to 4% after a September hike, and CME FedWatch gives about an eight-in-ten chance of a hold at the Oct. 28 meeting. Markets firmly expect a hike on Dec. 9.
Bitcoin price: Going up, but weak
On the daily chart, Bitcoin opened Wednesday at $82,928.80 and has reached $84,726.28, up 1.94% for the candle, after bouncing about 6% from this month's low near $79,711. Its current price is pressing up, trying to approach the natural resistance at $87,422.70.
Bitcoin’s latest rally ran from $62,763 to a September high of $87,422.70. That trend marked a strong support at $81,603. Bitcoin lost the level in the October dip and has now reclaimed it, with movement still in the upper side of its bounce..
The 50-day exponential moving average, an average of recent closing prices that gives more weight to the most recent days, sits near $80,782, above the 200-day moving average at about $76,084. A 50-day above the 200-day is the standard sign of an uptrend, and Bitcoin trades 4.6% above the shorter average.
The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, which scores recent buying against selling on a 0-to-100 scale, reads 58.5. Readings above 50 mean buyers hold the edge, while 70 marks overbought territory, so momentum is not yet stretched but is moving towards a bullish mood.
The bullish scenario needs a daily close above $84,726, today's high, ideally with ADX—an indicator of a trend’s strength over time—climbing back above 25 to confirm a trend. That would open a natural target at around $86,090, and then the September high at $87,422.70.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market built by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, put the odds of Bitcoin touching $87,500 in October at 31%, down from 45% on Oct. 12. A $90,000 touch is priced at 18%.
A stall below $84,726 would keep Bitcoin inside the roughly $79,700 to $87,400 range that has held since late September, which fits an ADX under 20.
The bearish case starts with a daily close below $81,603. That would expose the 50-day EMA at $80,782, then the October low near $79,711, and the 200-day EMA at $76,084.

articles.title: CertiK Warns Crypto Apps Remain at Risk From eMudhra Flaw
articles.text:
Big Tech’s eMudhra fixes may leave crypto bots exposed, CertiK warns
CertiK says crypto trading bots and exchange applications may remain exposed to the eMudhra certificate flaw because browser fixes may not protect all software.
Cryptocurrency trading bots and exchange applications may remain exposed to the eMudhra certificate security flaw despite emergency fixes from major technology companies, according to blockchain security company CertiK.
By Tuesday, tech giants including Google, Apple and Microsoft had blocked eight vulnerable certificates issued by India’s eMudhra, but the fixes may not protect crypto applications using separate security systems, CertiK’s senior director of digital assets security, Peiyu Wang, told Cointelegraph.
“Major browser blocks substantially reduce the risk for clients that receive and enforce them,” Wang said. “Some applications outside the browser ecosystem do not enforce Certificate Transparency or receive the same revocation protections.”
Wang stressed that crypto services are not inherently more susceptible to the flaw than other industries, but attackers could exploit compromised certificates to impersonate the HTTPS connections used by exchanges, wallet interfaces and APIs.
Attackers could specifically impersonate crypto services and replace deposit addresses or trick users into approving malicious transactions, Wang said. Such attacks would also require intercepting or redirecting users’ internet traffic, while the compromised certificate authority keys alone would not expose wallet private keys.
Wang urged crypto operators to update their software and certificate trust stores and verify that their applications reject the affected certificates.
Felix Ng contributed reporting.
Related: Ledger’s early implant warnings deserved more action, Karpelès says

articles.title: Dogecoin Gets a Dedicated Company to Build Out Its Ecosystem - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Dogecoin Labs launched together with the Dogecoin Foundation, consolidating the meme coin’s scattered products, IP, and development teams.
- Led by CEO Jordan Jefferson, it aims to close the gap between Dogecoin’s massive community and its thin lineup of real apps.
- It builds on recent groundwork: DogeOS’s Sept. 30 testnet and MyDoge’s 500,000-plus users.
Dogecoin is getting a dedicated company to build out its ecosystem, as the teams behind the meme coin’s biggest consumer products fold into a single organization aimed at giving DOGE more everyday uses.
Announced Tuesday, Dogecoin Labs was formed together with the Dogecoin Foundation to consolidate the products, intellectual property, and development teams scattered across the Dogecoin world into one independent outfit.
It will own and operate three flagship products: the MyDoge wallet, the DogeOS app platform, and Such App, a merchant-payments tool, with assets and talent contributed by both the Foundation and House of Doge.
The pitch is to close a gap the company sees as Dogecoin’s defining weakness. Despite ranking among the largest and most recognizable cryptocurrencies, with deep liquidity, millions of holders and one of crypto’s most active communities, the number of actual products and businesses built on DOGE remains small relative to that audience. Dogecoin Labs, led by CEO Jordan Jefferson, the founder of MyDoge and DogeOS, intends to change that by building wallets, payments, commerce, trading, DeFi, gaming, AI and social apps.
“No other digital asset has Dogecoin’s combination of liquidity, community and cultural reach, and its potential has barely been tapped,” Jefferson said, adding that the community has chanted “DOGE to $1” for years and that the goal now is “to build the economy that ambition calls for.”
The move builds on recent groundwork. DogeOS opened its public testnet on Sept. 30, giving developers an Ethereum-compatible environment to build Dogecoin apps, while MyDoge, which grew past 500,000 users without paid acquisition, rolled out a V3 update connecting the wallet to those applications. Together with Such App’s merchant rails, the three products are meant to link developers, consumers and businesses into a functioning DOGE economy.
The Foundation will continue its stewardship, open-source support and advocacy while Labs handles commercial product development.
The reorganization arrives during a soft stretch for the token. DOGE traded around $0.084 on Tuesday, up 3.9% on the day for a roughly $13 billion market cap, but down about 14% over the past month and off roughly 88% from its May 2021 record.
Dogecoin’s institutional story has been mixed, too: a Dogecoin Foundation-backed 21Shares DOGE ETF launched on Nasdaq this year, though Bitwise later shut its own Dogecoin fund citing low demand and a need to “optimize its product range to meet evolving investor needs.”
