articles.title: Fatty liver disease is actually five different conditions, scientists discover
articles.text:
Fatty liver disease is actually five different conditions, scientists discover
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- Mayo Clinic
- Summary:
- A common liver disease affecting nearly 30% of adults worldwide may be far more complicated than scientists previously realized. Mayo Clinic researchers have discovered that fatty liver disease actually consists of five distinct biological subtypes, each carrying different risks for liver failure, cancer, heart disease, and other serious complications.
- Share:
A common liver disease affecting nearly 30% of adults worldwide is far more complex than previously understood. Researchers at Mayo Clinic have identified five biologically distinct forms of the condition, each associated with different risks of serious health complications, including heart disease, liver failure, cancer, and the need for a liver transplant.
The findings, published in Nature Communications, come from a collaboration between Mayo Clinic and Virginia Tech. Scientists discovered that metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, or MASLD, can develop through several different biological pathways. Some are closely connected to obesity and diabetes, while others appear to be driven by inherited genetic differences.
One of the most important findings involves the genetic forms of the disease. These subtypes are associated with a greater likelihood of progressing to advanced liver damage, even in people who do not have the metabolic risk factors typically linked to fatty liver disease.
By identifying these differences, doctors may eventually be able to recognize vulnerable patients sooner, improve screening, and select treatments based on the specific biological processes responsible for their illness.
"When clinical and genomic data are analyzed together at this scale, you begin to see patterns of disease progression that would otherwise remain hidden," says Shulan Tian, Ph.D., co-senior author and a bioinformatician at Mayo Clinic. "Once you separate these subtypes, you can start to match treatments to the biology that's actually driving the disease."
Why Fatty Liver Disease Can Be Dangerous
MASLD, previously known as nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, develops when excess fat accumulates in the liver. Many people experience no noticeable symptoms, allowing the condition to go undetected for years.
Although fatty liver disease does not always cause serious complications, it can progress to inflammation, scarring, and permanent liver damage. Over time, severe cases may develop into cirrhosis, a condition in which extensive scarring prevents the liver from functioning properly.
MASLD is a major contributor to cirrhosis, liver cancer, and liver transplantation worldwide. Understanding why some patients experience severe complications while others do not has therefore become an important goal for researchers.
Genetic Analysis Reveals Five Distinct Liver Disease Subtypes
To investigate these differences, the research team examined genetic sequencing results alongside extensive medical information from more than 4,600 patients diagnosed with MASLD.
Their analysis included liver enzyme measurements, body mass index, blood lipid levels, and other indicators of metabolic health. The researchers also considered additional medical conditions, including diabetes, depression, and sleep apnea.
Using advanced computer models, they searched for patterns connecting patients with similar genetic characteristics and clinical findings. This approach revealed five distinct groups, each with its own underlying biological features.
The results suggest that patients who receive the same fatty liver disease diagnosis may actually have substantially different forms of the condition, with different risks of developing serious complications.
"What's emerging here is a way to systematically identify meaningful subgroups within complex disease," says Eric Klee, Ph.D., co-senior author and the Everett J. and Jane M. Hauck Midwest Associate Director of Research and Innovation. "It helps us map complex disease with such precision that we can begin to anticipate its course and intervene before the most serious damage occurs."
How Large-Scale DNA Research Made the Discovery Possible
The researchers relied on Mayo Clinic's Research Data Atlas, a system designed to connect patients' genetic information with detailed medical records. By bringing these large collections of data together, scientists can detect relationships that might be difficult to recognize when studying individual patients.
Dr. Klee helped develop the platform, which draws on resources including the Tapestry Study.
That project has produced Mayo Clinic's largest collection of exome data, involving more than 100,000 participants. An exome is the portion of a person's DNA that contains instructions for making proteins, which carry out many of the body's essential functions. Studying this genetic information can reveal inherited differences that influence how diseases begin and progress.
The combination of genetic data and medical histories allows researchers to investigate diseases in much greater detail, potentially uncovering important differences that conventional diagnostic methods cannot detect.
"This is exactly the kind of insight large-scale genomic research was built to deliver," says Konstantinos Lazaridis, M.D., the Carlson and Nelson Endowed Executive Director for the Center for Individualized Medicine who led the Tapestry Study and is a co-author of the research. "When you connect genetic data with detailed clinical information across large populations, you can start to redefine diseases in ways that directly impact patient care."
Surprising Links to Depression, Sleep Apnea, and Migraines
The findings also suggest that the differences between fatty liver disease subtypes extend beyond the liver itself.
For the first time, researchers identified associations between particular MASLD subtypes and conditions such as depression, sleep apnea, and migraine.
These connections suggest that the biological processes underlying certain forms of fatty liver disease may be linked to health problems affecting multiple parts of the body.
Although the findings do not establish that fatty liver disease directly causes these conditions, they highlight how closely liver health may be connected to other biological systems.
Could Personalized Treatments Change Fatty Liver Disease Care?
The discovery could eventually change how doctors assess and treat MASLD. Rather than approaching every patient as though they have the same disease, clinicians may be able to use genetic and clinical information to determine which subtype is present and which complications are most likely to develop.
Such an approach could be particularly valuable for identifying patients with genetic forms associated with severe liver damage, including those who appear to have relatively few conventional risk factors.
The research team now plans to evaluate its findings in larger and more diverse patient populations. Scientists also want to determine whether different subtypes respond differently to available treatments, including GLP-1 receptor agonists, a class of medications used to treat conditions such as type 2 diabetes and obesity.
If future studies confirm these differences, the findings could help move fatty liver disease care toward more precise screening, earlier intervention, and treatments tailored to each patient's underlying biology.

Lazaridis, Eric W. Klee, Danfeng Daphne Yao, Shulan Tian. Subtyping metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease using electronic health record-linked genomic cohorts reveals diverse etiologies and progression. articles.title: Modern neuroscience is rediscovering a surprising idea freud had 130 years ago
articles.text:
Modern neuroscience is rediscovering a surprising idea freud had 130 years ago
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oslo
- Summary:
- Researchers have identified striking parallels between Sigmund Freud’s century-old theories and modern neuroscience, suggesting that the brain’s constant predictions shape how we experience reality. The findings could help explain why harmful thought patterns are so difficult to break and offer new insights into treating mental disorders.
- Share:
What if the human brain works in ways that Sigmund Freud began describing more than 130 years ago? A new scientific analysis suggests that some of his ideas about the mind share surprising similarities with one of the most influential theories in modern neuroscience.
Published in the scientific journal Entropy, the paper explores connections between Freud's original theories, later developments in psychoanalysis, and a modern approach to brain research known as the prediction paradigm.
This approach describes the brain as a prediction machine. Rather than simply responding to information from the outside world, the brain is constantly anticipating what will happen next. It then compares those expectations with incoming information from the senses and works to reduce any differences between what it predicted and what actually occurred.
Scientists believe this ongoing process plays a central role in how people perceive their surroundings, make decisions, behave, and regulate emotions.
Researchers Erik Stänicke, Bendik Hovet, and Line Indrevoll Stänicke, together with colleagues, argue that this modern understanding of brain function has important parallels with ideas that psychoanalysts have been developing for more than a century.
"For over 130 years, psychoanalysis has developed psychological theories about how predictions take place at a subjective level, which cognitive neuropsychology is now studying at a physiological level."
How Freud's Ideas Connect to the Predictive Brain
Although neuroscience and psychoanalysis approach the mind differently, the researchers suggest that both may be describing related processes.
Neuroscience examines the physical mechanisms behind thought and behavior, often using mathematical models to explain how the brain processes information. Psychoanalysis, which grew out of Freud's work, focuses more on unconscious mental processes, emotional experiences, and the ways past relationships influence present behavior.
In other words, one field investigates what happens inside the brain, while the other explores how those processes are experienced by the individual.
A particularly interesting connection involves the psychoanalytic concept of projection and the neuroscientific concept of prediction.
In psychoanalysis, projection involves attributing feelings, intentions, or qualities to someone else. The researchers suggest that this resembles how the brain uses previously learned expectations to interpret new experiences.
"When we attribute qualities, intentions or feelings to other people, our brain shapes our experience of the world in line with established expectations," says Stänicke.
For instance, someone who has repeatedly experienced rejection may become especially sensitive to signs that other people are rejecting them. Even an ambiguous remark or facial expression might be interpreted negatively because past experiences have shaped what the person expects.
Over time, these expectations can influence how someone approaches unfamiliar situations and forms new relationships.
"This corresponds to the neuroscientific distinction between changing one's own predictions, perceptual inference, and the attempt to make the world conform to them, namely active inference."
Perceptual inference refers to the way the brain interprets sensory information and updates its expectations in response. Active inference, by contrast, involves taking actions that help bring experiences into line with predictions or reduce uncertainty.
Together, these concepts help explain why people do not always experience the world as it objectively is. Their expectations can influence what they notice, how they interpret events, and how they respond.
Why the Brain Holds On to Negative Expectations
The researchers believe the similarities between Freud's ideas and modern neuroscience could offer valuable insights into mental health disorders, particularly those involving deeply established patterns of thinking and behavior.
Both approaches portray the mind as constantly seeking stability and predictability. This tendency is related to homeostasis, the process through which a system maintains a relatively stable internal state.
In the predictive brain model, reducing uncertainty is an important part of maintaining that stability. The brain relies on familiar expectations to make the world easier to understand, even when those expectations are inaccurate or no longer helpful.
"Psychoanalysts refer to the tendency in the mind to recreate familiar relational patterns, even when these are poorly adapted," says Stänicke.
This could help explain why people sometimes repeat harmful patterns in relationships or continue interpreting situations negatively despite evidence that challenges their assumptions.
"Rigid and persistent symptoms, such as paranoid ideas or an internalized critical voice, may be stable but not very flexible prediction models," says Stänicke.
"For example, there may be people who automatically expect criticism, rejection or hostility from others, and therefore interpret situations through this filter despite the fact that reality does not warrant it."
Such expectations can become deeply entrenched because they make experiences feel familiar and predictable. Even when the resulting interpretation is distorted, maintaining an established mental model may feel less uncertain than changing it.
According to Stänicke, this offers a possible explanation for why some psychological symptoms can persist for years and why changing longstanding patterns of thought and behavior often requires considerable time.
The connection is particularly interesting because it suggests that some mental health difficulties may involve more than consciously held beliefs. They may also reflect deeply learned expectations that automatically shape emotional responses and interactions with others.
How Psychotherapy Could Help Change Deeply Rooted Patterns
The researchers also highlight an important distinction between what people consciously believe and what they have learned through experience.
"In addition, both models give us insight into how parts of our expectations of the outside world are not only anchored cognitively, but in procedural memory that is expressed in relational ways of being," he says.
Procedural memory is a type of long-term memory involved in learned habits and skills. It allows people to perform familiar actions without consciously thinking through every step.
In the context of relationships, the researchers suggest that a similar form of learning may help explain why certain emotional reactions and patterns of interaction become automatic.
Someone might intellectually understand that other people are not necessarily hostile or critical, for example, yet still instinctively respond as though rejection is inevitable.
These expectations are not simply thoughts that can be changed through reasoning. They can also be embedded in habitual ways of reacting to people and navigating relationships.
This distinction may help explain why psychotherapy sometimes needs to address personal relationships and emotional experiences rather than focusing only on conscious thoughts.
"Therefore, psychotherapy sometimes has to work relationally. For example, new experiences in the relationship between therapist and patient can gradually help to change entrenched relational patterns."
Through repeated experiences that challenge familiar expectations, patients may gradually develop different ways of interpreting situations and relating to other people.
Bringing Freud's Psychoanalysis and Neuroscience Together
The researchers argue that connecting psychoanalysis with modern predictive brain theory could benefit both fields.
Neuroscience may provide a biological framework for understanding processes that psychoanalysts have long described through subjective experience. At the same time, psychoanalytic theories may offer more detailed explanations of how expectations are experienced emotionally, interpreted personally, and expressed through relationships.
The proposed similarities do not establish that Freud's broader theories were correct. Instead, they suggest that two very different traditions of studying the mind may offer complementary ways of understanding some of the same psychological processes.
By examining both the brain's physical mechanisms and the individual's inner experience, researchers hope to develop a more complete understanding of human behavior and mental health.
"Bringing these two fields together can open up for a more holistic psychology, in which both neurological mechanisms and subjective experience are included. In this way, we can understand subjectivity in a more scientific manner."

Materials provided by University of Oslo. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Erik Stänicke, Bendik Sparre Hovet, Line Indrevoll Stänicke. Freud’s Model of the Mind Within a Predictive Processing Neuroscientific Paradigm. Entropy, 2026; 28 (3): 318 DOI: 10.3390/e28030318

articles.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
articles.text:
Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
A soy-derived compound protected mice from high blood pressure and memory problems linked to excessive salt consumption, offering a promising new avenue for research.
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- Fujita Health University
- Summary:
- Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure. It could also harm memory and social behavior. In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet. Mice given the supplement had lower blood pressure, better memory, and improved social interactions compared with mice consuming excess salt alone.
- Share:
Consuming too much salt can affect more than blood pressure. Growing evidence suggests that excessive salt intake may also interfere with memory, thinking, and emotional well-being. High salt (HS) consumption is already a major public health concern because of its connection to hypertension, but its potential effects on the brain make finding ways to reduce the damage even more important.
Researchers in Japan have identified a promising possibility in LPC70, a compound derived from soy. Previous research found that this ingredient could reduce high blood pressure and cognitive problems associated with a high-salt diet (HSD) in mice. The latest study takes a closer look at how it works, revealing that the compound influences important chemical signals in the brain and kidneys.
How a Soy Compound May Counter the Effects of Excess Salt
The research centers on prostaglandins (PGs), signaling molecules made from a fatty acid called arachidonic acid (AA). These substances act much like local hormones, helping regulate essential functions throughout the body.
In the cardiovascular system, prostaglandins help control blood pressure by balancing the widening and narrowing of blood vessels. Their effects in the brain are more complicated. Depending on which receptors they activate, they can trigger signals that either protect nerve cells or contribute to harmful processes, potentially affecting memory, thinking, and emotional responses.
LPC70 is a form of soy lysolecithin in which lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) accounts for more than 70% of the phospholipids. Although earlier experiments showed that LPC70 could ease salt-related hypertension and cognitive difficulties, scientists had not fully understood the mechanisms responsible, particularly its influence on prostaglandin signaling.
To investigate, a research team led by Professor Akihiro Mouri and Dr. Hisayoshi Kubota, working with Dr. Kazuhiro Kagotani, examined how LPC70 affected these signaling pathways in mice consuming a high-salt diet.
Dr. Kubota, the study's first author, played a central role in the experiments. He assessed blood pressure, monitored behavioral changes, and analyzed molecular activity associated with prostaglandins. His work helped clarify how LPC70 produces different effects in the organs involved in salt-related cardiovascular and cognitive problems.
Prof. Mouri and Dr. Kubota are affiliated with the Department of Regulatory Science for Evaluation and Development of Pharmaceuticals & Devices at Fujita Health University Graduate School of Medical Science, as well as the International Center for Brain Science (ICBS) at Fujita Health University in Japan. Dr. Kagotani is affiliated with Tsuji Oil Mills Co., Ltd, in Japan and the Tsuji Health and Beauty Science Laboratory at Mie University, Japan.
The findings were released online on May 14, 2026, and published in Volume 197 of Neurochemistry International on July 1, 2026.
"We wanted to understand the role of LPC70 in coordinating changes in PG signaling across organ systems," mentioned Prof. Mouri. "Our study originated from a collaborative research project with Tsuji Oil Mills Co., Ltd, a company that develops naturally derived food ingredients," he added.
Soy Compound Improves Blood Pressure and Memory in Mice
As expected, mice that consumed a high-salt diet developed elevated blood pressure. However, the consequences extended beyond their cardiovascular health.
The animals also became less socially interactive and had difficulty recognizing objects they had encountered before, indicating problems with memory. Interestingly, their general movement and anxiety-like behavior showed no substantial changes. This pattern suggests that excessive salt selectively disrupted more complex cognitive and social functions rather than causing widespread behavioral impairment.
When researchers supplemented the animals' diets with LPC70, several of these effects were reduced. Blood pressure improved, and the mice performed better on tests of social interaction and object recognition memory.
These improvements prompted the researchers to examine what was happening inside the animals' kidneys and brains.
Different Protective Effects in the Kidneys and Brain
In the kidneys, a high-salt diet increased the expression of two components involved in prostaglandin signaling: cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and the PGE2 receptor EP3. Both may contribute to the development of high blood pressure associated with excessive salt consumption.
LPC70 reduced these salt-related increases, suggesting that the compound helps correct changes in kidney signaling that can interfere with normal blood pressure regulation.
The researchers found a different response in the prefrontal cortex, a brain region essential for thinking, memory, and social behavior.
Excess salt reduced the expression of the PGD2 receptor DP1, which plays a role in protective and anti-inflammatory signaling in the brain. LPC70 restored expression of this receptor without changing DP2, another receptor associated with potentially harmful effects on nerve cells.
This distinction is important because it suggests that LPC70 does not simply increase or suppress all prostaglandin activity. Instead, it may selectively favor signaling pathways that help protect the brain, potentially explaining the improvements in memory and social behavior observed in the mice.
A Surprising Change in Chemical Signaling
The team also discovered an unexpected change involving arachidonic acid, the fatty acid the body uses to produce prostaglandins.
Mice consuming excess salt had lower levels of circulating arachidonic acid. Yet when they received LPC70, levels of prostaglandins derived from this fatty acid, including PGE2 and PGD2, increased.
This seemingly contradictory result suggests that LPC70 may help the body use available arachidonic acid more efficiently to produce prostaglandins under high-salt conditions.
Taken together, the findings reveal a coordinated but highly selective response. In the kidneys, LPC70 appears to suppress signaling changes associated with hypertension. In the brain, it restores signaling linked to protection against inflammation and damage.
The compound's effects therefore depend on both the organ involved and the specific prostaglandin receptors being regulated.
Could Soy-Based Ingredients Help Protect Against Excess Salt?
The results suggest that LPC70 could eventually become a useful functional food ingredient for reducing some of the health consequences of excessive salt intake.
Its ability to improve blood pressure and cognitive performance in mice raises the possibility that it could support cardiovascular and brain health, particularly among people whose diets contain high amounts of salt.
However, the findings come from animal experiments, and further clinical studies are needed to determine whether the same benefits occur in humans.
"Our study elucidates LPC70's role in PG signaling, laying the groundwork for future clinical research and dietary interventions aimed at reducing hypertension-related cognitive decline and promoting healthy aging globally," concluded Prof. Mouri.
The research provides a clearer picture of how a soy-derived compound can influence the body's response to excessive salt, opening new possibilities for nutritional approaches to protecting long-term health.
Research Funding and Support
The study received support through Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS: 20K07931, 22K07606, 22K11891, and 23H02843).
Additional support came from the Fujita Mind-Brain Research & Innovation Center for Drug Generation (Fujita Mind-BRIDGe) through Japan's Peak Research Universities (J-PEAKS) Program (JPJS00420240019), along with the Japan Science and Technology Agency FOREST Program (JPMJFR215H).
Tsuji Oil Mills Co., Ltd. provided funding for the research. Grants and other support were also supplied by the Education and Research Facility of Animal Models for Human Diseases at Fujita Health University, the Smoking Research Foundation, and the Takeda Science Foundation.

articles.title: Top 5 loài động vật khổng lồ có thể bạn sẽ không tin là chúng tồn tại
articles.text:
Từ những khu rừng nhiệt đới ẩm ướt cho đến độ sâu bí ẩn của đại dương, những sinh vật khổng lồ này có thể là những loài mà bạn không thể ngờ tới.
Ốc sên khổng lồ Ghana, đôi khi còn được gọi là ốc sên khổng lồ, là một loài nhuyễn thể lớn, phàm ăn, đôi khi có chiều dài hơn 30cm.
Đây là loài ốc sên lớn nhất trên Trái đất.
Có nguồn gốc từ Đông Phi, loài chân bụng này không phải là loài ăn chậm thông thường. Đây là loài ốc sên lớn nhất trên Trái đất.
Kích thước của nó rất ấn tượng và sự thèm ăn của nó cũng vậy. Những con ốc sên này không kén ăn, chúng sẽ ngấu nghiến hầu hết mọi thứ mà chúng bắt gặp. Thực đơn của chúng bao gồm hơn 500 loại thực vật, những con ốc sên này có khả năng biến cảnh quan tươi tốt thành vùng đất cằn cỗi với tốc độ đáng kinh ngạc. Vì chúng ăn rất nhiều và đẻ nhiều con nên chúng được coi là một trong những loài xâm lấn nhất trên thế giới.
Kỳ nhông khổng lồ Andrias davidianus là một trong những loài kỳ giông lớn nhất và độc đáo nhất trên thế giới. Loài lưỡng cư này nguồn gốc từ miền Trung và miền Đông Trung Quốc, loài này có thể dài tới 1,8 mét và nặng gần 60 kg. Điều này khiến nó trở thành loài lưỡng cư lớn nhất còn tồn tại trên hành tinh.
Đây là một trong những loài kỳ giông lớn nhất và độc đáo nhất trên thế giới.
Trong lịch sử, kỳ nhông khổng lồ luôn được cho là một loài duy nhất, nhưng nghiên cứu gần đây, các nhà nghiên cứu đã phân biệt được chúng thành 3 loài riêng biệt từ miền Nam, miền Trung và miền Đông Trung Quốc.
Một trong những loài mới được đặt tên, Andrias sligoi, hay kỳ nhông khổng lồ Nam Trung Quốc, được cho là loài lớn nhất trong 3 loài, đạt chiều dài gần 2 mét.
Kỳ nhông khổng lồ Trung Quốc, không giống như nhiều loài lưỡng cư khác, chúng có tuổi thọ cao, một số còn có thể sống lâu hơn người bình thường.
Chúng có thể sống tới 30 năm trong tự nhiên và thậm chí tới 60 năm trong điều kiện nuôi nhốt. Tuổi thọ của kỳ nhông khổng lồ Trung Quốc hoang dã và nuôi nhốt khác nhau đến từ thức ăn và điều kiện sống của chúng. Trong khi kỳ nhông hoang dã tự bảo vệ mình, nơi chúng có thể bị ốm và chết, đồng thời đối mặt với nhiều mối đe dọa hơn, thì kỳ nhông nuôi nhốt được hưởng lợi từ việc chăm sóc y tế và bảo vệ khỏi những kẻ săn mồi.
Dơi ăn quả khổng lồ thường sinh sống theo bầy đàn. Tuy nhiên, không phải tất cả các loài dơi ăn quả đều có kích thước khổng lồ: loài nhỏ nhất chỉ dài 6 cm. Tuy nhiên, loài lớn nhất, dơi ăn quả khổng lồ (đôi khi chúng được gọi là cáo bay) lại khác, chúng có chiều dài cẳng tay dài nhất trong số các loài, kích thước lên tới 21,5cm. Sải cánh của chúng cũng có độ dài ấn tượng từ 1,5m đến 1,7m, đủ để bao phủ một con người có kích thước trung bình.
Loài dơi này giờ chỉ có thể thấy ở khu rừng Maitum, miền Nam Philippines.
Giống như tất cả các loài dơi, loài dơi khổng lồ này sống trên cây với móng vuốt sắc nhọn và ngủ trong tư thế treo ngược. Chúng có thị lực tốt và sử dụng thị lực để bay cũng như tìm kiếm thức ăn. Loài dơi này giờ chỉ có thể thấy ở khu rừng Maitum, miền Nam Philippines.
Người ta cho rằng những con dơi này khá đáng sợ nhưng thực chất, chúng lại hoàn toàn vô hại. Loài dơi này chủ yếu ăn trái cây, lá cây và nguồn thực phẩm chính của chúng là quả sung. Chúng có thể bay tới 40km mỗi đêm để tìm kiếm thức ăn. Những con dơi này dành phần lớn thời gian trong ngày để ngủ vì chúng cũng sống về đêm như những loài dơi khác.
Loài dơi ăn quả khổng lồ hiện đang được bảo vệ bởi công ước quốc tế và nằm trong danh sách các loài động vật hoang dã có nguy cơ tuyệt chủng. Tuy nhiên, ngay cả khi loài dơi này được luật pháp quốc tế bảo vệ, nạn săn bắn, buôn bán chúng vẫn diễn ra. Từ năm 1986 đến năm 2016, số lượng của chúng đã giảm hơn 50%.
Cá đuối sông Mekong.
Không phải tất cả cá đuối gai độc sống trong đại dương - trên thực tế, những con lớn nhất lại sống ở sông Mekong.
Cá đuối nước ngọt khổng lồ hay cá đuối sông Mekong là một loài cá đuối nước ngọt trong họ Dasyatidae thuộc bộ Myliobatiformes phân bố tại vùng bán đảo Đông Dương và đảo Borneo của Indonesia.
Với chiều rộng hơn 2,2 mét, những con vật khổng lồ dưới nước này là một trong những loài cá lớn nhất thế giới. Nhưng mặc dù có kích thước khổng lồ, nhưng với chúng ta, loài vật này vẫn là những sinh vật khó nắm bắt. Cơ thể phẳng lì của chúng cho phép chúng chôn mình dưới lòng sông và biến mất khỏi tầm mắt. Tệ hơn nữa, cá đuối nước ngọt khổng lồ đang bị đe dọa do đánh bắt quá mức và suy thoái môi trường sống do phá rừng, phát triển đất và xây đập. Cá đuối nước ngọt khổng lồ thường nặng 500 đến 600 kg.
Khi nhắc tới sứa, nhiều người sẽ nghĩ rằng chúng là những sinh vật nhỏ bé đáng yêu với dáng vẻ trong suốt như pha lê. Tuy nhiên trên thực tế, đại dương bao la ngoài kia tồn tại rất nhiều loài sứa lớn. Và loài sứa khổng lồ dưới đây cũng là một trong số đó.
Khi trưởng thành, chúng đạt chiều dài đường kính khoảng 2m, cân nặng hơn 220kg.
Đường kính của những con sứa Nomura có thể dài hơn chiều cao trung bình của một người đàn ông. Khi trưởng thành, chúng đạt chiều dài đường kính khoảng 2m, cân nặng hơn 220kg. Sứa Nomura sinh sống chủ yếu tại vùng nước giữa Trung Quốc và Nhật Bản (trung tâm Hoàng Hải và khu vực biển Trung Quốc).
Trước kia, loại sinh vật này chủ yếu sống tại những vùng biển sâu, tuy nhiên do môi trường sinh thái biển bị tàn phá, lại thêm sự nóng lên toàn cầu trong những năm gần đây đã khiến cho tập tính của chúng bị thay đổi.
Điểm đáng nói nằm ở chỗ, loài sứa Nomura không chỉ có kích thước to lớn mà còn sở hữu độc tính cao. Nếu vô tình bị chạm phải, những vết đốt du chúng gây ra có thể gây nguy hiểm đến tính mạng.
Từ năm 2005 đến nay, chúng là tai họa đối với ngành công nghiệp đánh bắt cá trong các khu vực biển ở Nhật. Chúng gây ra các cuộc tấn công không chủ ý vào các tàu thuyền đánh bắt cá, cũng như ảnh hưởng không nhỏ đến chuỗi cân bằng thức ăn trong biển.

articles.title: Physicists create a bizarre new quantum state called a fractional fermi sea
articles.text:
Physicists create a bizarre new quantum state called a fractional fermi sea
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- University of Innsbruck
- Summary:
- Physicists have discovered a strange new state of quantum matter in which ultracold atoms defy familiar organizational rules, forming a highly excited yet surprisingly orderly configuration called a "fractional Fermi sea." The discovery challenges established quantum theories and hints at exotic quasiparticles that scientists have dubbed potential "super-Fermions."
- Share:
Physicists have uncovered a strange new form of quantum behavior in which particles organize themselves in ways that challenge established theories. Even more surprising, the particles maintain a remarkable hidden order despite being driven into an extremely energetic state.
In a study published in Physical Review Letters, researchers from the group led by Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, working with theoretical physicist Alvise Bastianello of the CNRS and Université Paris-Dauphine, describe how to engineer an exotic quantum state known as a "fractional Fermi sea."
The breakthrough involves pushing ultracold cesium atoms far beyond their normal conditions by repeatedly changing how strongly they attract or repel one another. Rather than simply becoming disordered, the particles rearrange themselves into an unusual configuration that behaves differently from the quantum systems scientists have traditionally studied.
The theoretical findings provide the foundation for recent experimental research conducted by Nägerl's team at the Department of Experimental Physics.
Pushing Quantum Particles Beyond Their Normal Limits
Under ordinary conditions, quantum particles follow well-established rules that determine how they arrange themselves, particularly at extremely low temperatures.
One important example involves fermions, a category of particles that includes electrons. These particles cannot all occupy the same quantum state, so they fill available energy levels according to specific restrictions. At very low temperatures, this arrangement produces what physicists call a Fermi sea.
But what happens when researchers deliberately disrupt the conditions that normally govern how particles behave?
As Alvise Bastianello explains: "Fermions, for instance, stack neatly into the available energy states to form the so-called 'Fermi sea'. But what happens if one forces interacting atoms to continuously cycle through extreme conditions, smoothly shifting them from strongly repelling each other to strongly attracting each other?"
To investigate this possibility, the researchers studied ultracold cesium atoms confined to a one-dimensional system. This means the atoms are restricted to moving along a single direction, creating an environment in which their quantum interactions can be studied with exceptional control.
The team examined what happens when the interactions between these atoms are repeatedly adjusted, cycling between powerful repulsion and attraction.
Their calculations revealed something unexpected. Starting from the ground state, the lowest energy configuration available to the system, the atoms could be driven into a highly excited state without losing their underlying organization.
The researchers call this unusual arrangement a fractional Fermi sea because its particles appear to obey a modified rule governing how quantum states are occupied.
"Instead of simply heating the system, the interaction cycle reorganizes the atoms into a new many-body state," says Yi Zeng, the leading author of this study. "This gives us a controlled way to explore quantum matter beyond the usual equilibrium paradigms."
A Strange New Quantum State With Hidden Order
One of the most intriguing features of the fractional Fermi sea is that its particles remain organized even though the system has been pushed far from equilibrium.
In physics, equilibrium describes a condition in which a system's overall properties have settled into a stable balance. Systems driven far from equilibrium can behave in complicated and unexpected ways, making them particularly challenging to understand.
Yet the fractional Fermi sea is not simply a collection of excited particles behaving randomly. Instead, it contains distinctive mathematical patterns that reveal a deeper structure.
Among these patterns are pronounced ripples called Friedel oscillations. These are wave-like variations associated with the way quantum particles influence one another. The researchers also identified unusual patterns in how correlations between particles weaken with increasing distance, even when the repulsive interactions are relatively weak.
These signatures are important because they differ from predictions associated with Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid theory, a long-established framework for describing how interacting quantum particles behave in one-dimensional systems.
The findings therefore point toward a previously unexplored type of quantum behavior that cannot be fully described using this familiar theoretical picture.
"This state is highly excited, but it is not random," says Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, the group leader. "It has a hidden order that becomes visible in its correlations."
The strange behavior also raises questions about the effective particles that emerge within the system. Physicists call these collective excitations quasiparticles because they can behave like individual particles even though they arise from the coordinated motion of many interacting particles.
Nägerl suggests that the unusual excitations might eventually deserve a name of their own.
"We are not yet sure how we should name these new quasiparticles. Perhaps 'super-Fermions'?"
Opening a New Frontier in Quantum Physics
The discovery suggests that fractional Fermi seas represent an exotic critical phase of quantum matter, with characteristic patterns of particle correlations that extend beyond existing descriptions of one-dimensional quantum systems.
It also demonstrates the growing power of quantum simulation, a technique that allows scientists to use carefully controlled quantum systems to investigate physical behavior that would otherwise be difficult to reproduce or study.
Ultracold atoms are particularly useful for this purpose because researchers can precisely adjust their interactions and observe how the resulting quantum states change.
Rather than limiting these experiments to recreating phenomena already understood through established theories, scientists can now explore deliberately engineered states that reveal entirely new possibilities.
As Hanns-Christoph Nägerl says: "The discovery of fractional Fermi seas shows how far we can push quantum simulation: not only reproducing known models, but creating and probing states that go beyond established paradigms."
The current publication establishes the theoretical framework for fractional Fermi seas. A companion study describing their experimental realization through quantum simulation is undergoing peer review.
Together, the research points toward new ways of investigating the fundamental behavior of quantum matter, including unusual collective excitations and hidden forms of order that emerge only when particles are pushed far outside their normal conditions.

articles.title: Nguyên nhân rùng mình khiến Trái đất từng biến thành "hành tinh quái vật"
articles.text:
Một ngày tận thế còn khủng khiếp hơn phim ảnh đã xảy ra với các động vật kỷ Tam Điệp, kích hoạt sự sản sinh của dòng họ quái vật khủng khiếp nhất mọi thời đại, thống trị xuyên 2 kỷ sau đó.
Đáng sợ hơn, đó là lựa chọn của chính Trái đất: tự "đóng băng" chính mình, gây nên một cuộc đại tuyệt chủng vào cuối kỷ Tam Điệp, dọn đường cho dòng họ khủng long phát triển và "lên ngôi" trong kỷ Jura và kỷ Phấn Trắng sau đó, theo nghiên cứu vừa được SciTech Daily trích dẫn.
Một động vật có vú cổ đại bị khủng long bắt - (Ảnh: Larry Felder/SCITECH DAILY)
Công trình thú vị dẫn đầu bởi nhà địa chất Paul Olsen từ Đài Quan sát Trái đất Lamont-Doherty của Trường Đại học Columbia - Mỹ đã phân tích các mẫu vật từ các cuộc khai quật gần đây ở vùng sa mạc hẻo lánh thuộc lòng chảo Junggar, Tây Bắc Trung Quốc.
Trước đó, khủng long được cho là xuất hiện khoảng 231 triệu năm trước ở vĩ độ ôn đới của lục địa Pangea - siêu lục địa duy nhất của Trái đất thời điểm đó, rồi di chuyển về phía cực Bắc khoảng 214 triệu năm trước.
Trong suốt kỷ Tam Điệp và phần lớn kỷ Jura, nồng độ carbon dioxide trong khí quyển cao gấp 5 lần hiện tại nên hầu như toàn cầu được boa phủ trong "mùa hè vĩnh cửu". Tuy nhiên, các mô hình khí hậu đã tìm thấy những mùa đông xen lẫn ở các vĩ độ cao.
Nghiên cứu mới này đã tìm hiểu bí mật về những mùa đông bí ẩn đó nhờ vào những tàn tích địa chất xen lẫn hóa thạch, và phát hiện ra nó dài và khủng khiếp hơn tưởng tượng.
Nói cách khác, có một mùa đông khủng khiếp gây ra đại tuyệt chủng cuối kỷ Tam Điệp, với 3/4 loài trên Trái đất - chủ yếu là các động vật có vú, tổ tiên của chúng ta và nhiều động vật ngày nay. Chính đại tuyệt chủng này đã dọn đường cho khủng long "bùng nổ" trong 2 kỷ Jura và Phấn Trắng sau đó.
Mùa đông bí ẩn này xảy ra bởi một cuộc trỗi dậy bí ẩn từ lòng đất: hàng loạt núi lửa phun trào, đủ để tạo ra các sol khí lưu huỳnh làm chệch hướng ánh sáng mặt trời, cũng như khiến carbon dioxit và các đám mây tro bụi nhiều tới mức làm chắn bớt ánh sáng gây hiệu ứng ngược: thay vì nóng lên thì Trái đất lại lạnh đi, trong một "mùa đông núi lửa" tưởng chừng vô tận.
Các bằng chứng cho thấy nhiều nơi trên siêu lục địa, bao gồm cả những vùng nhiệt đới, đã đóng băng nhiều thập kỷ. Quá trình này tạo thành sa thạch và một loại bột hạt mịn, còn được lưu lại cho đến ngày nay trong trầm tích ở vùng sa mạc bí ẩn.
Rất may vào cuối kỷ Phấn Trắng (66 triệu năm trước), sự xuất hiện của Chicxulub - tiểu hành tinh giết khủng long - đã làm chao đảo môi trường toàn cầu lần nữa và xóa sổ dòng họ quái vật này, từ đó các vị tổ tiên bé nhỏ của chúng ta mới có cơ hội "lấn sân" trở lại và tiến hóa mạnh mẽ.
Nghiên cứu vừa công bố trên tạp chí khoa học Science Advances.

articles.title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
articles.text:
Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
A new study hints that eating blueberries daily could help improve mood in older adults, potentially through surprising effects on the gut microbiome.
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- Hebrew SeniorLife Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research
- Summary:
- Eating blueberries every day could have surprising effects on mood, according to a small study that found greater reductions in depressive symptoms among older adults who consumed the fruit for three months. Researchers also detected changes in gut microbial enzymes, suggesting a possible gut-brain connection, although the mood benefits were not statistically significant compared with a placebo.
- Share:
A small pilot study suggests that eating blueberries every day may influence gut bacteria and potentially affect mood in older adults. Participants who consumed blueberries regularly experienced a greater and more consistent reduction in depressive symptoms, along with subtle changes in genes associated with gut microbial enzymes.
However, the improvements in depressive symptoms were not statistically significant when compared with the placebo group. Although the findings do not establish that blueberries can relieve depression, they offer preliminary clues about a possible connection between blueberry consumption, the gut microbiome, and mental health.
"Fiber and anthocyanins in blueberries have potential to modify the gut microbiome and metabolites that are relevant to depression in older adults," said lead author Courtney L. Millar, PhD, assistant scientist II at Hebrew SeniorLife's Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research and assistant professor of medicine at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School. "Our objective was to preliminarily determine the effect of blueberry consumption on the gut microbiome, metabolites, and depressive symptoms."
Testing the Effects of Daily Blueberry Consumption
To investigate the potential connection, researchers recruited adults aged 65 and older who were physically inactive and experiencing mild depressive symptoms. The pilot study used a randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm, placebo-controlled design to evaluate whether consuming blueberries could influence gut microbes and mood.
Over three months, participants consumed either 48 grams of blueberry powder each day (approximately two cups of fresh berries) or a matching placebo powder.
Researchers examined the participants' gut microbiomes using metagenomic sequencing, which allowed them to measure the abundance of different microbial species and genes. They also used liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry to analyze gut-derived fecal short-chain fatty acids, compounds produced through microbial activity. Depressive symptoms were assessed using validated questionnaires administered before and after the three-month intervention.
Blueberries Linked to Subtle Changes in Gut Microbial Activity
A total of 18 participants completed the study. Most were women, and the group was predominantly white (placebo group, n = 8; mean age: 75 ± 6; blueberry group, n = 10; mean age: 71 ± 4).
Despite the encouraging pattern in depressive symptoms among participants consuming blueberries, the researchers found no statistically significant difference in mood improvements between the blueberry and placebo groups.
The gut microbiome results also revealed a mixed picture. The overall abundance of microbial species, MetaCyc metabolic pathways, and short-chain fatty acid metabolites remained unchanged.
However, researchers identified statistically significant changes within the blueberry group in the abundance of genes associated with several gut microbial enzymes. One of these was EC 3.6.3.31 Polyamine Transporting ATPase, which is involved in the production of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a neurotransmitter that plays a role in brain signaling.
These findings suggest that blueberries may influence specific aspects of gut microbial function even without producing measurable changes in the overall composition of the microbiome. Larger studies will be needed to determine whether these changes are connected to meaningful improvements in mood or depressive symptoms.
The study, "A pilot study of daily blueberry intake modulates the gut microbiota enzyme commissions in older, sedentary adults with mild depressive symptoms," was published in the Journal of Nutrition, Health and Aging.
Other contributors included Mohit P. Chopra, MD, of the Deanna and Sidney Wolk Center for Memory Health at Hebrew SeniorLife and the Department of Psychiatry at UMass Chan Medical School; Xochitl Morgan, PhD, and Emily A. Green, PhD, of the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health; Alex Wolfe of the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research at Hebrew SeniorLife; Kerry A. Pierce of the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; and Lidan Gao, PhD, and Christopher N. Blesso, PhD, of the Department of Nutritional Sciences at the University of Connecticut.
Additional contributors were Alyssa B. Dufour, PhD, of the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research at Hebrew SeniorLife and the Department of Medicine at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School; Douglas P. Kiel, MD, MPH, of the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research at Hebrew SeniorLife, Harvard Medical School, and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; and Lewis A. Lipsitz, MD, of the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research at Hebrew SeniorLife and professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School.

articles.title: Tìm thấy ếch 2 triệu tuổi vẫn sống trong mỏ dầu: "Chìa khóa" trường sinh của loài người?
articles.text:
Khi xác định niên đại bằng carbon phóng xạ, các nhà khoa học phát hiện rằng con ếch đã 2.000.000 năm tuổi. Khi tìm thấy, da nó vẫn mềm và bóng. Phải chăng nó có thể trường sinh?
Vào tháng 7 năm 1946, một nhà địa chất dầu khí đã đi hàng nghìn dặm tới một mỏ dầu ở Mexico. Trong quá trình thăm dò, ông đã đào trúng 1 con ếch trong trạng thái ngủ đông. Khi nhà địa chất tìm thấy, con ếch đã bị vùi trong mỏ ở độ sâu 2m. Kỳ lạ là lúc mới đào lên, da của con ếch vẫn còn mềm và bóng. Mãi tới 2 ngày sau nó mới thực sự chết.
Việc con ếch đột nhiên chết khiến nhà địa chất cảm thấy vô cùng băn khoăn. Cho tới khi, các nhà khoa học tiến hành xác định niên đại bằng carbon phóng xạ thì họ đã phát hiện ra rằng hầm mỏ này có tuổi đời hơn 2 triệu năm. Con ếch có thể đã bị chôn vùi ngay từ khi hầm mỏ hình thành. Hay có thể hiểu rằng, con ếch đó đã sống trong hầm mỏ tới hơn 2 triệu năm.
Con ếch đã nằm trong hầm mỏ tới 2 triệu năm. (Ảnh minh họa: Baidu)
Như vậy, con ếch đã ở đây trong suốt một thời gian dài trong trạng thái ngủ đông và không chết. Sức sống như vật chắc chắn là một trong những điều khó hiểu nhất trong lịch sử sinh học. Quả thực, những con ếch ngủ đông không phải là mới được phát hiện.
Ở thế kỷ XVI, trong một ghi chép của nhà phẫu thuật Ambroise Pare, thầy thuốc riêng của Vua Henri III (Anh), có miêu tả về một người thợ xây vô tình làm rơi 1 hòn đá trúng 1 chú ếch. Ngay lập tức con ếch nằm bất động, nhưng chỉ một lát sau nó tỉnh lại và nhảy đi mất.
Ở Bắc Mỹ, loài thủy ngưu lùn Sirenia khi gặp các điều kiện khắc nghiệt có thể ngủ vùi tới hơn 1 năm. Trong thời gian này, cơ thể chúng sẽ giảm mức độ trao đổi chất xuống hàng nghìn lần, thậm chí ngừng hẳn. Do đó, vào mùa khô, thổ dân châu Phi thường tranh thủ đi bắt lươn, chạch bằng cách dùng cuốc. Ngay dưới lớp đất khô là những con lươn, chạch vẫn còn tươi rói. Chúng bất động nhưng không phải do mới chết, chỉ cần thả chúng vào nước, sau 10 phút sẽ sống lại như bình thường. Cách nhà khoa học gọi là hình thức "chết giả" trong đất khô cứng.
Các loài lươn, chạch cũng có tình trạng "chết giả" tương tự khi gặp điều kiện khó khăn. (Ảnh minh họa: Baidu)
Trong một đấu giá ở London, nước Anh vào năm 1862, người ta đã trưng bày một tảng than đá có vết rỗng in hình 1 con ếch và bên cạnh là con ếch đã nằm trong đó hàng nghìn năm. Tảng than đá này được tìm thấy ở mỏ than New Port. Không lâu sau, người ta lại tìm thấy một con ếch khác trong mỏ than Lilishal vùng Paddington.
Vào thế kỷ thứ 18, khi đang xây một kè đá dọc theo bãi biển Toulon (Pháp). Các công nhân sau khi bửa những kè đá này thì tìm thấy những con hào còn sống trong lòng đất đá. Năm 1818, một nhà địa chất tới đây lấy mẫu ở độ sâu 15 m. Ông trông thấy có 3 con vật lạ chui ra. Hai con chết ngay khi tiếp xúc với không khí, nhưng một con vẫn còn sống khi Clark thả xuống nước. Các nhà khoa học xác định con vật này thuộc loài động vật tồn tại trên trái đất 10 triệu năm trước.
Đầu năm 1856, một nhóm người dùng mìn phá sập một mỏm đá lớn và phát hiện ra một con vật có hình dáng như khủng long. Nó kêu lên một tiếng rồi chết. Vì họ không có điều kiện để bảo quản xác của nó, nên các nhà khoa học đã lưu giữ lại phần xương của nó cho đến ngày nay. Các nhà khảo cổ học cho rằng đó là một giống thằn lằn bay thời tiền sử…
Dường như những loài vật này, cũng như con ếch 2 triệu năm kia đều có khả năng ngủ đông vô thời hạn? Vậy đây có phải là chìa khoá để giúp con người đạt được sự bất tử?
Nhiều nhà khoa học đã bắt tay vào nghiên cứu để tìm ra bí mật thực sự đằng sau "giấc ngủ đông" dài hàng triệu năm của con ếch.
Có người cho rằng, vì con ếch bị kẹt trong hầm mỏ là yếu tố chính khiến cho nó rơi vào tình trạng ngủ đông thay vì chết như vậy. Họ đã thí nghiệm trên một số con ếch khác trong điều kiện tương tự. Kết quả của cuộc thí nghiệm cho thấy khi nhiệt độ xung quanh tăng thêm 10 độ thì việc trao đổi chất của ếch tăng mạnh từ 2-3 lần. Khi nhiệt độ giảm xuống 10 độ thì nhu cầu trao đổi chất của chúng cũng bị chậm lại chỉ còn 1/3 so với thông thường.
Nhiều nhà khoa học đã thử nhiều cách thí nghiệm khả năng trường tồn kỳ diệu của loài ếch. (Ảnh: Baidu)
Thế nhưng nhiệt độ trong hầm mỏ nơi con ếch bị chôn vùi luôn không đổi, nó cũng không phải chịu bất cứ kích thích nào. Con ếch cũng không bị ảnh hưởng gì từ nắng, mưa, nóng, lạnh, gió. Cứ như vậy, sự sống của con ếch đã tạm dừng lại, không phải tiêu hao năng lượng, vì thế nó có thể ngủ đông mà không cần ăn gì trong hàng triệu năm.
Trước đó, một nhà khoa học Mỹ đã tiến hành một thí nghiệm tương tự như vậy. Đầu tiên ông ta vớt một con cá vàng ra khỏi nước và khô nó sau đó đưa vào không khí lỏng. Nhiệt độ trong bể không khí này xuống tới âm 200 độ. Sau đó vài giây, ông lại thả con cá vàng đông lạnh trở lại vùng nước ấm. Ngay sau đó, con cá đã sống lại và hoạt động bình thường.
Hay kỹ sư Seghine người Pháp đã táo bạo hơn khi trộn 20 con ếch vào vữa rồi biến chúng thành tượng vườn. 12 năm sau, ông đập tượng của chúng. Trong đó, 16 con đã chết, 4 con ếch lại hồi sinh trở lại sau đó vài chục phút.
Hình ảnh một con ếch bị chôn vùi trong xi măng được tìm thấy tại Úc. (Ảnh: Baidu)
Một người Mỹ tên Frank cũng quyết định lập lại thí nghiệm trên vào năm 1852. Ông đã cho khoan nhiều lỗ trên 1 tảng đá vôi và thả vào 12 con ếch vào đó. Sau đó, ông ta dùng xi măng bịt kín các lỗ. Đồng thời, ông cũng nhốt 12 con ếch khác vào 1 khối sa thạch. Sau nhiều năm, ông ta đập vỡ 2 "nhà tù" và kỳ lạ là cả 24 con ếch đều sống lại và hoạt động bình thường.
Từ kết quả các cuộc nghiên cứu này, có thể thấy, không chỉ có ếch mà nhiều loài động vật đều có khả năng trường tồn kỳ diệu. Thế nhưng, bí mật trường sinh này có thể sử dụng với loài người không? Đây vẫn là câu đố mà tới nay chưa ai giải quyết được.

articles.title: Scientists link a strange sugar in red meat to a 63% higher diabetes risk
articles.text:
Scientists link a strange sugar in red meat to a 63% higher diabetes risk
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- European Association for the Study of Diabetes
- Summary:
- A study of nearly 90,000 adults found that people consuming the most of a little-known sugar found in red meat had a 63% higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Scientists suspect the sugar may trigger chronic inflammation, potentially revealing a hidden connection between red meat and diabetes that goes beyond weight gain.
- Share:
A sugar naturally present in red meat may help explain why eating these foods has been associated with a higher risk of type 2 diabetes. Preliminary findings from a large observational study suggest that people who consume the most of this sugar face a substantially greater risk of developing the disease, potentially because of its effects on the immune system and chronic inflammation.
The sugar, known as N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc), is particularly common in beef and lamb. Researchers found that participants with the highest intake of meat-derived Neu5Gc had a 63% higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes (T2D) compared with those who consumed the least.
The association remained statistically significant after researchers accounted for several established diabetes risk factors, including physical activity, overall diet, smoking, and existing health conditions. It became weaker after body mass index (BMI) was also considered, but remained significant.
The findings were presented at the Annual Meeting of The European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) in Milan, Italy.
“Our findings support chronic inflammation as a specific mechanism linking red meat consumption with T2D, partly beyond the amount of red meat a person eats and partly independent of body fat,” said lead author Dr. Leopold Fezeu from the Université Sorbonne Paris Nord, Bobigny, France.
The researchers also observed that diabetes risk generally increased with greater consumption of meat-derived Neu5Gc, particularly among those with the highest exposure.
“Although we do not know exactly what levels of Neu5Gc trigger an immune response, our data suggest that higher intakes of meat-derived Neu5Gc are associated with a progressively higher risk of T2D.”
Why a Sugar in Red Meat May Trigger Inflammation
Neu5Gc is produced naturally by most mammals, but humans lost the ability to make it following an ancient mutation in the CMAH gene. Despite this evolutionary change, the sugar can still enter the human body through food.
It occurs in red meat (particularly beef and lamb), with smaller amounts also found in dairy products.
After Neu5Gc is consumed, the body absorbs it and can incorporate it into human tissues. Because humans do not naturally produce the molecule, the immune system may recognize it as foreign. Scientists classify it as a xeno-autoantigen, a foreign substance that becomes incorporated into the body's own tissues and can provoke an immune reaction.
In response, the immune system produces antibodies against Neu5Gc. The resulting prolonged immune activity, called xenosialitis (xenosialitis), has previously been associated with cardiovascular disease and cancer.
Researchers suspect that this persistent inflammatory response could also contribute to type 2 diabetes. However, before this investigation, no large prospective study had examined whether dietary Neu5Gc might promote diabetes through chronic inflammation.
Nearly 90,000 Adults Studied Over Several Years
To investigate the possible connection, the scientists analyzed dietary and health information from 89,953 adults participating in NutriNet-Santé, a large French observational study that follows people over time to examine how nutrition and lifestyle influence health.
Participants were 42 years old on average, and 79% were women. None had type 2 diabetes or cancer when they entered the study.
Each person completed three 24-hour dietary records. The research team then used a validated food database to calculate how much Neu5Gc participants were likely consuming based on the measured amounts of the sugar in different foods.
The analysis included a broad range of red meats, such as beef, lamb, pork, rabbit, goat, and game. Processed meats (such as bacon, sausages and cured meats) were evaluated as a separate category, while dairy products were analyzed independently.
Using the dietary information, the researchers estimated total Neu5Gc intake from all reported foods. They then ranked participants separately by sex according to their intake of meat-derived Neu5Gc and divided them into five equally sized groups (quintiles).
Diabetes risk was compared across these groups, using those with the lowest intake as the reference.
During a median follow-up period of 7.2 years, researchers recorded 966 new cases of type 2 diabetes.
Higher Red Meat Sugar Intake Linked to 63% Greater Diabetes Risk
The results showed a significant relationship between meat-derived Neu5Gc consumption and the likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes. The association became particularly pronounced among participants with the highest estimated intake.
Compared with the lowest intake group, individuals in the highest group had a 63% greater risk of developing the disease. Those in the second-highest group had a 41% greater risk (men and women combined).
These estimates accounted for potentially influential factors, including age, sex, exercise habits, overall dietary quality, smoking, and existing medical conditions.
The researchers also examined how much meat participants typically consumed.
Among men in the highest Neu5Gc intake group, median red meat consumption was 97 grams daily (136 g including processed meat). For women, the corresponding amount was 73 grams (96 g).
By comparison, men in the lowest intake group consumed a median of just 5 grams of red meat per day (21 g), while women consumed 0 grams (9 g).
The relationship between Neu5Gc and diabetes was observed in both sexes, with no statistically significant evidence that it differed between men and women (see tables in notes to editors).
The findings were also consistent when differences in total calorie intake were considered.
Researchers noticed that the increase in diabetes risk was especially steep at higher levels of Neu5Gc exposure. One possible explanation is that the immune system begins to respond more strongly after enough of the foreign sugar has accumulated in body tissues, although this proposed threshold mechanism has not been confirmed.
Importantly, when the analysis additionally accounted for the total amount of red meat consumed, the relationship between Neu5Gc and diabetes weakened and was no longer statistically significant. The direction of the association remained the same, however.
This means the researchers cannot determine whether Neu5Gc itself (rather than other components of red meat) is responsible for the increased risk. The findings suggest it could contribute to the relationship, but they do not establish that the sugar acts independently of red meat consumption.
Diabetes Risk May Extend Beyond Weight Gain
Another notable finding was that obesity appeared to explain only a relatively small portion of the association.
According to the researchers' estimates, obesity accounted for approximately 13% of the relationship between meat-derived Neu5Gc consumption and type 2 diabetes.
This suggests that factors unrelated to excess body weight may contribute substantially to the observed connection.
One possibility is that immune reactions to Neu5Gc produce chronic inflammation that interferes with insulin-producing cells or tissues that normally respond to insulin. Such effects could potentially increase the likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes even without substantial weight gain.
However, additional studies are necessary to establish whether these inflammatory processes actually explain the association.
Why Dairy Products Showed Different Results
Although Neu5Gc occurs in both red meat and dairy products, the researchers found an important difference between these dietary sources.
Higher consumption of Neu5Gc from dairy products was not associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes.
This finding may reflect the relatively small amounts of Neu5Gc in cow's milk compared with red meats such as beef and lamb. The typically smaller amounts of Neu5Gc consumed through dairy servings may also contribute to the difference.
When the scientists considered Neu5Gc intake from all dietary sources combined, participants in the highest intake group had a 37% greater risk of developing type 2 diabetes compared with those in the lowest group.
That association appeared to be driven primarily by Neu5Gc obtained from red meat.
“Together, these findings suggest that the association between Neu5Gc and T2D may depend on its dietary source, with meat-derived Neu5Gc showing a stronger association with T2D risk than total dietary Neu5Gc,” said Dr. Fezeu. “There may be differences between sources, or other components of red meat may contribute.”
Could Changing Protein Sources Lower Diabetes Risk?
The findings raise the possibility that reducing dietary exposure to meat-derived Neu5Gc could eventually become one approach to lowering diabetes risk.
However, researchers emphasize that studies are still needed to determine whether replacing foods rich in Neu5Gc with other protein sources would actually produce measurable health benefits.
“Given how common red meat is in Western diets, the strong association between meat-derived Neu5Gc and T2D risk is an important finding. Future research should explore whether reducing exposure to meat-derived Neu5Gc, for example by favoring poultry or plant-based proteins over beef and lamb, which have the highest Neu5Gc content, could help prevent T2D. Studies directly measuring anti-Neu5Gc antibodies in large cohorts would also help to directly test the xenosialitis mechanism in humans.”
The research team plans to investigate how Neu5Gc interacts with other substances found in red meat, including heme iron (a form of dietary iron), and how these components may collectively relate to diabetes risk.
They also intend to measure antibodies against Neu5Gc directly. Doing so could help determine whether the proposed immune response is an important biological mechanism connecting red meat consumption with type 2 diabetes.
Important Limitations of the Findings
The researchers caution that their findings are preliminary and have not yet been validated. The reported estimates could change once the final analysis is completed.
Because the study was observational, it cannot establish that Neu5Gc causes type 2 diabetes or identify precisely which factors are responsible for the higher risk.
Although the analysis accounted for several established diabetes risk factors, unmeasured lifestyle and social influences could still have affected the results.
There were also limitations in how dietary exposure was assessed. Neu5Gc consumption was estimated using participants' food records rather than measured directly, and the researchers did not account for possible dietary changes during the follow-up period. Both factors could have introduced errors into the exposure estimates.
The findings therefore offer a potential new explanation for the established connection between red meat consumption and diabetes, but further investigation is needed to determine whether Neu5Gc directly contributes to the disease.
Table 1. Median Meat Consumption by Neu5Gc Intake
The table shows typical daily meat consumption in each of the five groups, ranked according to estimated intake of meat-derived Neu5Gc.
| Neu5Gc intake group | Men: red meat | Men: red + processed meat | Women: red meat | Women: red + processed meat | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 (lowest) | 5 g | 21 g | 0 g | 9 g | 
| Q2 | 30 g | 53 g | 19 g | 33 g | 
| Q3 | 46 g | 74 g | 32 g | 49 g | 
| Q4 | 65 g | 93 g | 47 g | 66 g | 
| Q5 (highest) | 97 g | 136 g | 73 g | 96 g | 
Participants were assigned to these groups based on their estimated Neu5Gc intake, calculated from all reported foods and their measured Neu5Gc content.
The meat consumption figures represent the typical amounts eaten by participants in each group. They do not establish a specific risk threshold or indicate how much meat can be considered safe.
Table 2. Type 2 Diabetes Risk by Neu5Gc Intake
Results for men and women combined, using the fully adjusted statistical model.
| Neu5Gc intake group | Hazard ratio vs. lowest group (95% CI) | Statistically significant | 
|---|---|---|
| Q1 (lowest) | 1.00 (reference) | Reference | 
| Q2 | 1.00 (0.78–1.28) | No | 
| Q3 | 1.10 (0.86–1.40) | No | 
| Q4 | 1.41 (1.11–1.77) | Yes | 
| Q5 (highest) | 1.63 (1.29–2.06) | Yes | 
The results suggest a similar association in men and women, without a statistically significant difference between the sexes.
However, relatively few diabetes cases occurred within each sex-specific intake group, making the separate estimates less precise. For this reason, the researchers presented their principal findings using the combined data.
