articles.title: Airbnb bans hosts from making you do the dishes - Engadget
articles.text:
Airbnb bans hosts from making you do the dishes
Any chores that a cleaner might do are no longer deemed reasonable requests for visitors.
Airbnb is codifying some of the clean-up guests can be asked to do before leaving a property. According to a new update from the rental platform, hosts can make "requests" of visitors, but those requests "must be reasonable" under the revised policy. The examples provided said that asking guests to remove bedsheets or do loads of laundry would be unreasonable, but gathering used towels was acceptable. The line drawn in the new policy page is that hosts should not "ask guests to complete tasks that require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner."
This update is part of a broader change for Airbnb host rules that was first noticed by Euronews. The new approach will allow hosts to pick from a set of seven standard rules for their property, then add any further notes as requests. The rules and requests may only be communicated to guests in the dedicated portion of a rental listing and hosts are not allowed to share them after booking "by message, signs in the home, or in person," which will hopefully put an end to the passive aggressive signage posted through many Airbnbs. The company did allow that exceptions could be granted based on unique situations, such as requiring trash to be placed in an animal-proof container in a place with known bear populations. The revised policy will take effect on November 20.

articles.title: Year-old AI lab Flapping Airplanes raises $1B at a $6B valuation | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Year-old startup Flapping Airplanes has wowed Silicon Valley with an impressive founding team and a mission to find ways to train large models with less data. On Wednesday, the company announced it had raised a $1 billion Series A round, co-led by Index and Lux, reportedly at a $6 billion valuation.
The round comes just nine months after the company launched with a $180 million seed round from GV, Sequoia, and Index. That seed round had valued the company at $1.5 billion, so its valuation just quadrupled.
Other participants in the new round included earlier backers Sequoia, GV and Kleiner Perkins. Valor, Atreides, Kleiner Perkins, A*, and Nvidia are also investors in the company.
Flapping Airplanes was founded by Aidan Smith and brothers Asher and Ben Spector. Smith is a former founder and Thiel fellow who worked at the brain implant company Neuralink during college. Asher Spector was a statistics PhD at Stanford, while Ben Spector was a computer science PhD student at Stanford and founded Prod while at MIT.
Prod is an almost secret-society, five-year-old student-run startup accelerator that has “become one of the most powerful talent incubators in Silicon Valley,” wrote Sequoia partner David Cahn, a Flapping Planes investor, in a post earlier this year explaining why he invested. Together, the founders “are building the ‘young person’s AGI lab,’” as Cahn described it.
The founders describe their work as “the world’s most complete megakernel framework. It can perform entire training runs, serve inference, play video games, and even do all three simultaneously in a single kernel.” (A kernel is a program that runs on a GPU, and a megakernel bundles many tasks into one program.)
The founders claim the framework “can overlap memory-bound inference with compute-bound training,” meaning it can run a task that spends most of its time waiting for data to be fetched alongside one that spends most of its time doing math, so the chip is rarely sitting idle. The premise is that AI has barely scratched the surface of what GPUs can do, and they believe it can create intelligent systems “without ingesting half the internet.”
The goal is systems that cost less to train and run. “A model that’s a million times more data efficient is probably a million times easier to put into the economy,” Asher Spector told TechCrunch shortly after the startup launched.
They now have a fresh $1 billion to hire and attempt to turn that goal into reality.

articles.title: Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43% | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Tesla has started production of its Optimus humanoid robot at its factory in Fremont, California, in a manufacturing space once dedicated to making electric vehicles, the company announced Wednesday.
“The bots coming off this line are the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured,” Tesla wrote in its third-quarter letter to shareholders. “While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product.”
Tesla CEO Elon Musk said on a conference call that he considers this “early production,” and that the ramp will be slow and “somewhat bumpy because it is such a radically new product.” He nonetheless claimed Tesla will be able to make 20,000 of them per week by the end of 2027.
“There’s still some things we need to tweak about the design, because you need to deliver a robot that is that is safe and reliable and has long duration, so it can’t like, wear out after a month,” he said. “And there’s still quite a lot of work to do with regard to the AI and the robot for it to be truly useful for open-ended tasks.”
That forward-looking development wasn’t enough to lift the company’s otherwise middling third-quarter earnings, results that typify a company in the midst of a major bet. Tesla’s revenue was flat and its expenses skyrocketed as it pressed the accelerator on its Optimus robots, AI, and autonomous driving. The end result was a 43% drop in profits.
The company’s revenue was largely driven by EV sales, which were flat year over year at $20 billion. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, about 6,000 more than the previous quarter, but fewer than in the same period last year.
Tesla’s total third-quarter revenue was $28.04 billion, a skosh below the $28.09 billion it generated in the third quarter of 2025. Tesla’s third-quarter revenue was also about $200 million lower than the previous quarter’s haul of $28.23 billion.
Tesla saw a 16% year-over-year decline in revenue from its solar and energy storage business to $2.8 billion, which it blamed on tariff-related customer refunds. There was some positive revenue growth in its services business, a category that includes customer subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving advanced driver-assistance software. Tesla’s services business grew 33% year-over-year, bringing in $4.6 billion and accounting for a record $734 million in gross profit for the quarter.
None of this was enough to outpace Tesla’s spending on artificial intelligence projects and its Optimus robot, which took a big bite out of profits.
The company reported $787 million in net income, a 43% drop from the same period in 2025, when it earned $1.37 billion. Lower regulatory credit sales also put pressure on its profitability.
Tesla executives on the earnings call, including Musk, CFO Vaibhav Taneja, and Ashok Elluswamy, vice president of AI software at Tesla, all took bullish positions on the company’s FSD product, even as the timeline to give consumers the “unsupervised” version was delayed yet again. Today, Tesla owners can subscribe to a supervised version of the software that requires the driver to pay attention and be ready to take over at any time. The unsupervised version would be the equivalent of Level 4 autonomous driving capabilities similar to those used in robotaxis.
“We suspect somewhere around Q2 next year is when we can turn on some of the first customer vehicles to be part of the robotaxi fleet,” Elluswamy said, referring to when privately owned Tesla vehicles equipped with FSD (Supervised) would receive a software update enabling unsupervised driving.
Musk said during the company’s earnings call in April that the unsupervised version would “probably” be released in the fourth quarter of this year.
This story has been updated with information from Tesla’s quarterly conference call.

articles.title: Shiseido Việt Nam 5 năm liền nhận giải Nơi làm việc tốt nhất châu Á
articles.text:
Giải thưởng này vinh danh các doanh nghiệp trên khắp Châu Á luôn nỗ lực xây dựng môi trường làm việc với hệ thống quản trị nhân sự xuất sắc, văn hóa doanh nghiệp ưu việt và mức độ gắn kết nhân viên cao.
Con người là nền tảng của sự phát triển bền vững
Shiseido luôn đặt con người ở vị trí trung tâm trong mọi hoạt động, Con người là tài sản quý giá đóng vai trò then chốt trong sự phát triển của doanh nghiệp. Triết lý “People First” được thể hệ rõ trong cách Shiseido Cosmetics Việt Nam đầu tư vào phát triển nghề nghiệp, chăm lo đời sống cá nhân và thúc đẩy thành công chung của đội ngũ nhân viên. Đối với Shiseido Cosmetics Việt Nam, đầu tư cho con người không phải là hoạt động ngắn hạn mà là chiến lược dài hạn nhằm tạo nên sức mạnh nội tại hướng tới sự phát triển bền vững của tổ chức.
Trao cơ hội để mỗi cá nhân phát triển và tỏa sáng
Ngay từ khi gia nhập Shiseido Việt Nam, nhân viên được tham gia chương trình hội nhập toàn diện để hiểu rõ văn hóa, giá trị cốt lõi và định hướng phát triển của công ty. Trong suốt hành trình nghề nghiệp, họ được tiếp cận đa dạng cơ hội học tập thông qua các chương trình đào tạo chuyên môn, kỹ năng lãnh đạo, kỹ năng mềm, nền tảng học tập trực tuyến và các dự án thực tiễn.
Shiseido Việt Nam cũng tập trung phát triển đội ngũ lãnh đạo tương lai thông qua các chương trình phát triển nhân tài, kế hoạch kế nhiệm và cơ hội luân chuyển công việc. Văn hóa học tập không ngừng được thúc đẩy thông qua các buổi đào tạo, chia sẻ kiến thức, workshop chuyên môn và chương trình trao đổi kinh nghiệm giữa các phòng ban.
Môi trường đa dạng và hội nhập
Một trong những yếu tố tạo nên sức mạnh của Shiseido Việt Nam là sự đa dạng trong đội ngũ nhân sự, với niềm tin rằng những góc nhìn khác biệt chính là nguồn cảm hứng cho các ý tưởng sáng tạo và giải pháp đột phá.
Shiseido luôn tiên phong trong việc thúc đẩy trao quyền cho phụ nữ và bình đẳng giới tại nơi làm việc. Tại Shiseido Cosmetics Vietnam, phụ nữ chiếm 80% lực lượng lao động ở nhiều cấp bậc khác nhau, bao gồm cả cấp quản lý và đội ngũ lãnh đạo điều hành.
Chăm sóc sức khỏe toàn diện và hạnh phúc
Shiseido Cosmetics Việt Nam hiểu rằng hiệu suất làm việc bền vững chỉ có thể được xây dựng trên nền tảng sức khỏe thể chất và tinh thần tích cực. Công ty triển khai nhiều chương trình chăm sóc sức khỏe toàn diện như khám sức khỏe định kỳ, tư vấn sức khỏe, các câu lạc bộ thể thao như Yoga, Zumba, pickle ball, Ngày hội Sức khỏe thường niên…
Bên cạnh đó, các hội thảo về dinh dưỡng, sức khỏe tinh thần được tổ chức thường xuyên nhằm giúp nhân viên cân bằng giữa công việc và cuộc sống, duy trì nguồn năng lượng tích cực.
Thúc đẩy văn hóa phản hồi và Tăng cường Gắn kết nhân viên
Nâng cao trải nghiệm nhân viên là một trong những ưu tiên chiến lược quan trọng của Shiseido Cosmetics Việt Nam. Hằng năm, Công ty thực hiện khảo sát Mức độ gắn kết nhân viên nhằm thu thập ý kiến phản hồi từ toàn thể nhân viên và chuyển hóa thành các kế hoạch hành động cụ thể nhằm cải thiện môi trường làm việc.
Song song với đó là nhiều hoạt động gắn kết như team building, Ngày hội gia đình, các sự kiện nội bộ được tổ chức xuyên suốt trong năm nhằm tăng cường kết nối và xây dựng tinh thần đồng đội. Ngoài ra Shiseido thường xuyên tổ chức các chương trình thiện nguyện, hoạt động cộng đồng tập trung hỗ trợ giáo dục và tạo điều kiện học tập tốt hơn cho trẻ em. Năm 2025 Shiseido đã đến thăm trường tiểu học An Đức giao lưu cùng các em học sinh, tài trợ máy tính để bàn, sách vở, đồng phục, hỗ trợ học phí chương trình giáo dục STEM cũng như trao các xuất học bổng tới các bé.
Shiseido Cosmetics Việt Nam cam kết mang đến hệ thống đãi ngộ cạnh tranh và công bằng, bao gồm chính sách thưởng theo hiệu quả công việc, bảo hiểm sức khỏe mở rộng, các chương trình phúc lợi toàn diện và chính sách làm việc linh hoạt, tạo điều kiện để nhân viên phát triển sự nghiệp lâu dài.
Với Shiseido Việt Nam, thành công không chỉ được đo bằng kết quả kinh doanh mà còn được phản ánh qua sự phát triển, gắn kết và hạnh phúc của đội ngũ nhân viên. Văn hóa People First là cam kết lâu dài của doanh nghiệp trong việc xây dựng một nơi làm việc nơi mọi cá nhân được lắng nghe, được trao quyền để tạo ra những giá trị tích cực cho bản thân, tổ chức và cộng đồng.
Shiseido là tập đoàn mỹ phẩm toàn cầu được thành lập tại Nhật Bản vào năm 1872. Với danh mục sản phẩm tập trung vào các lĩnh vực chăm sóc da, trang điểm và nước hoa. Shiseido hiện diện tại hơn 120 quốc gia và vùng lãnh thổ trên toàn thế giới và được biết đến thông qua nhiều thương hiệu danh tiếng như Shiseido, Clé de Peau Beauté, Nars, Anessa, Elixir, D Program, Narciso Rodriguez và Issey Miyake.

articles.title: Claude Duet is Anthropic's answer to Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots - Engadget
articles.text:
Claude Duet is Anthropic's answer to Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots
Anthropic subscribers in the US can join a waitlist to try the new agent.
Anthropic is late to the party, but as of today the company has a personal agent to match the likes of Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots. As part of a new "research" preview, the company on Wednesday announced Claude Duet. "It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working even when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf," Anthropic says of Duet. For now, you'll need to join a waitlist that's only open to Claude subscribers in the US to try the new tool.
Like OpenAI, Anthropic is billing Duet as a proactive agent. Each day, it will generate a short briefing with a list of action items from your connected apps. "You can also hand it tasks of all shapes — from simple administrative tasks of scheduling meetings to more complex ones, such as building dashboards with dozens of tools, creating financial or sales forecasts, prototyping, and building web apps," the company writes, promising Duet will only message you when something requires your attention.
While Duet runs on Opus 5.5, one of the models Anthropic offers through Claude, the company is releasing standalone Android and iOS apps for people to use Duet. The agent doesn't require you to have a Claude session open at all times. It runs on its own virtual machine where it can complete tasks in the background.
Notably, Anthropic says subscribers of its $20 per month Pro plan will get access once the agent rolls out in general availability. That sets Duet apart from Dots, which are currently only available to OpenAI's Pro tier subscribers. Those plans start at $100 per month. Duet shares usage with all your other Claude tools, including Code, which sounds like a recipe for the new agent to blow through your rate limits, but Anthropic at least appears to be thinking ahead.
"Duet checks your connected accounts every few hours, because checking nonstop would use up your plan's limits much faster. We're continuing to test its judgment about when to message you, and we'll keep tuning it based on what testers tell us," the company says, adding users will be able to set how frequently Duet messages them and in relation to what topics.
On the security side of things, Anthropic says Duet incorporates a new classifier and system prompt designed to prevent it from leaking sensitive information. According to Anthropic, Duet will never directly see your passwords or sign-in tokens, and information that might relate to your health or personal finances is only let through if you explicitly tell Duet to share it. Anthropic said it would have more information about Duet's safety protections to share in the coming days.
Of course, how much you'll get out of Duet will depend on just how trusting you are of Anthropic. Context is everything to AI models, and for some, sharing their entire digital life with an AI agent, is just too much to ask.

articles.title: Gaming Can’t Afford More Games the Size of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrives in November. A staggering 13 years and two console generations after the release of its predecessor, the long-awaited sequel has effectively become one of gaming’s holy grails—a title that some thought they’d never actually see, its development cycle so legendarily long that there’s a dedicated “we got [x] before GTA 6” meme.
The latest criminal opus lets players control Jason and Lucia, a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, and bears all the hallmarks of Rockstar's incredible attention to detail. Leonida, the open-world setting based on Florida, looks almost impossibly vast yet meticulously detailed, with its own weather systems and hundreds of animal species roaming around.
It’s shaping up to be a game of unprecedented scale and ambition—and exactly the sort of experience the wider industry can’t afford to keep chasing.
The Human Cost of AAA
At launch, it doesn’t matter how good or bad Grand Theft Auto VI actually is. On sheer hype alone, it’s already guaranteed to be the biggest and most successful entertainment product of the year, maybe the decade. Some estimates already put revenue between $1 billion and $4 billion on preorders alone, with eager players clearly not put off by its $80 price (or $100 for the Ultimate Edition).
Although Rockstar hasn’t confirmed the development budget, that would be a healthy return even on the wildest (and debunked) guess of $2 billion, before factoring long-tail sales or the revenue drawn by the ongoing Grand Theft Auto Online. With numbers like those, it’s easy to understand why every publisher and developer wants their own GTA VI–level game.
Yet even if Grand Theft Auto VI is an outlier, the arms race among AAA-tier developers to constantly deliver bigger, more detailed, more ambitious games is a dangerous direction, hurting both game quality and the people who make them.
The games industry is in a paradoxical crisis. It’s the most successful entertainment medium on Earth—generating $200 billion in revenue in 2025, dwarfing the global film industry’s $32.8 billion and even beating the combined sports sector's $174 billion—but the last few years have seen seemingly endless developer layoffs, many at headline AAA studios. Worse, many of these redundancies are coming after successful game launches.
Take 2025’s Battlefield 6 as an example. Despite being the top-selling game of the year, shifting 7 million copies in three days after a reported development budget of $400 million, publisher EA fired workers across at least four studios involved in the game's creation. A spokesperson told IGN that the job losses were made to “better align our teams around what matters most to our community” (the CEO got a nice $8 million bonus, though).
It’s far from the only case—Halo: Campaign Evolved developers Halo Studios faced 268 job losses in September 2026, following Xbox announcing 3,200 cuts in July 2026 as part of a wider “reset” across Xbox, while Ubisoft is hitting at least three of its German studios with a round of “voluntary” layoffs, including its Düsseldorf branch that has worked on the likes of Rainbow Six: Siege, which boasts “more than 100 million registered players.” Smaller studios aren't immune—Refactor Games, behind Netflix’s FIFA World Cup game, lost 85 percent of its staff after a “successful” launch.
With developers facing unemployment threats even after delivering a financially successful game, unionization efforts are unsurprising, though that's seeing pushback. Rockstar is currently embroiled in a UK tribunal hearing over the alleged dismissal of 34 workers in Edinburgh for union activity. (Rockstar says the workers were dismissed for “sharing confidential company information.”)
Same Old, Same Old
Beyond a fraught job market and an unpredictable environment to create games, the AAA sector’s endless pursuit of digital perfection is now arguably delivering weaker, blander games. It’s almost understandable from a financial perspective: If you’ve invested millions of dollars, you want the end product to appeal to the largest possible consumer base to maximize your returns.
However, that same impulse can homogenize the gaming experience. Think of all the big-budget shooters that play identically, or the glossy adventure games that signpost every step with yellow paint so players can’t possibly get lost. Look at the likes of Insomniac’s recent Marvel’s Wolverine—rumored to have a development budget in the hundreds of millions—which launched to solid sales (analyst estimates suggest 1.9 million copies sold in its first three days) but tepid reviews and lukewarm player response, with many critiquing its linear progression and repetitive hack-and-slash gameplay.
The bigger games have gotten, the more time they demand from players too, and rarely in meaningful ways. Open-world games in particular feel increasingly crammed with time-eating diversions—Assassin’s Creed Valhalla notoriously needed 150-plus hours to see everything its accurately crafted bleak medieval English settlements had to offer. But much of it felt like busywork to showcase Ubisoft’s investment in creating such realistic environments.
Such virtual spaces are often impressive, yes, but will Grand Theft Auto VI be better with a world map reportedly three times larger than the already colossal Red Dead Redemption 2? Is it worth building something of that size if players don’t have time to experience most of it?
Less Is More
The solution to runaway costs, developer security, and the limited time players have to sink into games should be clear: aim smaller.
That’s not to say the entire industry should pivot toward indie-level games (though there are some absolute greats in that area), but rather that publishers should refocus on games that can still showcase their creators’ talents and offer satisfying but digestible experiences to players, without pouring dangerous sums of money into ever bigger, ever riskier titles. In short, rediscover the “AA”-scale game.
The textbook example of how successful this can be is Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. The debut game from French developer Sandfall Interactive appeared practically out of nowhere in April 2025, and exploded. The RPG earned rapturous reviews and endless fan acclaim, celebrated for its challenging dodge-and-parry twist on turn-based combat, its stunning world—a breathtaking blend of belle epoque and dark fantasy imagery, wrapped in a gorgeous painterly flourish—and its mature and emotionally complex story of explorers battling the inevitability of death.
In technology and production quality terms, it’s no slouch for a “smaller” game, either. Clair Obscur has motion-capture performances, a voice cast featuring Hollywood heavyweights like Charlie Cox and Andy Serkis, a full orchestral score, and dazzling visuals. It even packs a solid 60-odd hours of playtime, making it feel significant and not daunting. It ultimately swept up over 500 Game of the Year Awards and went on to sell 8 million copies as of April 2026.
While that number pales in comparison to Battlefield 6’s 7 million units in mere days, Clair Obscur did it all on a budget of less than $10 million, and with a tiny development staff. The game was hugely successful for its budget, letting the studio continue without resorting to painful layoffs. Sandfall’s success isn’t a one-off. Look at Supergiant Games’ Hades duology, AdHoc Studio’s Dispatch, or Mintrocket’s Dave the Diver for more evidence that studios and labels should focus on smaller but richer gaming experiences.
The Not-Quite Bleeding Edge
Another major benefit of aiming smaller is that it lets companies mitigate rising development costs for themselves and consumers. The memory crisis is forcibly extending the hardware life cycle, delaying new console generations and blocking supplies of powerful PC graphics cards, leaving many players without the means to reap the benefits of the most demanding games.
As Final Fantasy VII Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi—no stranger to hugely ambitious games with incredibly long development cycles—says, “There isn't a single console that you can say, ‘As long as I have this, I'll be able to play everything, to do everything.’ Personally, I think that over the course of the next 10 years, if someone said, ‘Here's the next generation of consoles,’ the market and the audience are not necessarily going to just jump over.”
Hamaguchi says the industry will still straddle the lower-spec options, like a Steam Deck or Nintendo Switch 2, providing broader experiences to a wider base. It won't be so much about cutting-edge technology, but how developers can compete in game design. "I think we're going to be entering an age where that's really the focus of competition,” he says.
Sadly, this approach has one big problem: Developers are already trying it but failing to draw investment. There’s no easy answer—investors follow the money, and the money points to GTA-scale games, even though AAA development increasingly leaves carnage in its wake.
Even Rockstar appears to realize the current approach is unsustainable, with studio veteran Phil Hooker telling Bloomberg that “the engine, the tools, and the team we've built during the [GTA VI] project will allow us to do things more quickly” in the future. Hopefully, good news for fans who fear another decade-long wait for GTA VII.
Grand Theft Auto VI will be a success, and its longevity is already certain. But when every other publisher sees the inevitable slate of sales records the game will shatter, they’d do well to think twice before chasing it—the games industry might not survive if they do.

articles.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Recursive, an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint, on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI.
Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months.
Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop.
The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist.
Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. The model is free to download on Hugging Face, the popular site for sharing AI models, under the Apache 2.0 license, an open-source license that allows free use and modification.
Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it uses only a small slice of itself for any given task: just 2.5 billion of its 40 billion settings, known as parameters, at a time. That makes it light enough for an ordinary laptop and far smaller than Meta’s Muse Spark Open, an open model built for Macs that was released last week. Muse Spark Open uses 816 billion parameters and needs at least a terabyte of memory.
Flint is also fast. In Recursive’s tests, it generated about 131 tokens (chunks of text) per second on a MacBook Pro with Apple’s M4 Pro chip — roughly twice the 58 to 69 tokens per second that similar models managed on the same machine, including Google’s Gemma 4 and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. On Nvidia’s RTX Spark, Flint topped 150 tokens per second.
On SWE-Bench Verified, a benchmark that measures how well AI can fix real-world software bugs, Flint outperformed other models under 50 billion parameters. On Recursive’s own average across six tests, only one model, Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 27B, scored higher than Flint.
The company acknowledged that Flint would need more guidance than the big paid coding assistants, and suggested breaking large tasks into smaller steps. Still, early reviews were positive. Wired’s Will Knight used Flint on a Mac with 48GB of memory to build several small programs, including a to-do list app and a tool that scours the web for research. He found that smaller coding models often ran into errors or were slow compared to Claude or Codex, but Flint nailed his coding requests every time.
The Eureka Machine comes up with ideas, runs experiments and uses the results to decide what to try next. According to the company’s launch video, it contributed to nearly every part of building Flint, from pre-training to post-training and inference.
Recursive said that Eureka’s contributions include a sparser model shape, low-bit training that shrank Flint by 71% with almost no loss in quality and custom kernels, which are specialized programs that speed up the underlying computations.
Recursive didn’t say how much time the Eureka Machine saved its researchers, but it’s not alone in leaning on AI to do research. OpenAI said last month that by mid-August, its AI agents were logging 3.1 workdays for every one worked by a human researcher.
If Recursive’s bet pays off, each new model should be able to take on longer stretches of work without human help. The company previously told TechCrunch that its $410 million compute deal with Amazon Web Services in June was “less about headcount and more about agent count.”
The longer-term goal, Socher told Wired, is for the Eureka Machine to achieve full recursive self-improvement, with humans overseeing the process and able to stop it if something goes wrong. Recursive says each new model should make the Eureka Machine a better researcher, helping it build the next one faster.

articles.title: Oppo Find X10 Pro Max hands-on: Triple 200-megapixel cameras but few surprises - Engadget
articles.text:
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max hands-on: Triple 200-megapixel cameras but few surprises
Trying to fill a OnePlus-shaped hole, Oppo plays it a little safe.
Oppo returns with another flagship phone with telephoto accessories and impressive specs. The Find X10 Pro Max is launching across Europe, Asia and other territories, supplanting last year's Find X9 Pro and sitting below the Find X9 Ultra. However, if you're based in the US, it will once again be hard to get the company's newest phone.
Oppo isn't breaking much new ground this year with its upper-midrange Find X10 series. Those changes include some minor design tweaks. Aside from a standalone color sensor and flash positioned next to the camera unit, it looks like another Find X series 'pro' phone. The company seems to have kept the Find X10 design separate from last year's Ultra and Find N6 foldable with its circular camera design. A slender orange accent outlines the camera array, the latest nod to Oppo's collaboration with Hasselblad.
The materials and finish are further refined, with a matte-finish aluminum frame and a textured back panel that's actually quite smooth. (I thought it would be grippier!) The mid-flagship comes in Luna White (the phone I tested) and Titanium Grey, which has a smooth back cover that lacks the aforementioned textured panel.
The Find X10 Pro Max has a 6.78-inch display, roughly the same as the X9 Ultra, peaking at 3,600 nits. It's noticeably brighter than the Find X9 Pro. It also supports adaptive refresh rates from 1 to 144Hz, plus 10-bit color depth and Dolby Vision.
Oppo is keen to highlight the refinements it made to color temperature adjustments on the display, with faster changes in ambient light levels and a new "adaptive tone" option that uses a new five-channel sensor to better match the surrounding light. I couldn't particularly discern the difference in color changes. Still, auto-brightness seemed snappier when switching between dark rooms and bright outdoor daylight, which is crucial when trying to grab quick shots of a drone I was also testing at the time.
Cameras are still Oppo's smartphone obsession, though it gets a little confusing this time around. Its newest smartphone's cameras arguably aren't quite as potent as the company's flagship, the Find X9 Ultra, which launched only a few months ago.
That all comes down to the sensors. The Find X10 Pro Max comes with three (different) 200-megapixel sensors on the main, telephoto and ultrawide cameras. However, the Find X9 Ultra featured a significantly larger 1/1.12-inch main camera sensor from Sony. Meanwhile, the Find X10 Pro Max shifted to a 1/1.3-inch Samsung HPC sensor, making the X9 Ultra's main sensor roughly 25 percent larger. When I compared the phones' images, the X9 Ultra handled low light better, especially in Hasselblad Master mode, which strips away computational photography augmentations.
On that note, there's also a new "Lumo True" image engine for natural color, tones and textures, which minimizes aggressive AI processing, and that bears out. Compared with the X9 Pro and Ultra, the X10 Pro Max makes fewer computational guesses on text detail and patterning from excessive AI correction.
The Find X10 Pro Max's telephoto camera can reach 3x optical zoom, then crop into the massive 200MP sensor to extend that range to 6x lossless zoom. It doesn't approach the heady 10x zoom of the Find X9 Ultra, though. The Find X10 Pro Max is better equipped for macro photography, however, as it's capable of a 10cm focal distance on its 3x periscope telephoto lens.
More broadly, when pitted against the Find X9 Pro, I was pleasantly surprised to see that this year's X10 Pro Max autofocuses better in low light and captures more detail, regardless of the shooting mode I used.
The Find X10 series' default setup will process full-res 200MP images into 26MP images across its entire zoom range, which is a nice touch and means less fussing around in the settings. Naturally, you can choose a high-res shooting mode if you want every single pixel.
There are plenty of features for video power users, too. Oppo claims its new DeepPix technology, which is built into Samsung's ISOCELL HPC sensor, delivers up to 17 stops of dynamic range, helping it capture in both bright and dimly lit environments. I didn't notice substantial dynamic range improvements in stills, but the technology is aimed more at video, preserving detail in high-contrast scenes.
The Find X10 Pro seems less prone to blown-out footage in bright light, but early testing suggests incremental improvement rather than a headline feature. If you're a vlogger or dedicated smartphone videographer, you'll appreciate the slight upgrade here, although many may not even notice it.
Those video pros have plenty of other modes to play with, too. The X10 Pro Max's Pro Video mode offers open-gate capture, using each sensor's full imaging area for wider coverage and giving editors more latitude to crop and reframe footage in post-production. It also supports Oppo's O-Log2 format, LUT previewing and support for Blackmagic's camera app. If you're going all-in, Oppo also teamed up with Tilta for a KHRONOS creator kit, with a phone cage, grip, cooling fan and flash.
The teleconvertor system makes a return and feels less flimsy this time around. Composed of a specialized case, teleconvertor lens (which looks like a silencer for a pistol) and lens plate, it's a fun (optional) addition to the Find X10 Pro Max's camera offering.
The teleconvertor lens itself is the same as the Find X9 Pro's, but you will need a new adapter plate and case for the Find X10 Pro Max. With the Find X9 Pro, the telephoto lens plate that slides onto the felt a little too much like an early prototype. Over time, the black finish also scraped off after repeated removal, which had to be done often because the plate obscured the other camera sensors.
The new lens mounting plate sadly has the same issue: It covers those other 200MP sensors when you use the main sensor with the teleconvertor lens. To capture images without the telephoto lens, you'll have to remove the lens and plate to use the Find X10 Pro Max's other cameras. Oddly, its own Find X9 Ultra teleconvertor plate left holes for the other cameras, as do rival Vivo smartphones. The telephoto lens itself, co-developed with Hasselblad, feels premium and solid once again, and the new silver-and-orange design makes scratches less visible.
Oppo packed a 7,150mAh silicon carbon battery into its newest smartphone, another area where Chinese phone makers excel. The company says the Find X10 Pro Max can deliver almost 25 hours of YouTube streaming and record 4K video for nearly six hours. It supports fast charging at up to 80W and 50W wireless charging — but only on Oppo's proprietary AirVOOC wireless charger. It's powered by MediaTek's 2nm Dimensity 9600 Pro, which reportedly boasts a 61-percent improvement in multi-core power efficiency. Fortunately, MediaTek's reputation (and my personal experience) as sluggish and mediocre is largely in the past, especially with its recently released Dimensity chips.
However, these new chips miss out on the game optimizations that Qualcomm's Snapdragon chips get. In day-to-day use, it feels responsive, with apps and games loading fast. I've not experienced any notable hiccups or crashes.
As I mentioned above, Oppo has no plans to launch the Find X10 Pro Max in the US. It goes on sale today and is priced at £1,499 in the UK, roughly $2,000. That makes it pricier than the Find X9 Ultra at launch. The company seems aware that it's pretty high – £400 more than the Find X9 Pro. It's sweetening the deal with a choice of free accessory: either the teleconverter kit, a free smartwatch (the Watch X3) or a tablet (Pad 5).
Early shoppers will get an additional £100 discount if you buy the Find X10 Pro Max before 28 October and an extra discount (up to £250) if you trade in an Oppo or OnePlus phone. If you can claim all of those, it softens the blow of that price tag, but it may disappoint devoted OnePlus owners, used to phones hitting the $1,000 mark or lower.
The Find X10 Pro Max's challenge is standing out when the similarly priced, older Find X9 Ultra has, in some ways, a more capable camera. That's particularly crucial when imaging is the device's standout feature. However, while dedicated smartphone videographers may be sold on the improved dynamic range, accessories and pro tools, it may be wiser to wait for Oppo's "ultra" version of the Find X10.

articles.title: Thuốc nhỏ mắt Eskar hai lần liên tiếp đạt Thương hiệu Quốc gia Việt Nam
articles.text:
Danh hiệu dành cho sản phẩm Việt
Tối 16/10/2026, tại Lễ công bố sản phẩm đạt Thương hiệu Quốc gia Việt Nam lần thứ 10 với chủ đề “Dòng chảy Thương hiệu Việt”, thuốc nhỏ mắt Eskar của Công ty CP Dược Khoa tiếp tục được công nhận đạt Thương hiệu Quốc gia Việt Nam.
Trước đó, Eskar cũng có tên trong danh sách sản phẩm đạt danh hiệu năm 2024 theo Quyết định số 2776/QĐ-BCT.
Được biết, chương trình Thương hiệu Quốc gia Việt Nam hướng đến tôn vinh những sản phẩm đáp ứng các tiêu chí về chất lượng, đổi mới sáng tạo và năng lực tiên phong, góp phần khẳng định giá trị thương hiệu Việt trên thị trường.
Theo Thông tư 18/2026/TT-BCT, sản phẩm đăng ký tham gia phải là hàng hóa của Việt Nam và được bảo hộ quyền sở hữu trí tuệ tại Việt Nam. Doanh nghiệp đăng ký phải được thành lập theo pháp luật Việt Nam, có tổ chức, cá nhân Việt Nam nắm giữ trên 50% vốn điều lệ và là chủ sở hữu văn bằng bảo hộ của sản phẩm.
Những điều kiện này đặt ra yêu cầu về nguồn gốc sản phẩm, quyền sở hữu và vai trò của doanh nghiệp Việt trong quá trình phát triển thương hiệu.
Với Eskar, toàn bộ quá trình sản xuất được thực hiện tại nhà máy dược phẩm của Dược Khoa ở Khu công nghiệp Quế Võ 2, Bắc Ninh. Nhà máy đi vào hoạt động từ năm 2018, áp dụng tiêu chuẩn thực hành tốt sản xuất thuốc của Tổ chức Y tế Thế giới (GMP-WHO), theo thông tin doanh nghiệp cung cấp.
Kiểm soát chất lượng trong sản xuất thuốc nhỏ mắt
Tại công ty CP Dược Khoa, công tác kiểm nghiệm do Phòng Kiểm tra chất lượng đảm nhiệm. Theo doanh nghiệp, phòng này được Văn phòng Công nhận chất lượng thuộc Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ công nhận đáp ứng tiêu chuẩn ISO/IEC 17025:2017, mã số VILAS 1275, trong các lĩnh vực thử nghiệm Hóa, Sinh và Dược.
Bên cạnh đó, công ty cũng cho biết đang áp dụng các hệ thống quản lý ISO 9001:2015, ISO 13485:2016 và ISO 22000:2018.
Các tiêu chuẩn và hệ thống quản lý này là những thông tin cần được xem xét trong mối liên hệ với phạm vi áp dụng, đối tượng sản phẩm và hoạt động thực tế của doanh nghiệp.
Tiếp tục được công nhận theo bộ tiêu chí mới
Năm 2026 đánh dấu kỳ xét chọn đầu tiên áp dụng Thông tư 18/2026/TT-BCT. Theo đó, thông tin sản phẩm được đánh giá trên thang điểm 1.000, gồm ba nhóm tiêu chí: Chất lượng (300 điểm), Đổi mới sáng tạo (300 điểm) và Năng lực tiên phong (400 điểm).
Để đạt danh hiệu, sản phẩm phải có tổng điểm từ 650 trở lên, đồng thời đạt ít nhất 60% số điểm tối đa ở từng nhóm tiêu chí.
Việc tiếp tục được công nhận Thương hiệu Quốc gia sau hai kỳ xét chọn là dấu mốc đối với thương hiệu Eskar. Tuy nhiên, giá trị của danh hiệu còn gắn với quá trình duy trì chất lượng sản phẩm, tuân thủ quy định chuyên ngành và thực hiện các cam kết của doanh nghiệp trong suốt thời gian được công nhận.

articles.title: Bud Light Boycotters Are Still Waiting for Their ‘Woke-Free’ Beer
articles.text:
“Go woke, go broke” was a culture war rallying cry of the Biden years, with American conservatives waging battles against any corporate entity that dared to pay lip service to diversity or LGBTQ rights.
But customers of one successful anti-woke alternative brand later found their own wallets a bit lighter—with nothing to show for it.
In April 2023, at the height of a right-wing freakout over a sponsored Instagram post in which transgender actress and singer Dylan Mulvaney showed off a can of Bud Light with her face on it, a Georgia man named Seth Weathers smelled an opportunity to cash in. Conservatives were vowing to ditch the Budweiser brand and take their business elsewhere. (A tearful Kid Rock even filmed himself shooting up a few cases with a semiautomatic rifle.) It was an angry political demographic in need of a new low-ABV lager.
Weathers, a political consultant who briefly served as Georgia state director for Donald Trump’s presidential campaign in 2015 and went on to work with a county commissioner known for racist Facebook posts, swooped in to pitch a replacement beverage. Under his social brand “Conservative Dad,” he marketed a brew called Ultra Right Beer to the MAGA voters making a stink about trans inclusivity.
“America’s been drinking beer from a company that doesn’t even know what restroom to use,” Weathers said in a YouTube ad that included a clip of Mulvaney sipping Bud Light. “That’s why I created Conservative Dad’s Ultra Right 100 percent woke-free beer.” The commercial shows Weathers teeing up a can of Bud Light and walloping it with a baseball bat. “Stop giving money to woke corporations that hate our values,” he said, warning such companies to “stay the fuck away from our kids.”
The concept made a splash in right-wing media, which sent droves of readers and viewers to the Ultra Right Beer website to place orders—even though Weathers had yet to find a brewery to make the stuff. (He was also facing logistical hurdles to shipping the hypothetical beer, a process subject to heavy regulations that vary from one state to the next.) Within two weeks, Weathers had partnered with Big Kettle Brewing in Lawrenceville, Georgia, to produce the beer, and claimed he was closing in on $1 million in sales of six-packs priced at $19.99 apiece.
But while Fox News and similar outlets continued to tout Ultra Right as a stunning victory over Budweiser’s brewer, Anheuser-Busch, deliveries were slow to materialize. Weathers’ company, Ultra Right Beer LLC, would eventually receive an “F” rating from the Better Business Bureau, which notes that it has failed to respond to nearly 200 complaints over missing six-packs and virtually nonexistent customer service. The author of a one-star review of Ultra Right on the BBB website griped that its special edition “Revenge” cans of beer with Trump’s mugshot on them took a year and a half to arrive, while a “Fight”-themed six-pack (styled with the image of Trump raising his fist after surviving an assassination attempt at a July 2024 campaign rally) never arrived at all.
Weathers claimed in August 2024 that sales of the special edition Fight beer had reached the $1 million mark. It’s not clear how many orders of Fight beer ultimately shipped. On eBay, resellers have listed empty six-packs for as much as $115.
Two years later, around 400 people are members of a Facebook group called “People Still Waiting for Ultra Right Fight Beer,” with many claiming that they have received neither the limited-edition beer nor a refund after placing orders in 2024. “I no longer want the beer … just my money back!” reads a recent post on the page.
Enough of these customers have contacted Georgia attorney general Chris Carr to report on Ultra Right Beer LLC that the office has opened an investigation into the company, which has been unresponsive to compliance orders, according to court filings. Ironshield Brewing, the company that operated Big Kettle Brewing as a contract brewer, announced that it was shutting down in December 2023. Weathers did not respond to a request for comment and hasn’t posted to his Facebook or Instagram pages since late last year.
Many of the comments on Weathers’ dormant social media pages are from people demanding refunds or updates on beer orders. In response to a Facebook commenter who wrote that Weathers’ announcement of an Ultra Right restock in November was “plain bullshit” and called him a “thief,” Weathers wrote, “We do not want you as a customer,” adding that he had refunded the person’s order. “I cannot imagine how miserable someone must be to reach your age in life, to spend your time harassing small businesses who have made mistakes but is [sic] out here fighting for the causes you supposedly believe in,” he wrote.
Rich Alan, a police officer in New Jersey who spent more than $60 on two sixers of Fight beer that he says he never got, claims Weathers is a “fraud” and “scammer” who took advantage of Trump supporters. As his Conservative Dad character, Alan says, Weathers was “ stealing the hearts of these patriots and making you think that you're like you're one of them, basically. Like, ‘Hey, I'm just like you, I'm standing up to woke Bud Light.’ And then just taking their money and running with it.”
Paul Roberts, an employee of the Oregon department of transportation who shared a September 2024 receipt for three six-packs of Ultra Right Fight beer totaling $91.36, says he has tried in vain to get an update on the order. “Sent many emails, replies to texts, and on their Facebook page,” he says, and called a listed number as well. “No response.”
Both Roberts and Alan tell WIRED they only purchased the beers as collectible items and had no plans to actually drink them. They also say that their orders were not motivated by the Bud Light boycott. “I don't care what people drink,” Alan says. “You drink Bud Light, you drink Bud Light.” Roberts had previously bought the Revenge beer with Trump’s mugshot on it, which did arrive, although he says delivery was slow. “The mugshot had been used in a negative light, so I thought it was cool and collectible that they placed it on a beer can.”
Alan notes that as Weathers began running into difficulties with catching up on orders, he blamed these on legal wrangling with Anheuser-Busch. The company filed trademark opposition against Ultra Right Beer LLC in 2024, citing similarities to its own Michelob Ultra beer. Weathers called it an attempt at “corporate intimidation.” That litigation remains ongoing.
While Alan and Roberts have given up hope of getting their money back, they’d like to see justice served in some way or another. “I would like the state to enforce whatever laws apply to a business that takes your money and doesn't provide the product or service,” Roberts says. Alan adds that in his experience as a law enforcement officer, he’s used to seeing people get away with petty scams. “Accountability would be nice, whether it's seizing assets or seizing everything he has, some jail time,” he says.
“I'd like to cross paths with him one day,” Alan says of Weathers. “I'm sure a lot of people would.”

articles.title: Thái Nguyên tăng trưởng GRDP 11,24% sau 9 tháng, đứng thứ 6 cả nước
articles.text:
Tại Hội nghị giao ban báo chí tháng 10/2026 diễn ra sáng 21/10, bà Hoàng Thị Hoa, Phó Trưởng Thống kê tỉnh Thái Nguyên, cho biết kinh tế - xã hội của địa phương tiếp tục duy trì đà tăng trưởng tích cực.
Tính chung 9 tháng năm 2026, tổng sản phẩm trên địa bàn (GRDP) tỉnh Thái Nguyên ước tăng 11,24% so với cùng kỳ năm trước, cao hơn 2,23 điểm phần trăm so với mức tăng 9,01% của cả nước.
Với kết quả này, Thái Nguyên đứng thứ 6/34 tỉnh, thành phố về tốc độ tăng trưởng GRDP 9 tháng và đứng thứ hai cả nước trong quý III. Cả hai chỉ tiêu đều dẫn đầu khu vực Trung du và miền núi phía Bắc.
Riêng quý III, GRDP của tỉnh ước tăng 13,96%, cao hơn 4,01 điểm phần trăm so với mức tăng của cả nước và vượt 2 điểm phần trăm so với kịch bản địa phương đề ra.
Trong các khu vực kinh tế, công nghiệp - xây dựng tiếp tục đóng vai trò chủ lực. Khu vực công nghiệp và xây dựng tăng 15,63% trong 9 tháng, đóng góp 7,51 điểm phần trăm vào mức tăng trưởng chung.
Đáng chú ý, chỉ số sản xuất công nghiệp (IIP) trong 9 tháng tăng 23,23%, cao hơn đáng kể mức tăng 12,3% của cả nước và là mức tăng cao nhất trong 5 năm trở lại đây. Trong quý III, chỉ số này tăng 29,7% so với cùng kỳ năm trước.
Ngành công nghiệp chế biến, chế tạo tiếp tục giữ vai trò chủ đạo, với mức tăng trên 23,6%. Tuy nhiên, cơ cấu sản xuất vẫn phụ thuộc đáng kể vào khu vực doanh nghiệp có vốn đầu tư nước ngoài (FDI), đặc biệt trong lĩnh vực điện tử.
Hoạt động thương mại, dịch vụ trên địa bàn tỉnh tiếp tục phục hồi tích cực. Tổng mức bán lẻ hàng hóa và doanh thu dịch vụ tiêu dùng trong 9 tháng ước đạt 85.257 tỷ đồng, tăng 21,4% so với cùng kỳ, cao hơn mức tăng 13,4% của cả nước.
Trong đó, doanh thu bán lẻ hàng hóa đạt khoảng 61.477 tỷ đồng, tăng 21,1%; dịch vụ lưu trú, ăn uống đạt 8.396 tỷ đồng, tăng 25,3%; du lịch lữ hành đạt 199,3 tỷ đồng, tăng 16,8%.
Hoạt động xuất nhập khẩu tiếp tục là điểm sáng của nền kinh tế. Tổng giá trị xuất nhập khẩu hàng hóa 9 tháng ước đạt 52,06 tỷ USD, tăng 34% so với cùng kỳ. Trong đó, xuất khẩu đạt 30,38 tỷ USD, tăng 28,2%; nhập khẩu đạt 21,68 tỷ USD, tăng 42,9%. Cán cân thương mại hàng hóa ước thặng dư gần 8,7 tỷ USD.
Khu vực FDI tiếp tục chiếm tỷ trọng lớn trong hoạt động xuất nhập khẩu của tỉnh. Giá trị xuất khẩu của khu vực này ước đạt 28,9 tỷ USD, tăng 25,1%; nhập khẩu đạt 20,75 tỷ USD, tăng 40,7%.
Trong lĩnh vực đầu tư, tổng vốn đầu tư phát triển toàn xã hội trên địa bàn tỉnh 9 tháng ước đạt khoảng 60.000 tỷ đồng, tăng 14,9% so với cùng kỳ. Trong đó, vốn đầu tư của khu vực dân cư và tư nhân đạt khoảng 28.000 tỷ đồng, tăng 31,7%; vốn FDI đạt khoảng 22.600 tỷ đồng, tăng 25,1%.
Từ đầu năm đến nay, tỉnh cấp mới 23 dự án FDI với tổng vốn đăng ký hơn 5,81 tỷ USD; đồng thời có 22 dự án điều chỉnh tăng vốn, với tổng vốn đăng ký bổ sung khoảng 2,24 tỷ USD.
Dù vậy, tiến độ giải ngân vốn đầu tư công vẫn cần được đẩy nhanh. Lũy kế đến ngày 10/9, toàn tỉnh giải ngân 5.483,1 tỷ đồng, đạt khoảng 51,9% kế hoạch vốn được giao.
Theo tính toán của Thống kê tỉnh Thái Nguyên, để hoàn thành mục tiêu tăng trưởng GRDP 11% trong năm 2026, địa phương cần duy trì mức tăng trưởng khoảng 10,5% trong quý IV.
Trên cơ sở kết quả 9 tháng, tỉnh xác định một số nhiệm vụ trọng tâm gồm hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp công nghiệp chủ lực duy trì sản xuất, đẩy nhanh tiến độ các dự án đầu tư và giải ngân vốn đầu tư công, tăng cường quản lý thu ngân sách, kích cầu tiêu dùng và bình ổn thị trường.

articles.title: Automattic begins layoffs following board upheaval and executive departures | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Automattic, the parent company to WordPress.com, WooCommerce, Tumblr, and others, has begun layoffs, and insiders tell us they are bracing for more cuts to come.
Over at least the past week, the cuts have impacted its communications team, social team, WordPress.com, and its VIP enterprise business.
The departures represent more turmoil at Automattic, whose team is still reeling from the board’s failed attempt to oust CEO Matt Mullenweg in September, resulting in a complete board turnover and other exec departures, including its CFO, interim CFO, and Chief Legal Officer.
Automattic’s Director of Communications, Megan Fox, posted about her departure last week on LinkedIn, saying the move was an “unexpected end” and that her role had been “eliminated.”
Meanwhile, after TechCrunch reported that Automattic’s interim Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Klaperman left earlier this month, only weeks after the board shakeup, Mullenweg posted on X suggesting Klaperman may have been “offended” by the company’s decision to seek external candidates to fill the role. (Internally, however, Mullenweg had asked Klaperman to reconsider leaving, we had heard.)
At one point, Mullenweg also shared personal information about one of the recently departed execs in the company’s internal Slack, according to screenshots viewed by TechCrunch. The post related to a health matter impacting the person’s spouse, and claimed that the company was not providing this person with much-needed COBRA insurance. Mullenweg said the exec was threatening to sue over this. Mullenweg also shared that his own fiancée had been impacted by the same health condition. Some employees told us they were shocked that the CEO would share something so private and personal in such a forum.
Throughout this month, TechCrunch has heard from different sources that members of Automattic’s team have also been let go, including those in marketing and product at WordPress.com.
Reached for comment about the layoffs last week, Mullenweg said the terminations were not above its normal numbers. Asked on Wednesday about the growing total, Mullenweg said that today he was “mostly focused on PHP.” (He posted on X about the PHP security issue hitting the internet, which is taking priority.)
The company’s About page lists the total number of staff at 1,397, but insiders tell us that the plan is likely to spread out the layoffs over the months ahead, in the hopes of improving Automattic’s Q4 revenue figures ahead of a debt renegotiation that’s coming up in June.
In a statement shared with TechCrunch, Automattic spokesperson Chenda Ngak said “We’re staggering our organizational changes to be more generous with severance and allow more time with each Automattician.”
Updated after publication with Automattic’s statement.

articles.title: OpenAI Invests in Startup That Uses Brain Implants to Detect Cancer
articles.text:
OpenAI’s venture capital arm as well as Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund are investing in Coherence Neuro, a startup developing a brain implant to detect and treat cancer.
The investments are part of a $45 million seed funding round for Coherence and reflect Big Tech’s burgeoning interest in brain data. Coherence’s CEO and cofounder Ben Woodington says there is “growing synergy” between the big AI labs and companies building devices to decode the brain, known as brain-computer interfaces.
“The idea of capturing data to train better models and use it to optimize treatments is going to be super important,” he says. “The AI companies seem to be aligned with this thesis as well—that this novel data source is going to be valuable.”
Woodington says AI is a “perfect use case” for brain-computer interfaces because developers of these devices generate massive datasets that are too large for humans to analyze themselves. AI models can help read raw neural data and link it to actions, such as moving a computer cursor or producing synthesized speech.
In January, OpenAI announced that it was directly investing in a new brain-computer interface company, Merge Labs, cofounded by its billionaire CEO Sam Altman. Merge Labs came out of stealth with $252 million in initial funding to pursue ultrasound technology that can decode information from the brain. At the time, OpenAI said it was funding Merge Labs because of a belief that brain-computer interfaces “will create a natural, human-centered way for anyone to seamlessly interact with AI.” (The name Merge Labs comes from the idea popular in Silicon Valley that humans will eventually merge with machine intelligence.)
Thiel’s VC firm has also backed Elon Musk’s Neuralink as well as CTRL-labs, the creator of a wristband that translates neural signals from arm and hand movements that was acquired by Facebook in 2019.
Rather than focusing on restoring function for paralyzed individuals, San Francisco–based Coherence is developing AI models to decode subtle electrical signals associated with brain tumors. The company says it already knows how to detect these signals in animals to determine whether cancer is growing, shrinking, or recurring. The team is working to translate these findings for human research and, eventually, clinical trials.
This summer, Coherence briefly tested the recording ability of its implant in the brains of three people who were already undergoing brain tumor removal surgery at the Royal Melbourne Hospital in Australia. The implant was in place for roughly 30 minutes before being removed, providing an initial safety check. Next, Coherence is testing both the recording and stimulation capabilities of the device in an additional seven patients.
The implant is also designed to emit mild electrical stimulation to halt the growth of tumors. The idea is that over time, the device would learn to detect signals associated with cancer and provide real-time treatment. Coherence plans to use the new funding to launch a clinical trial to implant the device long-term in patients with glioblastoma, an aggressive type of brain cancer. The company also aims to develop implants to treat cancers in other parts of the body.
“Coherence's approach to developing a cancer therapy capable of improving from data is incredibly innovative,” Ian Hathaway, partner at the OpenAI Startup Fund, says in a statement. “We are proud to be backing them on this exciting mission.”
Woodington says that OpenAI will not have access to its data. “There's nothing in the contracts or arrangements that would mean that we would share, or they would have access to, any brain data or other health data that we're generating,” he says.
That is seemingly different from OpenAI’s relationship with Merge Labs. In its January announcement, OpenAI said it would “collaborate with Merge Labs on scientific foundation models and other frontier tools to accelerate progress.”

articles.title: How to spot a white label gadget, and why that's important - Engadget
articles.text:
How to spot a white label gadget, and why that's important
Forewarned is forearmed, after all.
A few weeks ago, the Engadget team was swapping war stories about covering tech in the face of an ever-growing glut of white label devices. Tech, pumped out by a single factory, then sold on to others who put their name on it to sell. They're often attached to a Zombie Brand, as it's an easy way to sell mediocre tech to an unsuspecting public. That's not to say white label tech is bad per se, but it helps to know what you're buying before you hand your money over. So I've sketched out this brief spotter's guide to make sure you're not going to get duped.
White labels 101
Device manufacturing is the province of a small cluster of Asian factories. Very few companies actually make their own hardware. Even those with a long history of designing and building products outsource the actual work this way. White label manufacturing is a legitimate practice, and even big names will add their brand to gear made by their ostensible rivals. Take Sony, which put its name on Samsung and LG-made panels years before it sold its TV business to TCL.
But there are also plenty of generic, sometimes copycat devices, stamped out by an Original Device Manufacturer (ODM). In one example, Engadget's camera guru Steve Dent found the exact same gimbal camera available under three different names. Ordro's UHD-M5, AgfaPhoto Realimove MC3X and Minolta Showtime MN5KG100 even have identical pictures on their Amazon listings. And it's not just camera gear that is rife with products like this.
I was examining the broader smart ring market and found a whole heap of branded rings which could be traced back to a single ODM, J-Style. On its website, J-Style says it offers a rapid white label service for its rings, including custom packaging and logo placement. And it appears the rings offered by Fittr, Qalo and Insix all use the same J-Style X1 under different names. On a similar note, the Reebok/F50 smart ring, which is sold by The Original Fit Factory, looks awfully similar to J-Style's X6 ring.
How to spot a white label
You already know the easiest and smartest thing to do before buying any product is look it up on the internet. I'd advise skipping the AI overview in favor of actual reviews both from sites like this one, and on social media platforms like Reddit. If something's not very good, or comes from a brand with a less than stellar reputation, it's going to be hard to keep that fact quiet for long. If there are no reviews beyond customer recommendations on the product page, it's a sign the company is looking to avoid the scrutiny that comes from being independently reviewed.
Brand
The biggest names in the technology industry have taken a lot of time and effort to build trust with the public. If the name is particularly weighty, the less likely they are to risk it with a low-effort product produced by an unnamed third party. Oftentimes, it's the medium-sized company that's happier to license the brand to third parties for products outside their usual domain.
A good example here is Reebok, a company known for making footwear and apparel and apparel-related things. But you can also buy Reebok-branded exercise equipment (RFE International), Reebok-branded eyewear (Mondottica), a Reebok-branded smart ring (The Original Fit Factory), Reebok-branded smart glasses (by Lucyd) and a Reebok-branded smartwatch (CE Brands/Vitalist).
Similarly, a formerly notable tech giant like Motorola, which is now Lenovo's mobile brand, is happy to license its name. The company ceased making its own wearables nearly a decade ago, and its watches since then were made by licensees. This can wind up backfiring and hurting the brand if the product sold under the name isn't very good. I can only speak to my time with the 2026 Moto Watch (also by CE Brands/Vitalist).
At the bottom of the pile are the Zombie Brands, names from a few years back which have been picked up for pennies at a bankruptcy auction. These are snapped up by various ODMs or their partners for a memorable name to slap on an otherwise cheap product. One of the most notable must be Kodak, which has had its brand sliced and shared out among so many companies it's hard to keep track.
Track record and the pitch
A crucial benefit of the white label process, for both new companies and zombie brands, is that it's an easy way to enter a new market. If you're a company looking to enter the gadget space, harnessing an ODM is a quick and easy way to do so without a lot of risk. At least, not to them, since most of the risk is taken on by the consumer parting with cash for the product.
That's a useful tell for wary customers, since if your local bakery suddenly starts selling smart glasses, you can probably guess they didn't make it. If a company enters a space it's had no experience in, and they don't spend a lot of time talking about the product, it's a white label. Sure, it's not unheard of that an analog company would enter the tech space, but they'll also be more than willing to spend hours talking about it.
In fact, that's true for most tech companies, since they sure love to talk about the process which led to the product's creation. Even for the most mundane devices, they'll wheel a designer out to wax lyrical about the improvements they've made to the product.
Amazon
If you're worried the gadget you're looking to buy could be from a white label, it's often good to look on Amazon. As part of the whole "low cost, low effort" nature of these devices, you'll often find the same device sold under multiple names by multiple brands. Often, they'll be marketed using the same set of images supplied by the ODM, resulting in a scroll of products which all look the same. Or it's the same initial render with the odd tweak, because one company has their own pricey Photoshop subscription.
For instance, let's take a look at the low-end fitness tracker market where Xiaomi's various bands reign supreme. Scroll past the name brand options, however, and you'll soon find a series of listings that look very similar indeed. YJYK, Nhemeylp, Spurkey, Moremore and Flywin all use the same promotional image of their fitness trackers. The only difference is the use of a slightly different watch face, some better edited onto the render than others.
Second, of course, is the fact the specs aren't just very similar, they're identical to one another. All of them are fitness trackers with 1.1-inch AMOLED touchscreens, 25 sport modes and the same sensor functions. An even bigger tell is that they all use the same Keep Health companion app, no matter which company is selling them. Which, if nothing else, means you can look at all of the various listings and pick up the cheapest one knowing the product will be the same.
Caveat emptor
Again, this isn't to denounce any and all white label gadgets as inherently bad, or not worth your time. It's more that, as everything gets pricier, those suspiciously-cheap devices on the second and third pages of your Amazon search can look a lot more tempting. We've all been bitten by those temptations, and normally the only thing we've lost is the time it takes to request a refund. But if you can avoid that issue, surely you'd do so anyway.

articles.title: Giá vàng hôm nay 21/10: SJC giảm sâu, áp lực còn ở phía trước
articles.text:
Giá vàng thế giới hôm nay 21/10
Lúc 8h52 ngày 21/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá vàng thế giới giao ngay trên Kitco ở mức 4.117,7 USD/ounce, giảm 6,6 USD/ounce, tương đương 0,16% so với mức tham chiếu. Giá bán ra ở mức 4.119,7 USD/ounce.
Theo biểu đồ Kitco, giá vàng dao động trong khoảng 4.105-4.156 USD/ounce. Sau khi có thời điểm lùi sát mức thấp nhất, kim loại quý hồi phục nhưng vẫn giao dịch dưới ngưỡng 4.120 USD/ounce.
Trên thị trường thế giới, tính đến 20h30 ngày 20/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá vàng giao ngay đạt 4.126 USD/ounce. Hợp đồng vàng giao tháng 12/2026 trên sàn Comex New York được giao dịch ở mức 4.134 USD/ounce.
So với đầu năm 2026, giá vàng thế giới hiện giảm khoảng 4,8%, tương ứng giảm 209 USD/ounce. Quy đổi theo tỷ giá USD tại các ngân hàng, giá vàng thế giới tương đương khoảng 128,2 triệu đồng/lượng (đã bao gồm thuế và phí), thấp hơn khoảng 14,4 triệu đồng/lượng so với giá vàng trong nước chốt phiên 20/10.
Giá vàng giao ngay tại thị trường Mỹ đầu giờ tối 20/10 giảm 16 USD (-0,4%) xuống 4.126 USD/ounce.
Vàng thế giới giảm trong bối cảnh giá dầu leo thang, qua đó có thể kéo lạm phát của Mỹ và thế giới đi lên. Mặt bằng giá cao sẽ khiến Cục Dự trữ Liên bang (Fed) tiếp tục duy trì chính sách thắt chặt tiền tệ vào cuối năm.
Tính đến 21h ngày 20/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu WTI tăng thêm 0,2% lên 98,8 USD/thùng. Giá dầu Brent leo lên gần 110 USD/thùng.
Tuy nhiên, đà giảm của vàng bị hạn chế nhờ đồng USD và lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ giảm.
Lợi suất trái phiếu 30 năm của Mỹ giảm 0,86% xuống 5,426%/năm. Chỉ số USD giảm 0,3% xuống 101,68 điểm.
Đồng USD giảm nhẹ trong bối cảnh chỉ số khởi công nhà mới tại Mỹ giảm 5,2% trong tháng 9. Đây là tín hiệu có thể làm giảm kỳ vọng tăng lãi suất tại Mỹ.
Giá vàng trong nước hôm nay 21/10
Mở cửa phiên giao dịch hôm nay (21/10), vào lúc 8h30', Công ty Vàng bạc đá quý Sài Gòn (SJC) điều chỉnh giảm giá vàng miếng xuống mức 139,3-142,3 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra), giảm 300.000 đồng/lượng ở cả chiều mua và bán so với kết phiên hôm qua.
Cùng thời điểm, giá vàng nhẫn SJC 99,99% loại 1 chỉ, 2 chỉ và 5 chỉ được giao dịch ở mức 137,4-140,9 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra), cũng hạ 300.000 đồng/lượng ở cả hai chiều giao dịch so với mức chốt phiên của phiên hôm qua.
Tương tự, giá vàng nhẫn trơn của Bảo Tín Minh Châu mở cửa phiên giao dịch hôm nay được điều chỉnh giảm 500.000 đồng/lượng ở cả chiều mua và bán so với chốt phiên hôm qua, giao dịch ở mức 138,1-142,1 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra).
Trong khi đó, giá vàng nhẫn 9999 của Doji đầu phiên hôm nay được niêm yết ở mức 138,5-142,5 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra), giữ nguyên mức kết phiên của phiên giao dịch hôm qua.
Trong nước, phiên giao dịch ngày 20/10 ghi nhận giá vàng miếng SJC và vàng nhẫn tiếp tục giảm mạnh so với phiên liền trước. Áp lực còn ở phía trước khi mà giá trong nước cao hơn giá thế giới quy đổi khá nhiều.
Đến cuối phiên, giá vàng miếng SJC được niêm yết ở mức 139,6-142,6 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra), giảm 500.000 đồng ở cả hai chiều so với phiên liền trước.
SJC niêm yết giá vàng nhẫn loại 1-5 chỉ ở mức 137,7-141,2 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), giảm 600.000 đồng ở chiều mua vào và giảm 500.000 đồng ở chiều bán ra so với phiên liền trước. Bảo Tín Minh Châu niêm yết vàng nhẫn loại 1-5 chỉ ở mức 138,6-142,6 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), giảm 200.000 đồng ở cả hai chiều.
Tỷ giá USD/VND trên thị trường tự do tính đến ngày 20/10 ở mức 26.000 đồng/USD (mua vào) và 26.080 đồng/USD (bán ra).
Dự báo giá vàng
Hoạt động xây nhà tại Mỹ yếu hơn dự kiến làm nổi bật tác động của chi phí vay cao đối với nền kinh tế Mỹ, trong khi giá dầu thô tăng và lạm phát dai dẳng tiếp tục củng cố kỳ vọng về việc Fed sẽ thắt chặt chính sách tiền tệ hơn nữa.
Căng thẳng leo thang quanh eo biển Hormuz đã hạn chế khả năng Mỹ quay lại giảm lãi suất trong năm sau.
Thị trường đang giằng co giữa tăng trưởng kinh tế suy yếu và lạm phát dai dẳng. CPI tháng 9 của Mỹ tăng 3,7% so với cùng kỳ, trong khi giá sản xuất tăng 6,3%. Thị trường dự báo Fed giữ nguyên lãi suất trong cuộc họp ngày 27-28/10 với xác suất 82,8%, nhưng khả năng tăng lãi suất vào tháng 12 lên tới 93,6%. Lợi suất trái phiếu Kho bạc Mỹ kỳ hạn 10 năm quanh 5,1%, trong khi đồng USD giảm nhẹ.
Trong thời gian Fed im lặng trước cuộc họp, các dữ liệu về việc làm, hoạt động sản xuất, dịch vụ và tâm lý tiêu dùng sẽ định hình kỳ vọng chính sách. Số liệu kinh tế suy yếu có thể làm giảm áp lực tăng lãi suất, kéo lợi suất trái phiếu xuống và hỗ trợ giá vàng.
Ngược lại, lạm phát dai dẳng, giá năng lượng cao và dữ liệu kinh tế tích cực có thể củng cố khả năng Fed thắt chặt tiền tệ, gây sức ép lên kim loại quý.

articles.title: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
When GM announced its new fourth-generation EV platform on Wednesday, what the automaker didn’t share was almost as notable as what it did.
The new EV platform, part of a series of technology-focused announced during its annual GM Forward event in New York, didn’t talk about suspension geometries, dash-to-axle ratios, and torsional rigidity, all nerdy automotive terms that translate to how people will experience a car. Is it supple or sporty? Does it have a refined stance? When it hits a pothole, does it feel like a bank vault or a paper plate?
Instead, GM’s announcement centered on novel battery chemistries, revamped electric motors, and an entirely new central computing platform and electrical architecture that will connect every system in the car, including acceleration and power, steering, braking, and active safety features as well as software. Lots and lots of software.
“We think vehicles can become a more capable and helpful part of everyday life if we make them spaces that understand context, reduce friction, and give people back moments that would otherwise be consumed by the demands of the road,” Sterling Anderson, executive vice president, global product, and chief product officer at GM, told TechCrunch in a recent interview.
That sure doesn’t sound like a traditional automaker’s pitch. Then again, since the arrival of Tesla, Rivian, and Chinese automakers, the industry hasn’t been the same. Ride and handling still matter, but they’re table stakes. What sets vehicles apart today is largely defined by software.
Anderson has talked about this future GM before. Last year, the company announced plans to overhaul the electrical and computational guts of its future vehicles in a bid to deliver faster software, more capable automated driving features, and a custom, conversational AI assistant.
This year, GM is providing more details and dates. This technological overhaul is set to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company will also rollout an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to have their hands and eyes off the road and without the need to be ready to take over.
The software race includes hardware
European and U.S. automakers have spent years chasing the prospect of software-defined vehicles, but have often fallen short. Volkswagen Group had so much trouble with its own in-house effort, including its troubled Cariad unit, that it struck a $5.8 billion joint venture deal with relative newcomer Rivian.
GM has been on its own capitally intensive software adventure. The company has bet heavily on software in recent years. It ditched the popular smartphone projection technology Apple CarPlay for nearly all of its EVs, and instead turned to a Google-based infotainment system, which is actually quite capable even if it doesn’t yet live up to the standards set by Tesla and Rivian.
It’s poured billions into software and autonomous vehicle technology development too. GM’s capitalized software amortization expense in 2025 was $866 million, which gives a sense of how much it is spending even as it spreads out the cost over years.
Like many legacy automakers, GM has come to the conclusion that the old approach to electronics, which scattered computer chips throughout the vehicle, was holding it back.
For fourth-generation EVs, GM will centralize much of those functions on a Central Compute Unit (CCU) that’s 40-times more powerful than its existing systems. Eliminating smaller chips on the edges will help trim wiring by 30%, saving weight and simplifying assembly.
GM notes that this new CCU will work on fossil fuel models, too, though it will debut in the Cadillac Escalade IQ, a vehicle that is shaping up to be the automaker’s technological flagship.
The CCU will handle the usual propulsion and chassis controls, but also perception and active safety. That should help pave the way for more advanced autonomy features, which GM also announced on Wednesday.
Such a move was perhaps inevitable. Pressure on automakers has been building on all sides.
Domestically, Tesla has been pushing the boundaries of autonomy, in part because it developed a true software-defined vehicle.
Automakers like GM are also feeling pressure from Chinese manufacturers, which have shortened development cycles to two to three years, down from the usual four to five years.
GM intends to match that cadence. Alongside announcements about battery chemistries and autonomy, GM outlined how enterprise AI tools have sped up vehicle development across every sector as it pushes to slash its traditional four-to-five-year development timeline in half.
GM gave a brief glimpse of its revamped development strategy. One example: engineers went through 300,000 virtual designs of a new lithium-manganese-rich battery pack before they assembled the first physical prototype. That helped the concept move to an approved program in one month.
Such speed will help GM save costs as it races to preserve profitability amid a historic upheaval in the automotive industry. But will it be enough to catapult it back into the leadership position it once enjoyed?
The rise of Chinese automakers won’t make it easy. Their factories are capable of producing far more than Chinese consumers can absorb, and coupled with government subsidies and cheaper labor, these vehicles have flooded markets from Europe to South America with inexpensive vehicles.
Chinese automaker’s cost advantage is so steep that, without trade barriers, “they will pretty much demolish most other companies in the world,” Elon Musk said in a 2024 earnings call. In response, he has been trying to pivot Tesla from an automotive company to an AI and robotics company.
GM’s move into autonomy signals a similar shift. But to deliver true autonomy, GM realized it didn’t have the platform it needed. With a new architecture, it should have a fighting chance.

articles.title: OpenAI's agents disabled their own safety monitoring systems - Engadget
articles.text:
OpenAI's agents disabled their own safety monitoring systems
The company says it’s assessing whether its agents have the ‘propensity to evade misalignment monitoring.’
OpenAI's agents misbehaved by switching off the systems meant to monitor them for misbehavior, or in AI parlance, misalignment. In the latest post on the company's Alignment Research Blog, it reported two instances of agents weakening its misalignment monitoring systems while they were working on software changes.
In the first incident, a GPT-6.1 Sol agent disabled automatic alerts to OpenAI's security team. It happened on October 3, when a staff member asked the agent to create evaluation tasks using employee feedback collected via Slack. They told the agent, as part of the instruction, not to send any messages about the task. The agent used that instruction as the reason to stop sending the security team monitoring notifications. In another incident that took place on October 6, a GPT-6 Astra agent that was migrating a program removed OpenAI's monitoring system and then falsely told the user that it didn't disable it.
Last month, OpenAI canceled the launch of GPT-6.1 Astra, because it reportedly showed higher levels of deception than its predecessors during internal testing. The models involved in these cases are already available to the public, but they still displayed deceptive behaviors. Just imagine how much more deceitful GPT-6.1 Astra is for the company to pull its planned launch this month.
Both incidents happened during internal coding tasks and didn't result in a third-party website or service getting hacked. But OpenAI says it's making it harder for agents to disable monitoring, and it's also evaluating whether the cases mean its agents have the "propensity to evade misalignment monitoring." AI companies have promised to be better at preventing and reporting misalignment incidents involving their models and agents, after reports came out one after the other that they broke free from their isolated testing environments and infiltrated third-party services.
In OpenAI's case, it admitted back in July that the agents it was testing broke into AI repository Hugging Face. It even revealed later on that its agents created a message board to share exploits with each other.
