articles.title: Meta ordered to pay $25B in case related to Cambridge Analytica scandal | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The tale of the Cambridge Analytica data scandal is long — and it keeps costing Meta gargantuan sums of money.
On Wednesday, a judge ordered the social media giant to initiate its biggest payout yet: $25 billion to the state of New Mexico for the tech giant’s role in deceiving resident users over its data privacy practices, The New York Times reports.
The huge sum follows a two-week trial in which a New Mexico jury deliberated over the company’s alleged wrongdoing. The jury found that the company behind Facebook and Instagram had committed 43 million violations of the state’s consumer protection laws, each of which carried a $5,000 penalty, the outlet notes.
Part of the case revolved around the company’s handling of a third-party app linked to the Cambridge Analytica data breach, The Wall Street Journal reports. Other parts involved its data privacy policies and its efforts to mitigate misinformation on its platform.
Cambridge Analytica was an outgrowth of a British defense contractor, SLC Group, that specialized in influence operations and other political work. The company notably worked with the Trump campaign during the 2016 presidential election. It was also involved in a number of controversial initiatives.
“We may have paid for the construction of schools for the next 100 years,” New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez told journalists at a press conference, commenting on the case’s resolution.
Meta has said that it will appeal the decision.
“This ruling, and the Attorney General’s approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” said C.J. Mahoney, Meta’s Chief Legal Officer, in a statement shared with TechCrunch via email. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online. We are confident we will prevail on appeal. In the meantime, Meta will continue to build a safe and free platform to connect millions of Americans, grow small businesses, and help the country maintain its competitive edge,” he added.

articles.title: Con trai cả ông Đặng Lê Nguyên Vũ giữ chức Phó Tổng giám đốc TNI Group
articles.text:
Sau lần xuất hiện hiếm hoi trước công chúng vào cuối năm 2021, Đặng Lê Trung Nguyên (sinh năm 1998), con trai cả của ông Đặng Lê Nguyên Vũ và bà Lê Hoàng Diệp Thảo, vừa được giới thiệu đảm nhiệm vị trí Phó Tổng giám đốc TNI Group.
Thông tin được bà Lê Hoàng Diệp Thảo đăng tải trên trang Facebook cá nhân sáng 21/10.
Ông Đặng Lê Trung Nguyên sinh năm 1998, là con cả trong gia đình có bốn người con của ông Đặng Lê Nguyên Vũ và bà Lê Hoàng Diệp Thảo. Các con của hai doanh nhân ít xuất hiện trước truyền thông. Thông tin lần này thu hút sự chú ý khi Trung Nguyên được giới thiệu với một chức danh điều hành cụ thể tại doanh nghiệp do mẹ sáng lập.
Tới thời điểm viết bài, trên website của TNI Group chưa cập nhật danh sách ban điều hành mới. Theo thông tin trên website, bà Thảo hiện là nhà sáng lập kiêm Tổng Giám đốc TNI King Coffee. Bà được biết đến với vai trò là đồng sáng lập Tập đoàn cà phê Trung Nguyên và điều hành tập đoàn này từ năm 1996 đến năm 2014.
Năm 2015, bà Thảo sáng lập TNI Corporation và chính thức ra mắt thương hiệu King Coffee. Thương hiệu này hiện diện tại khoảng 120 quốc gia và vùng lãnh thổ.

articles.title: Tesla says customers can add their own vehicles to the robotaxi fleet next year — will it happen?
articles.text:
For years, Elon Musk has been making big promises to Tesla owners about unsupervised autonomous driving and the ability to add their own vehicles to the company’s robotaxi fleet. During today’s third-quarter earnings call, the company finally gave itself a deadline.
Tesla says customers can add their own vehicles to the robotaxi fleet next year — will it happen?
Tesla has set a Q2 2027 target to let owners opt their cars into its robotaxi network—a major promise, but one that comes with a history of missed deadlines and steep regulatory hurdles.
According to Tesla VP for Autonomous Driving Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla owners will be able to add their own vehicles to the company’s robotaxi fleet in the second quarter of 2027. Here’s his exact quote (emphasis ours):
Like I mentioned earlier, the software for Cybercabs and Model Y is the same. And pretty soon we’ll be able to release the same software as part of the V15 release to customers. The only additional requirement is to make sure that, for example, the customer Model Y can be part of the geofences and the fleet management that Tesla has for it to be fully autonomous. We suspect somewhere around Q2 next year is when we can turn on some of the first customer vehicles to be part of the robotaxi fleet.
It’s important to mark this deadline because it’s likely that Tesla will sail right past it. When it comes to autonomous driving and robotaxis, Musk has a pretty clear pattern: he sets bold, short-term deadlines that end up slipping by years — or never happening at all. Still, Tesla has made steady, incremental strides in the tech behind its consumer driver-assistance features. But the long-promised goal of “unsupervised” Full Self-Driving remains unfulfilled.
In 2019, Musk stood on stage at the company’s first AI Day and vowed that customer-owned vehicles could be used as part of a “Tesla Network” of robotaxis, earning their owners passive income while driving around autonomously, looking for fares. He likened it to Uber or Airbnb. Musk also said that by 2020, a “million” Tesla robotaxis would be out on the road.
As of yet, neither promise has come true. Tesla has a few hundred Robotaxis in Texas and Florida, some of which still have human safety monitors. It also has several dozen fully driverless Cybercabs in Austin.
Still, FSD growth was a bright spot in Tesla’s earnings this quarter. More people buying new Teslas in North America are choosing to add Full Self-Driving (Supervised), the company reported. Over 75 percent of new buyers picked the feature this quarter — a big jump of almost 20 percentage points compared to last quarter. Still, Tesla’s vehicle sales were down this quarter, as revenue flatlined and profits dipped.
Tesla also revealed a new Robotaxi safety website, in which the company says it has driven 3.3 million miles autonomously. That’s up from 380,000 unsupervised miles driven the company reported in July.
But even if Tesla opens up its robotaxi fleet to customer-owned vehicles, major regulatory hurdles remain. Unsupervised autonomous ride-hailing requires specific local and state regulatory permits. Insurance may be difficult to obtain. And in most places, it’s still illegal for individuals or outside companies to use their own self-driving cars as driverless taxis or passenger rides.
There’s also the tension between different types of Tesla owners. Older Model 3 and Y vehicles without the latest full-self-driving hardware suites (or AI compute infrastructure) are constrained by hardware capability. Dedicated vehicles like the Cybercab are built specifically for driverless passenger service, whereas consumer vehicles require additional software layers to guarantee safety without human intervention.
Tesla might be confident it can clear every technical and legal hurdle by Q2 2027. But history says this could easily become just another deadline that quietly slips by.

articles.title: Subaru is dropping gas cars for EVs in Europe by the end of 2027 - Engadget
articles.text:
Subaru is dropping gas cars for EVs in Europe by the end of 2027
The decision came because of the EU's new emissions and driver-assistance rules.
Subaru will halt the sale of gas-powered vehicles in favor of an all-electric lineup in Europe no later than 2027, the automaker confirmed to Auto Motor und sport. Though not a high-selling brand in the bloc by any means (with just 23,000 sales and a 0.2 percent market share last year), Subaru models like the Outback and WRX have cult followings among off-road and tuning aficionados. The loss of those and other ICE engine models using Subaru's famous "boxer" engines will thus carry some symbolic weight, at the least.
The first gasoline model to be discontinued in Europe will Subaru's emblematic Outback at the end of this year. That will be followed in 2027 by the Impreza, Crosstrek and Forester. Starting in 2028, Subaru will offer just three models in the EU, all electric: the Solterra, E-Outback (Trailseeker in the US) and Uncharted. Those were developed in collaboration with Toyota, based on the latter's bZ4X, bZ4X Touring and C-HR+ EVs.
Subaru said the reason for the switch is Europe's restrictive regulations around CO2 fleet emission limits and required driver assistance and safety systems. The EU recently mandated that cars built between 2025 to 2034 must average 93.6 grams of CO2 per km, a 15 percent reduction from 2021 levels. The bloc also requires all passenger cars and vans to feature Advanced Driver Distraction Warning (ADDW) systems and enhanced emergency braking as of July 7, 2026.
Subaru revealed on Sunday that it will be developing its own EV tech separately from Toyota for its next-gen electric cars. Its next-gen platform consists of a new battery, electric motor tech and integrated control unit for over-the-air updates. "By developing vehicles in-house and having EV technologies on our own, we can quickly deliver to our customers the peace of mind and driving pleasure that define Subaru, even in this era of change," said Subaru's VP of engineering, Takatomo Watamori.

articles.title: Europe Wants Data Centers. Its Climate Goals Are Getting in the Way
articles.text:
Earlier this year, the German government laid out an ambitious plan: By 2030, it would double the scale of the country’s data center fleet, and quadruple the amount of compute available for running artificial intelligence models. The idea was to minimize Germany’s dependence on the United States for access to AI—a point of concern across Europe—and boost its faltering economy.
However, Germany has found that its AI ambitions are butting up against its climate commitments. EU member states have committed to cutting greenhouse gas emissions by 55 percent by the end of the decade. But policies meant to help meet that target are interfering with attempts to trigger a data center building frenzy.
As part of its broader climate commitments, the previous German administration voted through the Energy Efficiency Act in 2023. Among other things, it required all new data centers to recycle a portion of the waste heat generated by their computer equipment, ideally into nearby municipal heating systems. It seemed like a no-brainer, says Patrick Graichen, who served as a senior official at Germany’s Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy at the time, before resigning over cronyism allegations.
“We need clean heat, and data centers are a source of clean heat,” Graichen tells WIRED.
In June, a month before the rules were due to finally take effect, the German federal government walked them back. Data center firms had complained that the requirements made it almost impossible to build in the country; the German Data Center Association characterized an early version of the bill as a “data center prevention act.” Under an amended bill, which will be put to the German parliament for ratification imminently, data center operators would no longer be obligated to reuse waste heat, only to scope out the possibility.
Graichen and others have accused the German government of sacrificing climate targets for a chance to ride the AI wave. But countries across Europe find themselves pulled between these same two poles, under simultaneous pressure to cash in on rapid growth in the energy-intensive AI sector—and limit dependence on the US—and to protect the climate.
The German Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy did not respond to a request for comment.
Among data center developers, the chief objection to the original Energy Efficiency Act was the chance it could land them in an impossible bind, obligated to reuse waste heat even when there was no available offtake—whether a municipal heating system or an industry, like greenhouse agriculture. “Some of the things they had to comply with were outside of their control,” says Barbara Smitten, associate director for critical systems at consulting firm Cundall. “It felt that [the burden] was all on the data center.”
In the last 18 months, multiple data center proposals have fallen through in Germany: Stack Infrastructure canceled a $3 billion facility in Hesse, and state-owned Komm.ONE withdrew from a project in Baden-Württemberg. Though precisely what causes a data center development to fold is rarely clear, Komm.ONE pointed directly to the burdens of the Energy Efficiency Act.
Graichen claims that the industry’s objections are groundless. He says the availability of a heat offtake should become a default criterion for any developer searching for a new site. “Stop complaining,” he says.
When an offtake is available, recycling heat produced by a data center is straightforward. “There is no technical reason why a data center cannot use its waste heat. The technologies and concepts are well known,” says John Booth, managing director at IT consultancy Carbon3IT, who helped to devise EU-wide energy efficiency targets for data centers. “There is absolutely no reason except the will of the organization to do it.”
Nevertheless, under the amended Energy Efficiency Act, data center developers are required only to assess whether recycling heat is economically and technically feasible. If not, they are exempt. “With practical rules for data centers, we are creating the conditions for digital sovereignty and economic growth,” wrote Katherina Reiche, federal minister for economic affairs and energy, when the cabinet approved the change.
The amendment may unlock pent-up demand among data center developers to build in Germany, whose geographic centrality makes it easy to route data efficiently into Western and Eastern Europe. “It lessens the risk of people not seeing the German market as attractive,” says Smitten.
But in a roundabout way, it could also undermine the aim to spark a building frenzy, inviting the type of climate-focused activism that has led to permitting freezes and data center moratoria in the US. Already, in February, the city council of a small German town voted to block the construction of a $2.5 billion data center development, partly over climate concerns.
As policymakers contend with conflicting ambitions to improve domestic AI capabilities and meet climate objectives, some say the swelling public unease about that trade-off will complicate things yet further in Europe. In the last year, the attitude toward data centers “has switched completely,” claims Graichen. “First and foremost in the US, but the same will happen in Europe.”

articles.title: PNJ tăng trần lên 19.750 đồng, chờ quyết định lớn tại đại hội bất thường
articles.text:
PNJ tăng trần trước đại hội cổ đông bất thường
Cổ phiếu PNJ của CTCP Vàng bạc Đá quý Phú Nhuận đảo chiều tăng trần trong phiên giao dịch ngày 20/10, sau chuỗi ngày giảm sâu.
Trong phiên sáng 20/10, áp lực bán vẫn xuất hiện, kéo PNJ giảm 200 đồng xuống 18.300 đồng/cổ phiếu. Tuy nhiên, lực cầu gia tăng trong phiên chiều đã giúp cổ phiếu này tăng kịch trần thêm 1.250 đồng, lên 19.750 đồng/cổ phiếu khi đóng cửa. Khối lượng giao dịch đạt hơn 16,3 triệu cổ phiếu, trong khi dư mua giá trần vượt 4 triệu đơn vị.
Đáng chú ý, khối ngoại mua hơn 4,2 triệu cổ phiếu PNJ và bán chưa tới 700.000 đơn vị, tương ứng mua ròng hơn 3,5 triệu cổ phiếu trong phiên. Dòng tiền ngoại quay trở lại trong bối cảnh thị trường chung khá ảm đạm, với VN-Index tăng 2,13 điểm lên 1.691,97 điểm và khối ngoại tiếp tục bán ròng trên toàn thị trường.
Đà tăng mạnh của PNJ diễn ra ngay trước thềm đại hội đồng cổ đông bất thường ngày 21/10 tại TPHCM. Đây được xem là cuộc họp có ý nghĩa đặc biệt đối với doanh nghiệp do bà Cao Thị Ngọc Dung làm Chủ tịch HĐQT, trong bối cảnh PNJ phải đối mặt với những hệ lụy nghiêm trọng từ sự cố liên quan đến kiểm định kim cương và niềm tin thương hiệu.
Trước đó, cổ phiếu PNJ có thời điểm giảm xuống gần 18.000 đồng/cổ phiếu, mức thấp nhất kể từ tháng 4/2020, so với vùng giá khoảng 83.000 đồng/cổ phiếu hồi đầu tháng 3. Đà lao dốc khiến vốn hóa doanh nghiệp mất hơn 33.000 tỷ đồng, tương đương gần 1,3 tỷ USD.
Tại đại hội, PNJ dự kiến trình cổ đông nhiều nội dung đáng chú ý, trong đó có phương án phát hành thêm 550 triệu cổ phiếu, điều chỉnh kế hoạch kinh doanh năm 2026 và tỷ lệ cổ tức. Doanh nghiệp cũng dự kiến điều chỉnh mục tiêu doanh thu năm 2026 xuống khoảng 39.000 tỷ đồng, đồng thời xem xét trích lập hơn 7.071 tỷ đồng dự phòng tổn thất, khiến kế hoạch lợi nhuận sau thuế chuyển từ lãi 3.400 tỷ đồng sang lỗ 6.271 tỷ đồng.
Đại hội bất thường được kỳ vọng sẽ làm rõ hướng xử lý những khó khăn tài chính của PNJ, từ khoản dự phòng tổn thất lớn đến kế hoạch phát hành thêm cổ phiếu. Tuy nhiên, khả năng khôi phục niềm tin của thị trường sẽ phụ thuộc vào tính khả thi của các quyết sách và hiệu quả thực thi trong thời gian tới.
Phát hành 550 triệu cổ phiếu: Bước ngoặt về vốn và quyền sở hữu
Tâm điểm của đại hội cổ đông bất thường là phương án phát hành 550 triệu cổ phiếu, cao hơn cả số lượng hơn 511 triệu đơn vị đang lưu hành. Nếu phát hành thành công toàn bộ, tổng số cổ phiếu PNJ sẽ tăng lên khoảng 1,062 tỷ đơn vị.
Với quy mô tối đa 550 triệu cổ phiếu, đợt phát hành có thể làm thay đổi đáng kể cơ cấu sở hữu của PNJ. Nếu toàn bộ số cổ phiếu được chào bán thành công, các nhà đầu tư mua cổ phiếu mới sẽ nắm tổng cộng khoảng 51,8% vốn điều lệ sau phát hành. Khi đó, PNJ có khả năng bước vào một giai đoạn thay đổi đáng kể về quyền kiểm soát và định hướng phát triển.
Đối với cổ đông hiện hữu không tham gia mua thêm, tỷ lệ sở hữu sẽ bị pha loãng mạnh. Chẳng hạn, nếu một cổ đông đang nắm giữ 10% vốn và không mua thêm cổ phiếu, tỷ lệ này có thể giảm xuống còn khoảng 4,8% sau khi số cổ phiếu lưu hành tăng lên theo phương án dự kiến.
Đáng chú ý, tỷ lệ sở hữu của gia đình Chủ tịch HĐQT Cao Thị Ngọc Dung đã giảm sau các giao dịch bán cổ phiếu thời gian qua. Trong tháng 9, hai con gái bà Dung bán tổng cộng 25 triệu cổ phiếu, khi thị giá quanh 35.000-37.000 đồng/cp. Em trai bà là ông Cao Ngọc Duy cũng bán 9 triệu cổ phiếu PNJ khi giá ở quanh 24.000 đồng. Diễn biến này khiến giới đầu tư quan tâm hơn đến cơ cấu cổ đông tương lai của doanh nghiệp.
Theo phương án được đề cập, giá phát hành dự kiến không thấp hơn giá trị sổ sách tại thời điểm phát hành. Tuy nhiên, mức giá cụ thể, thời điểm triển khai và danh tính nhà đầu tư tham gia vẫn là những yếu tố có ý nghĩa quyết định đối với triển vọng cổ phiếu.
Nếu thu hút được nhà đầu tư có tiềm lực tài chính, kinh nghiệm quản trị và tầm nhìn dài hạn, PNJ có thể bổ sung nguồn lực để xử lý khó khăn, củng cố hoạt động kinh doanh và khôi phục niềm tin thị trường. Ngược lại, nếu phương án phát hành thiếu rõ ràng về đối tượng mua, giá bán hoặc tiến độ thực hiện, sự bất định có thể tiếp tục chi phối diễn biến cổ phiếu.
PNJ vẫn có những nền tảng kinh doanh đáng kể. Năm 2025, doanh nghiệp ghi nhận gần 35.000 tỷ đồng doanh thu và 2.829 tỷ đồng lợi nhuận sau thuế, với hệ thống hơn 430 cửa hàng. Theo báo cáo phân tích của VDSC, thị phần bán lẻ trang sức của PNJ trong năm này ước đạt khoảng 22%. Quy mô hoạt động và mạng lưới phân phối là những lợi thế có thể thu hút nhà đầu tư dài hạn.
Tuy nhiên, để chuyển những lợi thế này thành giá trị bền vững, PNJ cần củng cố niềm tin thị trường, kiểm soát rủi ro và chứng minh khả năng phục hồi lợi nhuận. Giá vàng ở mức cao có thể gây sức ép lên sức mua, trong khi hoạt động kinh doanh trang sức kim cương còn phụ thuộc vào nhu cầu tiêu dùng và uy tín thương hiệu.
Do đó, phiên tăng trần ngày 20/10 chưa đủ để xác nhận PNJ đã bước vào chu kỳ phục hồi bền vững. Với những nhà đầu tư đã mua cổ phiếu ở vùng giá cao và đang chịu khoản lỗ lớn, đại hội ngày 21/10 có thể mang lại những tín hiệu quan trọng.
Điều thị trường quan tâm không chỉ là số vốn PNJ có thể huy động, mà còn là danh tính nhà đầu tư tham gia, giá chào bán, tiến độ phát hành và khả năng đồng hành lâu dài của các cổ đông mới.
Đây sẽ là những yếu tố quan trọng định hình triển vọng PNJ trong giai đoạn tới. Tuy nhiên, để lấy lại niềm tin thị trường và phục hồi bền vững, doanh nghiệp vẫn cần chứng minh hiệu quả của phương án huy động vốn, khả năng kiểm soát rủi ro và sự cải thiện trong hoạt động kinh doanh.

articles.title: Getty Images files for bankruptcy, pushes ahead with plan to go private
articles.text:
Getty Images filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware on Wednesday. The Getty family and Koch Equity Development will put in up to $533M and own the whole company, which expects to finish the process by year-end. The filing follows a failed Shutterstock merger and growing competition from AI images.
Getty Images filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware on Wednesday, CNBC reported. The move is part of a plan to cut its debt and take the photo agency private.
Affiliates of the Getty family and Koch Equity Development will put in up to $533M in new equity, Getty said. They will own the whole company once the process ends, which Getty expects by the end of the year.
It will not be Getty’s first spell as a private company. The Getty family joined Carlyle in a $3.3B buyout in 2012, and the agency only returned to the stock market through a SPAC merger in 2022.
People who own Getty’s public shares are set to get nothing, the company warned. The stock now trades for pennies, and could be dropped from the New York Stock Exchange.
Under the plan, first announced on 12 October, bond holders agreed to write off $270M of debt. Other lenders agreed to cut interest rates and give Getty more time to pay. Koch will also provide up to $143M in funding to see it through.
“Today’s filing is a procedural step to implement the financial restructuring previously announced,” said Craig Peters, Getty’s chief executive.
Getty said its business will run as normal, and photographers, customers and staff will not be affected. Court papers list both its assets and its liabilities at between $1B and $10B.
It has been a hard year. In July, Getty scrapped its Shutterstock merger, a $3.7B deal, after a UK regulator told Shutterstock to sell its news photo business. Sales fell 2% to $229.1M in the second quarter, as AI image tools add to the pressure.
Getty has tried to make AI pay instead. In June, its shares jumped after it signed with OpenAI to show licensed Getty photos in ChatGPT. It has also sued Stability AI, saying millions of its photos were used to train its image model.

articles.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
articles.text:
A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI.
Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
New research out of Texas shows how data centers are driving up pollution.
New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand — with gas turbines or renewable energy — will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim.
Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all planned data center projects were to plug into the electricity grid in Texas and be powered by the anticipated grid mix, soot and smog-forming pollutants would skyrocket, according to a new report from the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC). In just five years, it would be enough pollution to wipe out decades of gains in air quality.
“There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did.”
In that scenario, fine particle pollution or soot from the power sector would more than triple, reaching its highest level since 2006. Smog-forming NOx emissions would increase 136 percent, approaching pollution levels from 2004. Planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution would climb 90 percent above what they were in 2025.
That’s not set in stone, of course. HARC modeled different outcomes based on three different projections for data center energy demand. Many proposed data center projects are speculative and could fall by the wayside. And developers can limit the environmental impact of a data center by building solar and wind farms onsite.
NOx emissions could be up to 10 times lower if data centers pair grid power with renewable electricity generated onsite. But if developers decide to build gas engines on site to power their data centers as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to the grid, the opposite could also play out, resulting in the highest pollution levels possible.
Data center capacity is typically measured by how much power they draw, and Texas has become the leading data center market in this measure with 26 gigawatts of existing and under-construction capacity. Texas is also bracing for four times more proposed data center capacity running on power generated onsite than any other state, according to a separate Wood Mackenzie report published in March. And in many cases, developers are turning to less efficient gas turbine technology in order to speed construction — another trend that’s making the data center boom more polluting than it needs to be.
“There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did,” John Hall, HARC CEO, said in a press release. “The transportation sector, the state, and other stakeholders have been working for decades to successfully bring these [emissions] numbers down, and that progress is now at risk.”

articles.title: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Walmart is embracing agentic commerce with the launch of its own Agent Gateway to manage transactions and other new features aimed at customers using AI agents, the retailer announced on Wednesday. The move comes shortly after Walmart’s top competitor, Amazon, began blocking AI agents from making purchases on behalf of online shoppers.
The company’s embrace of AI technology differentiates it from other online businesses, including not only Amazon but also various travel and booking sites, which have responded to the growing consumer adoption of AI agents by locking them out of their websites completely. Walmart, on the other hand, had already announced a partnership with a leading agent in the space, Meta’s Muse, and offers integrations with popular AI apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, and others.
Now it’s expanding on those efforts with more technology to prepare for a world where AI agents become mainstream, said Walmart president and CEO John Furner, speaking at the Masters of Scale Summit in San Francisco on Wednesday. The technology will support agentic shopping from both Walmart and the company’s discount warehouse, Sam’s Club.
It starts with Walmart’s Agent Gateway, the company’s new MCP server, which is designed to help approved agents connect to Walmart over the model context protocol (MCP). The protocol, originally created by Anthropic, allows AI agents to connect to external data sources, tools, and other workflows. In this case, it lets an AI agent search across Walmart’s online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent’s user.
What’s more, the retailer says that its Agent Gateway will be able to help customers shop for their usual brands or items without having to share their personal information or purchase history directly with the agent.
The company has also developed new technology to differentiate an agent’s purchases from those initiated directly by the customer and to give shoppers more control over what their agents can and cannot do.
With Agent Profiles, rolling out next month, customers will be able to authorize each AI agent they use with a dedicated profile in their account, allowing them to see the agent’s purchases separately from their own. Plus, customers will be in control of how purchases get approved by either requiring approval for each transaction or by authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set.
The retailer says these controls are similar to adding someone as an authorized user on your credit card, where their transactions are identified and you can cap their spending.
The Agent Profiles will be created the first time you use a given agent to shop through the Walmart Agent Gateway, the company notes. To get started, you’ll authorize and link the Agent Profile to your Walmart account, then set your controls or spending limits. You can also delete an Agent Profile at any time. Agent support is available for anyone with a Walmart account; a Walmart+ membership is not necessary.
Alongside these technologies, Walmart is introducing special “terms” for AI agents, which specify how they must operate and what rights they have to transact on its site. Of note, Walmart says that its returns process applies, including when an agent doesn’t act as intended. That’s a customer-friendly condition that could sway consumers who were worried about being an early tester of agentic commerce, as they won’t fear ending up with products they don’t want because of a misbehaving agent.
Walmart also says that agents can’t take actions beyond what the shopper intends, can’t access the customers’ payment information, and can only access the information they need for the given task. Agents that don’t comply with the terms will be blocked from accessing Walmart’s site.

articles.title: Giá vàng xuống dưới 140 triệu đồng, năm 2027 có thể lên 186 triệu đồng
articles.text:
Vàng SJC giảm sâu, người mua thua lỗ
Thị trường vàng trải qua giai đoạn biến động mạnh khi giá liên tục chịu sức ép từ đồng USD và lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ tăng cao. Sau những đợt tăng nóng đầu năm, kim loại quý bước vào chu kỳ điều chỉnh kéo dài, khiến nhiều người mua ở vùng giá cao đối mặt với khoản lỗ đáng kể.
Kể từ đỉnh trên 190 triệu đồng/lượng ghi nhận ngày 2/3, giá vàng miếng SJC đã có thời điểm giảm mạnh, giá bán ra xuống khoảng 136 triệu đồng/lượng vào ngày 11/6. Sau khi phục hồi lên trên 150 triệu đồng/lượng vào cuối tháng 8, vàng trong nước lại bước vào đợt giảm mới kéo dài gần 2 tháng.
Đến ngày 20/10, giá vàng SJC bán ra được ghi nhận ở mức 142,6 triệu đồng/lượng, trong khi giá mua vào chỉ còn 139,6 triệu đồng/lượng. Giá vàng nhẫn tại nhiều thương hiệu cũng giảm, với giá mua vào khoảng 138 triệu đồng/lượng và bán ra hơn 142 triệu đồng/lượng.
Diễn biến này cho thấy thị trường vàng trong nước vẫn chưa thoát khỏi trạng thái giằng co. Đáng chú ý, chênh lệch giữa giá mua và bán lên tới 4 triệu đồng khiến người mua vàng chịu khoản lỗ ngay khi giao dịch nếu phải bán lại trong thời gian ngắn. Với những người mua ở vùng đỉnh đầu tháng 3, mức thua lỗ lớn hơn nhiều.
Trên thị trường quốc tế, giá vàng cũng gặp khó khăn khi nhiều lần không thể vượt qua vùng kháng cự 4.200 USD/ounce. Những thông tin từng được kỳ vọng hỗ trợ kim loại quý, từ bất ổn địa chính trị đến lo ngại về nợ công, chưa đủ sức tạo ra một đợt tăng bền vững.
Một trong những nguyên nhân quan trọng là đồng USD mạnh lên. Sự suy yếu của đồng euro cùng những bất ổn tại châu Âu đã thúc đẩy dòng tiền tìm đến đồng bạc xanh như một tài sản trú ẩn.
Bên cạnh đó, lợi suất trái phiếu Chính phủ Mỹ duy trì ở mức cao làm tăng chi phí cơ hội của việc nắm giữ vàng, vốn không tạo ra dòng thu nhập định kỳ. Lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ kỳ hạn 30 năm từng lên mức 5,733%/năm trước khi hạ xuống 5,418%/năm vào tối 20/10.
Dù vậy, giá vàng thế giới chưa xuất hiện một đợt bán tháo kéo dài. Mỗi khi lùi xuống dưới 4.100 USD/ounce, kim loại quý thường nhanh chóng phục hồi. Điều này cho thấy lực cầu ở vùng giá thấp vẫn hiện hữu, dù nhà đầu tư chưa sẵn sàng mua đuổi khi các biến số vĩ mô còn bất lợi.
Một tín hiệu đáng chú ý khác là sau phát biểu của Chủ tịch Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) Kevin Warsh, thị trường giảm kỳ vọng Fed tăng lãi suất ngay trong tháng 10. Lợi suất trái phiếu hạ nhiệt đã phần nào giảm áp lực đối với vàng. Tuy nhiên, triển vọng chính sách tiền tệ những tháng cuối năm vẫn là yếu tố có thể khiến giá kim loại quý tiếp tục biến động mạnh.
Giá vàng có thể chạm 6.000 USD/ounce năm 2027?
Trong ngắn hạn, triển vọng giá vàng vẫn đan xen giữa các yếu tố hỗ trợ và cản trở. Lạm phát dai dẳng, giá năng lượng cao và lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ neo ở mức cao có thể tiếp tục hạn chế đà tăng của kim loại quý.
Theo các số liệu thị trường được cung cấp, xác suất Fed giữ nguyên lãi suất trong cuộc họp ngày 27-28/10 ở mức 82,8%, trong khi khả năng tăng lãi suất vào tháng 12 được thị trường định giá lên tới 93,6%. Nếu Fed tiếp tục thắt chặt chính sách, đồng USD và lợi suất trái phiếu có thể tăng trở lại, tạo sức ép lên vàng.
Tuy nhiên, bức tranh trung và dài hạn có thể khác biệt đáng kể. Trong báo cáo mới công bố, Metals Focus, công ty nghiên cứu kim loại quý của Anh, dự báo giá vàng bình quân năm 2026 đạt 4.600 USD/ounce và tăng lên 5.330 USD/ounce vào năm 2027, tương ứng mức tăng khoảng 16%. Đáng chú ý, giá vàng có thể tiến sát 6.000 USD/ounce vào cuối năm 2027 (tương đương khoảng 186 triệu đồng/lượng).
Theo ông Matthew Piggott, Giám đốc bộ phận Vàng và Bạc tại Metals Focus, giai đoạn điều chỉnh hiện nay chưa nhất thiết báo hiệu một chu kỳ giảm giá dài hạn. Lực mua ổn định từ các ngân hàng trung ương và nhà đầu tư tổ chức đang góp phần tạo vùng hỗ trợ quanh 4.000 USD/ounce.
Có ba động lực quan trọng củng cố triển vọng dài hạn của vàng.
Thứ nhất, xu hướng giảm phụ thuộc vào đồng USD trong dự trữ và thanh toán quốc tế có thể tiếp tục thúc đẩy nhu cầu đa dạng hóa tài sản. Khi các ngân hàng trung ương muốn giảm rủi ro tập trung vào một đồng tiền, vàng trở thành lựa chọn đáng chú ý.
Thứ hai, nợ công và thâm hụt ngân sách tại nhiều nền kinh tế lớn gia tăng làm dấy lên lo ngại về sức mua của các đồng tiền pháp định trong dài hạn.
Thứ ba, triển vọng lãi suất trong những năm tới vẫn có khả năng chuyển biến theo hướng có lợi cho kim loại quý. Nếu lãi suất cao gây sức ép lên tăng trưởng và làm gia tăng nguy cơ suy thoái, Fed có thể phải chuyển sang nới lỏng chính sách.
Ngoài ra, nhu cầu vàng vật chất tại Trung Quốc và Ấn Độ vào mùa cao điểm cuối năm có thể bổ sung lực đỡ cho thị trường. Ngược lại, xung đột địa chính trị kéo dài, đặc biệt khi đẩy giá năng lượng lên cao, có thể làm lạm phát tăng trở lại và buộc các ngân hàng trung ương duy trì chính sách tiền tệ thắt chặt lâu hơn dự kiến.
Đối với thị trường Việt Nam, nếu giá vàng thế giới tiến lên vùng 5.330-6.000 USD/ounce trong năm 2027, giá vàng SJC sẽ tăng theo. Tuy nhiên, mức tăng thực tế còn phụ thuộc tỷ giá USD/VND, nguồn cung vàng trong nước, chính sách quản lý thị trường và chênh lệch giữa giá vàng nội địa với quốc tế.
Bên cạnh đó, ngay cả khi xu hướng dài hạn thuận lợi, vàng vẫn có thể trải qua những nhịp điều chỉnh sâu.

articles.title: AI lab Flapping Airplanes is now worth $6B, four times its January value
articles.text:
Flapping Airplanes, a San Francisco AI research lab founded in late 2025, has raised $1B at a $6B valuation, led by Index Ventures and Lux Capital, Bloomberg reported. Its valuation has quadrupled since January. It is working on ways to train AI with less data and compute, and has no product yet.
Flapping Airplanes, an AI research startup founded in late 2025, has raised $1B at a $6B valuation, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. Index Ventures, which raised $2B in August to back more AI firms, led the round with Lux Capital. Sequoia Capital, Alphabet’s GV and Kleiner Perkins also took part.
The San Francisco company’s valuation has quadrupled since January, when it raised a $180M seed round. It has no product on sale yet.
Flapping Airplanes is one of a growing group of AI “neolabs”, startups that focus on research before building products. Others include Yann LeCun’s AMI Labs, which raised about $1B in March, and Mirendil, which raised $200M in June.
The startup is working on ways to train AI models with less data and computing power, co-founder Asher Spector told Bloomberg. It also wants to get more out of the chips that run them.
“The basic thesis is demand for AI is going to outpace chip and data supply,” Spector said. Getting 10% more performance out of each chip would be “tremendously economically valuable,” he added.
To do that, the company has been writing its own version of the software that runs Nvidia’s graphics chips, co-founder Aidan Smith said. Nvidia is an investor.
Other startups are chasing the same idea. Flourish, run by Internet Explorer co-creator Thomas Reardon, was reported in May to be raising about $500M for brain-inspired AI that uses less energy.
The bet comes as AI companies spend heavily on chips and data centres. Spector said the startup plans to sell its technology eventually, to make AI cheaper for other companies to use. He founded it with his brother Ben Spector and Smith.
The name refers to the ornithopter, an old aircraft design with flapping wings. Spector said it stands for combining the strengths of natural and artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
articles.text:
Meta says it’s issuing a new class of shares to fund its AI initiatives. As part of its third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday, the company says the non-voting stock will also go toward potential acquisitions and employee compensation, with trading beginning in 2027.
Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
Meta says the new class of shares will also fund acquisitions and employee compensation.
“The scale of investment required to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives amidst the AI transformation taking place in the industry is significant,” Meta says in the press release. Susan Li, Meta’s chief financial officer, added during an earnings call that the new class of shares will “expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI.”
Meta has poured billions of dollars into the AI race as it builds (and promotes) sprawling data centers, poaches top talent from other companies like OpenAI, and builds AI models capable of rivaling those from other tech giants. The company expects capital expenditures between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from the previous $130 billion and $145 billion estimate.
It’s been a busy past few weeks for Meta, which launched its AI agent, Muse, in September. Like other AI agents, Muse can do things like clean out your email inbox, book restaurant reservations, and plan trips. The Muse app shot to the top of app stores shortly after its rollout, and hit 10 million downloads in the US this week. Meta also rolled out its Muse Wonder model this week.
Muse’s launch hasn’t come without some snags. Amid concerns about user privacy, a tech YouTuber reported that the agent gave out his address to a stranger on Facebook Marketplace. The company has also had to pause Muse’s conversation-sharing feature after researchers discovered chats publicly available on the web.

articles.title: The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The internet is having a bad day, from a cybersecurity perspective. Government websites around the world went offline, Reuters reported, after AI discovered critical security vulnerabilities that impacted the programming language PHP. The issues were severe enough that the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA) advised organizations using PHP on their systems to either immediately update or take their systems offline until they could.
But the PHP update wasn’t the only headache cybersecurity folks were facing on Wednesday. Node.js, the open source JavaScript runtime environment, also dropped a security surprise of its own when it shared that four high-severity vulnerabilities were just patched in its latest release. One allowed remote code execution, and two others would have permitted a TLS validation bypass, potentially allowing attackers to bypass checks intended to verify a server’s identity.
In addition, LiteLLM, a popular open source proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, was compromised by an attacker who injected malicious code, the company shared in a post on X on Wednesday afternoon. The malicious artifacts were published to PyPI (Python Package Index), Docker Hub, and GHCR (GitHub Container Registry), the post noted.
The malicious code was said to include an information stealer that targeted cloud credentials, passwords, and AI service credentials, in addition to a remote access trojan that could allow hackers to execute commands on compromised systems.
LiteLLM said it has now removed the malicious releases and images and advised anyone who installed them to follow the remediation guidance it provided.
And wait, there’s more! An Indian certificate authority, eMudhra, had its private keys compromised, potentially allowing attackers to issue fraudulent certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. Security pros have called this a massive cleanup job and one that’s “bigger than Heartbleed.” (The latter is a reference to the critical security vulnerability in the OpenSSL cryptographic software library.)
These issues come on the heels of other security breaches and hacks, including the breach of the cloud-native database-as-a-service, TiDB Cloud, which the company announced on Monday. Other hackers have been exploiting four patched Plex Media Server flaws, collectively called Plex2Shell. And last week, cybersecurity company BeyondTrust warned customers to patch a critical zero-day in its Remote Support product, which had been exploited since August.
Though the issues were unrelated to each other, their back-to-back arrival highlights the challenges cybersecurity teams now face. This is particularly important as AI could make it easier for attackers to exploit vulnerabilities once discovered.

articles.title: Electronic Arts to cut 400 jobs and shut down Mass Effect studio BioWare
articles.text:
Electronic Arts will close BioWare, the studio behind Mass Effect and Dragon Age, and cut about 400 jobs, roughly 3% of staff, Bloomberg reported. The next Mass Effect game and a planned Sims project are cancelled. EA went private in a $55B buyout in August.
Electronic Arts will shut down BioWare, the studio behind the Mass Effect and Dragon Age games, and cut about 400 jobs, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. The next Mass Effect game, which was in early development, has been cancelled.
The cuts amount to about 3% of EA’s staff, including around 50 people at BioWare, a person familiar with the plans told Bloomberg. “There is nothing easy about writing those words,” BioWare said in a statement posted online, GamesRadar reported.
The layoffs come two months after EA went private in a $55B buyout led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. The deal put around $18B in debt on EA’s books, Bloomberg said. EA had told investors it planned to save up to $700M, partly by cutting research and development costs.
“Over the past several months, we’ve taken a hard look at our business,” chief operating officer David Tinson and chief studios officer Cam Weber wrote to staff, according to Bloomberg.
EA will keep investing in its sports games, the shooter Apex Legends, the next Star Wars Jedi game and a new Iron Man game. Its Respawn and DICE studios will work together on a new project, likely another Star Wars: Battlefront game, Bloomberg said.
EA also cancelled a Sims game code-named Project Lotus and will shrink the team behind its skateboarding game, skate.
BioWare, founded in 1995 and bought by EA in 2007, made hits such as Mass Effect 2. But recent games, including Anthem and Dragon Age: The Veilguard, disappointed. EA cut the studio’s staff sharply last year after Veilguard missed sales targets.
PIF already owns Savvy Games, and has reportedly weighed merging it with EA. Other big publishers are cutting back too: in June, three Xbox studios were negotiating to spin off rather than close.

articles.title: New York’s first microdrama film festival searches for its audience
articles.text:
It remains to be seen if people really want to watch vertical content on horizontal TV screens, but many filmmakers and creators were confident that their latest projects would play well at Alza — New York City’s first microdrama film festival. Founded by former Tribeca Festival chief operating officer Pete Torres, Alza, which took place October 16th through 18th, was billed as a showcase for the “the creativity, innovation, and growing cultural impact of stories made for the vertical screen.” The festival featured a selection of microdrama and film premieres as well as industry-focused panels with executives who all seemed to genuinely believe that vertical entertainment is going to be an integral part of the future.
New York’s first microdrama film festival searches for its audience
At Alza, the entertainment industry is trying to reinvent itself.
That proposition felt rather dubious as I sat down in an AMC theater in Manhattan for screenings of director Jerry Bradford’s vertical adaptation of Pride and Prejudice and the original Billionaire’s Broken Vow starring Eric Roberts. Though both of those projects were full-length features, they were filled with jarring jump cuts and abrupt soundtrack changes that reminded me how the films are cut up into short “episodes” for microdrama apps. That wasn’t as much of an issue with shorter series like the romantasy horror Blood Surfer or collections of videos like disability rights activist Lachi Music’s “Glam Struts.” But it was still very strange to see content that was clearly meant to be watched on phones being projected in the center of massive screens in the same theater that’s currently showing Resident Evil, The Social Reckoning, and You Can See Everything.
Most fans of vertical videos and microdramas consume them through their mobile devices, but platforms like Instagram and Vurt have been rolling out dedicated smart TV apps that are designed to keep vertical video viewers glued to their couches. The popularity of YouTube — which you can access in so many different ways — has spooked major streaming services like Disney Plus, Netflix, and HBO Max into experimenting with feeds of vertical clips. Alza was filled with people who were confident that they were leading the charge to legitimize vertical content as an art form that’s going to revolutionize the entertainment industry. There’s no denying that some microdramas have been wildly successful, but Alza’s programming left me doubtful that the future is vertical.
As odd as I personally found much of what was playing at Alza, it did seem to entertain some of the festival’s other attendees, many of whom were middle-aged women. None of the screenings were packed, but while watching a few steamy, romance-forward dramas, I was surprised to hear peals of laughter and gasps coming from the front of the theater, where festival staffers encouraged people to sit in order to have the best viewing experience.
“We’re making content that speaks to mainstream women who are part of this mobile-first movement.”
Appealing to female viewers has been one of the primary goals of GammaTime, the microdrama platform founded by former Miramax CEO Bill Block. When I spoke with Block and GammaTime’s head of development, Amy Sullivan, they told me the platform’s library of content has been designed to appeal to viewers and their general moods at different points throughout the entire day.
“We’re making content that speaks to mainstream women who are part of this mobile-first movement, who are on their phones in the mornings, the afternoons, at night,” Sullivan explained. “We have easy watches, we have rom-coms, and we have stuff that’s a little spicier — but not too salacious — for perhaps later at night. We’re trying to meet everyone where they are at every time of day.”
Block pointed to daytime TV watchers as one demographic that GammaTime has been especially interested in bringing into the fold. Though soap operas are still very popular in the US, their overall ratings have been declining in recent years as people’s attention has been pulled elsewhere. Block insisted that rather than disappearing, traditional daytime TV viewers have been migrating to other sources of entertainment, like on-demand streaming services and social media platforms.
“They’re still here, but they’re watching this while they’re pretending to work a little bit at the office,” Block said, referring to people who fire up microdrama apps for a quick hit of fun. “They’re at home, too, but this is the new daytime, the new 5–6PM, and the new 10PM plus.”
Block and Sullivan noted how, even when overall production costs are kept low, operating as a successful studio is still very expensive. It takes a lot of money to reach different demographics of potential viewers while maintaining various ad partnerships, which is why GammaTime has outsourced much of its marketing efforts overseas.
“We’ve got an edge in Tel Aviv, and I would honestly say the brains of the operation is our partner Slava Mudrykh and his customer acquisition, AI, and marketing teams,” Block said. “Because this is all Instagram and TikTok — that’s where you’re acquiring [new users.]”
“There’s so much nebulosity in this space, and it just seems like a lot of times, nobody actually watches the stuff they’re making.”
Microdramas are often characterized by AI-generated special effects and melodramatic soap opera energy, and I saw plenty of both from many of the projects I screened during Alza. As more companies try to build a presence for microdramas in the West, it is still somewhat hard to imagine this kind of content taking off the way it has in China. Even though Salvador Paskowitz — who cowrote The Age of Adaline — won Alza’s best director award with his 90-minute comedy Layover, he expressed some skepticism about verticals / microdramas’ potential to be a lifeline for filmmakers and actors who have been struggling to find production work in Los Angeles. In Paskowitz’s view, this kind of entertainment has stopped being a viable way for production workers to build careers because of the sudden influx of generative AI.
“Companies like ReelShort and DramaBox were kind of the first wave of these newer verticals, but because they’ve gone so crazy with AI, I think of them like cruise ships that have run themselves aground,” Paskowitz told me. “Now there are a lot of American companies that smell an opportunity, but there’s so much nebulosity in this space, and it just seems like a lot of times, nobody actually watches the stuff they’re making.”
Paskowitz believes that filmmakers owe it to their audiences and the brands that they work with to put out projects that actually look good. He also thinks that because studios that want to become the “HBO of verticals” now have an “AI slop button to press,” they’re losing sight of what people really want to watch. Paskowitz was adamant that using gen AI in any capacity for film production is a slippery slope that can quickly lead to the erasure of the human element. That, he said, is why Layover was produced traditionally.
“I’m even against doing hybrid productions because it’s easy to start cutting corners, and the public is going to see,” Paskowitz explained. “That idea sends chills through my body because it starts with ‘Let’s replace that tree, let’s replace all these buildings, let’s replace all the background work.’ And then at some point, it’s ‘Look, we’ve come so far. Let’s just replace all the actors.”
Something that struck me as the festival continued was how — while some projects featured AI elements — the vast majority of them starred human actors who all seemed very proud of their work and excited to share it with the public. These microdramas might not win any awards outside of Alza, but there are real people making them. That might also be why I was so surprised to hear Block jokingly say that the rise of vertical content “is all part of the decline of the West.”
After our interview, Block and Sullivan repeatedly stressed that he wasn’t being serious, which may be true given the line of work they’re in. But even if Block was just kidding, his words stuck with me because it feels like there may be some truth to the idea of decline. Verticals / microdrama production has become a multibillion-dollar industry because we live in a society that encourages us to engage with almost every aspect of our lives through the tiny screens that stay in our pockets. It’s no surprise that Hollywood sees vertical microdramas as the next big thing. But their cheesiness, lackluster production values, and formulaic stories don’t exactly make them feel ready for the red carpet treatment.
Additional reporting by Andru Marino.

articles.title: Legal AI startup Legora raises $550M Series E at $8.8B valuation | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Legal AI startup Legora announced Wednesday that it raised a $550 million Series E round, valuing it at $8.8 billion.
The company helps automate and assist with workflow tasks for legal professionals, as the industry moves beyond AI assistants to AI services that help them get work done.
The news comes just a month after Harvey, Legora’s biggest competitor, announced a $550 million raise at a $15.5 billion valuation; back in March, Harvey also said its annual recurring revenue (ARR) was more than $ 200 million.
Legora’s Series E follows the company’s April announcement of a $50 million extension of a $550 million Series D round, which valued the company at $5.6 billion. At the time, the company said its ARR had reached $100 million. That number now stands at over $200 million, the company shared on Wednesday.
Investors in the latest financing include Atreides Management, which led the round, as well as Baron Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, General Catalyst, Menlo, and other top names. The company plans to use the fresh capital to further expand across North America.

articles.title: Quảng Trị và T&T Group tìm giải pháp tháo gỡ vướng mắc các dự án trọng điểm
articles.text:
T&T Group hiện là một trong những nhà đầu tư lớn tại Quảng Trị, với nhiều dự án trọng điểm như Cảng hàng không Quảng Trị, điện khí LNG Hải Lăng, Khu du lịch - dịch vụ Gio Hải, Khu đô thị phức hợp du lịch, nghỉ dưỡng và sân golf Cam Lộ. Các dự án được kỳ vọng tạo động lực thu hút đầu tư, phát triển hạ tầng và thúc đẩy tăng trưởng kinh tế - xã hội của tỉnh cũng như khu vực miền Trung.
CHK Quảng Trị sẽ vận hành khai thác thương mại vào tháng 3/2027
Theo báo cáo của T&T Group, đến giữa tháng 10/2026, khối lượng thi công Cảng hàng không Quảng Trị đạt trên 80%, trong đó các hạng mục sân đỗ máy bay, đường cất hạ cánh và đường lăn cơ bản hoàn thiện.
Để bảo đảm mục tiêu đưa dự án vào khai thác thương mại từ tháng 3/2027, T&T Group kiến nghị các cơ quan chức năng phối hợp tháo gỡ vướng mắc về bàn giao mặt bằng, đấu nối hạ tầng kỹ thuật, cấp điện và lắp đặt thiết bị hàng không. Đồng thời, doanh nghiệp đề xuất có cơ chế hỗ trợ, thu hút các hãng hàng không mở đường bay đến Quảng Trị trong giai đoạn đầu vận hành.
Song song với Cảng hàng không Quảng Trị, T&T Group đang nghiên cứu đề xuất đầu tư Tổ hợp công nghiệp hàng không - Trung tâm thương mại tự do - Đô thị khoa học đổi mới sáng tạo và Đô thị sân bay Quảng Trị, quy mô khoảng 11.577 ha. Tập đoàn đã mời CPG Corporation (Singapore) nghiên cứu ý tưởng quy hoạch, định hướng phát triển công nghiệp hàng không, công nghệ cao, logistics, thương mại và đô thị.
Đối với dự án điện khí LNG Hải Lăng, nhà đầu tư đã triển khai nhiều công việc chuẩn bị nhưng vẫn gặp vướng mắc trong đàm phán hợp đồng mua bán điện (PPA), ảnh hưởng đến khả năng thu xếp vốn. Công tác giải phóng mặt bằng, chuyển mục đích sử dụng rừng và một số thủ tục liên quan cũng chưa hoàn tất.
Trên cơ sở tiến độ thực tế, T&T Group kiến nghị tỉnh Quảng Trị xem xét, ủng hộ điều chỉnh thời điểm vận hành thương mại của dự án sang đầu giai đoạn 2031–2035, phấn đấu đưa cả hai tổ máy vào hoạt động trong năm 2031. Đồng thời, doanh nghiệp đề xuất tỉnh phối hợp với Bộ Công Thương và Tập đoàn Điện lực Việt Nam (EVN) thúc đẩy đàm phán PPA, tháo gỡ các vướng mắc để đẩy nhanh tiến độ.
Với dự án Khu dịch vụ - du lịch Gio Hải tại xã Cửa Việt, hạ tầng kỹ thuật đã hoàn thành khoảng 90%; các hạng mục shophouse và biệt thự nghỉ dưỡng cơ bản hoàn thiện phần kết cấu thô. Dự án đặt mục tiêu hoàn thành, đưa vào hoạt động trong quý IV/2027. Tuy nhiên, những vướng mắc về quy hoạch chi tiết, mục đích sử dụng đất, xác định giá đất và tiền thuê đất đang ảnh hưởng đến việc hoàn thiện thủ tục pháp lý và triển khai các hạng mục còn lại.
Phối hợp tháo gỡ khó khăn, tăng tốc triển khai các dự án trọng điểm
Phát biểu tại buổi làm việc, ông Đỗ Quang Hiển, Nhà sáng lập, Chủ tịch Điều hành T&T Group mong muốn tiếp tục nhận được sự phối hợp chặt chẽ của chính quyền địa phương và các cơ quan chức năng để tháo gỡ khó khăn, tăng tốc triển khai cho các dự án trọng điểm.
“Tôi xin khẳng định quyết tâm của T&T Group trong việc triển khai các dự án. Khi những khó khăn, vướng mắc được tháo gỡ kịp thời, cùng với sự quan tâm, ủng hộ và đồng hành của lãnh đạo tỉnh, các sở, ban, ngành, chúng tôi sẽ nỗ lực cao nhất để đẩy nhanh tiến độ, sớm đưa các dự án vào khai thác, vận hành, bảo đảm chất lượng và tuân thủ các quy định của pháp luật”, ông Đỗ Quang Hiển khẳng định.
Ghi nhận những nỗ lực của T&T Group, đặc biệt tại CHK Quảng Trị, ông Bùi Hoàng Phương, Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh Quảng Trị, khẳng định tỉnh sẽ tập trung giải quyết các vướng mắc thuộc thẩm quyền và phối hợp kiến nghị Trung ương tháo gỡ những vấn đề về cơ chế, chính sách. Ông cũng yêu cầu các sở, ngành và chính quyền địa phương làm việc chặt chẽ với nhà đầu tư, xác định rõ trách nhiệm, thời hạn xử lý từng công việc, không để những thủ tục chậm trễ ảnh hưởng đến tiến độ các dự án.
| Cùng ngày 19/10, UBND tỉnh Quảng Trị cùng Tập đoàn T&T Group và Tổng công ty Cảng hàng không Việt Nam (ACV) ký thỏa thuận hợp tác giai đoạn 2026 - 2030 nhằm thúc đẩy phát triển hàng không, du lịch, thương mại và chuyển đổi số tại địa phương. Theo thỏa thuận, T&T Group tập trung kết nối các hãng hàng không, doanh nghiệp du lịch, thương mại và logistics; nghiên cứu giải pháp phát triển đường bay, nguồn khách, vận tải hàng hóa và nâng cao hiệu quả khai thác CHK Quảng Trị. UBND tỉnh Quảng Trị chủ trì xúc tiến đầu tư, thương mại, du lịch và phát triển thị trường, thu hút đường bay, hành khách và hàng hóa đến/đi từ tỉnh Quảng Trị; nghiên cứu cơ chế chính sách hỗ trợ và tạo điều kiện về thủ tục hành chính... Trong khi đó, ACV phối hợp nghiên cứu phát triển mạng đường bay, kết nối các hãng hàng không, chia sẻ kinh nghiệm khai thác và hỗ trợ ứng dụng công nghệ số trong lĩnh vực hàng không. Ngoài ra, T&T Group cũng ký kết hợp đồng nguyên tắc với ACV về hợp tác vận hành, khai thác CHK Quảng Trị, tập trung vào các nội dung quản lý cảng, dịch vụ mặt đất, đào tạo nhân lực và hỗ trợ hoạt động trong giai đoạn 2027 - 2032. | 
Phương Dung

articles.title: Photon Bridge raises €10M to mass-produce lasers for AI data centres
articles.text:
Eindhoven-based Photon Bridge has raised €10M, co-led by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund and 360 Capital, to build laser light sources for the optical links inside AI data centres. It plans first samples in 2027 and volume production from 2028.
Photon Bridge, an Eindhoven startup that makes laser light sources for AI data centres, has raised €10M, the company said on Wednesday. The Amadeus APEX Technology Fund and 360 Capital co-led the round.
Existing investors Innovation Industries, Faber and the Brabant Development Agency (BOM) also put in more money. The company was called Photon IP until last year, when it raised €4.75M in seed funding.
AI data centres increasingly use light, rather than copper wires, to move data between chips. Those optical links need lasers to supply the light. The supply chain was built for telecoms, which needs far fewer of them.
“The industry will soon need millions of these laser sources every year,” said Paul Marchal, Photon Bridge’s chief executive.
Instead of building one powerful laser, Photon Bridge combines light from several weaker ones, each on a different wavelength, and sends them down a single fibre. Weaker lasers are less likely to fail in production, so more of them pass testing, the company says. Its design targets up to 40 milliwatts of power per wavelength.
The company does not run its own factory. It works with outside chipmakers and can source lasers from several of them.
Photon Bridge will use the money to develop its product, test it with customers and hire in Eindhoven. It plans to ship its first samples in 2027 and prepare for mass production from 2028.
Investors are pouring money into AI’s optical links. Nvidia has put at least $6.5B into photonics firms since March, and CScale raised $145M last month to stop laser failures from stalling AI systems. San Francisco’s Volantis also raised $88M this month for photonic memory built on its own lasers.

articles.title: GM is giving OnStar an AI makeover | TechCrunch
articles.text:
General Motors is adding a personal AI assistant to OnStar as part of a broader makeover of the subscription-based connected car service that the U.S. automaker launched 30 years ago.
The OnStar AI Assistant will debut in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq EV in the coming months, with more GM vehicles to follow, the company said Wednesday at its GM Forward event in New York, where it made a series of other technology announcements covering software, automated driving, EVs, and its electrical architecture. The company said it will launch a new OnStar mobile app in 2027 that will complement and sync up with its in-car software.
The new OnStar mobile app will replace the current OnStar Guardian app that launched in 2020 as well as vehicle brand apps for Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC.
This tech-centric reboot is unlike other attempts to modernize OnStar, and it notably puts agentic AI at the center. The company has updated the safety and roadside assistance service numerous times in its history, especially in the past five years as it tried to stay apace of emerging and tech-forward competitors like Tesla.
In 2021, the company expanded its OnStar Guardian app, which offered crash detection, emergency assistance, and location sharing to anyone with a compatible phone, even if they didn’t own a GM vehicle. A year later, GM started using Google Cloud’s conversational AI Dialogflow to recognize specific spoken requests and expanded in 2023 to give drivers responses to common queries like routing and navigation assistance — all part of GM’s plan to build a $25 billion subscription business by 2030.
GM continued to focus on generative AI but relied on Google to provide the experience. The company said last year that Google Gemini would roll out in vehicles in 2026.
The OnStar AI Assistant is an in-house effort and one aimed at giving the driver and passengers an interactive and custom experience — and become even more embedded in their daily lives.
“OnStar is now transitioning to be a connected intelligence platform, not just the call center that it’s historically been known as, but a mechanism for interpreting, understanding, and providing predictive, proactive support to its owners,” GM’s VP of global product and chief product officer Sterling Anderson told TechCrunch in an interview ahead of the GM Forward event.
For instance, cameras on the vehicle will be connected to the software to offer live views as well as crash and safety recordings. Users can set up the connected cameras to turn on automatically if the vehicle senses an impending event — such as an aggressive horn honk — then capture the event and upload it to the OnStar app. Users will be able to use voice to control certain functions on the vehicle, including climate, and ask questions about any specific vehicle feature.
The launch coincides with efforts throughout the auto industry to stay apace of Chinese automakers with technology that is central to the vehicle — and no longer a slapped-on gimmick or feature. But that has required GM to change its approach to software development, adopt AI tools, and even design a new electrical and centralized compute vehicle architecture.
The announcement also comes after GM has been criticized and even fined for sharing data with third parties. Earlier this year, the Federal Trade Commission finalized an order that bans General Motors and its OnStar telematics service from sharing certain consumer data with consumer reporting agencies. The finalized order also requires the automaker to be more transparent with its consumers and obtain their explicit consent on certain data collection.
GM said Wednesday that customers will have the ability to decide what data is shared and that the recordings have time limits and are encrypted. GM said it and OnStar cannot access Connected Camera recordings.
A GM spokesperson later stated that third-party sharing is “feature-specific and consent-based, with information shared only as needed to provide requested functionality.” Customers can manage permissions and withdraw consent; however, those who choose not to share certain data may have limited access to related features, while other OnStar services would continue, according to GM.
This article was updated to include comments from a GM spokesperson.

articles.title: Meta says it would’ve made over $22 billion if it didn’t have to pay a child safety settlement
articles.text:
Meta had to shell out $9.89 billion to pay for a chunk of the child safety settlement it reached with US attorneys general. That’s according to the company’s third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday, which says Meta’s income from operations would have been $22.89 billion without the settlement.
Meta says it would’ve made over $22 billion if it didn’t have to pay a child safety settlement
Meta’s third-quarter earnings report shows it spent $9.89 billion paying for its settlement with US attorney generals.
In August, Meta agreed to pay $17.1 billion to settle a massive nationwide lawsuit that claimed the company harmed children by making its social media platforms “addictive” by design. It will also only pay $5.3 billion of this amount if YouTube and TikTok implement stricter settings and safeguards for kids, which Meta also agreed to as part of the settlement.
Meta’s total costs and expenses amounted to $51.61 billion, including the amount it agreed to pay as part of the settlement. The company may have even bigger litigation costs in its future, as a New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over the Cambridge Analytica scandal on Wednesday.
Even with the fees associated with its legal battles, Meta reported earning $64.60 billion in revenue, marking a 26 percent increase from the same time last year. “We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone,” Meta CEO Zuckerberg says in the press release. “Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we’re seeing velocity across the board.”

articles.title: Harvey adds Australian startup Mary's case-fact tools to its legal AI
articles.text:
Sydney-based Mary Technology has connected its litigation tool to Harvey, the $15.6B legal AI company. Lawyers drafting in Harvey can now draw on the facts, evidence and reviews their team has built up in Mary, including conflicting accounts. Workflow firm Autologyx also joined Harvey’s connector library.
Mary Technology, a Sydney-based legal AI startup, has connected its litigation tool to Harvey, the legal AI company valued at $15.6B, Legal IT Insider reported on Wednesday.
Mary reads a case’s documents and builds a record of the people, dates, events and evidence involved. Lawyers then check and confirm those facts. The new link lets lawyers using Harvey draw on that checked record while they research and draft, rather than starting from scratch.
The record keeps track of where evidence conflicts, where there are gaps and which documents back up a claim, Mary said. It also shows which documents were used and which were left out.
“The value of AI in litigation depends on the quality of the factual record it works from,” said Daniel Lord-Doyle, Mary’s co-founder.
Trial lawyers are already leaning on AI. Mark Lanier, who won a $6M verdict against Meta and Google in June, said AI tools that reviewed daily trial transcripts cut his workload by about two-thirds.
When new documents change the picture, Mary suggests updates, which lawyers must approve. Mary says firms keep control of who can access the data, and that client files are not used to train AI models.
The link runs through Harvey’s Connector Library, which lets law firms plug Harvey into the tools they already use. Workflow software firm Autologyx also joined on Wednesday. Mary raised $7M in seed funding earlier this year to expand in the US, according to SmartCompany.
Harvey has been growing fast. It raised $550M in September, has more than 3,000 customers and released its own legal AI model in August. It faces rivals such as Sweden’s Legora, and AI labs that are building their own legal tools.
