articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 21/10: Thế giới ở mức cao, trong nước chiều mai điều chỉnh
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Giá dầu quốc tế trong phiên giao dịch 20/10 được điều chỉnh giảm nhưng vẫn duy trì ở mức cao.
Chốt phiên giao dịch 20/10, theo Reuters, giá dầu Brent giảm 0,69%, xuống 108,8 USD/thùng. Trong khi giá dầu WTI hạ 0,72%, về mức 97,82 USD/thùng.
Đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay (21/10), giá dầu WTI đảo chiều đi lên.
Theo dữ liệu từ Oilprice, vào lúc 6h16' ngày 21/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent vẫn được niêm yết ở mức 108,8 USD/thùng. Còn giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh lên mức 98,13 USD/thùng, tăng 0,32% so với phiên liền trước.
Giá dầu thế giới đi xuống trong phiên 20/10 sau thông tin Mỹ và Iran được cho là đã đạt thỏa thuận nhằm chấm dứt chiến tranh, giúp giảm bớt những lo ngại về nguồn cung năng lượng toàn cầu.
Hãng tin Nournews của Iran cho hay, Tổng thống Iran Masoud Pezeshkian đã thảo luận về vai trò trung gian hòa giải và tình hình khu vực trong cuộc gặp với người đứng đầu quân đội Pakistan, Thống chế Asim Munir tại Tehran, vào ngày 20/10.
Những nỗ lực làm trung gian hòa giải của Pakistan từng giúp Mỹ và Iran đạt được thỏa thuận hòa bình tạm thời được ký kết vào tháng 6 vừa qua. Song thỏa thuận này nhanh chóng bị đổ vỡ khi các cuộc giao tranh mới giữa Iran và Mỹ bùng phát chỉ vài tuần sau đó.
Tuy vậy, diễn biến giảm trong phiên giao dịch 20/10 chưa đủ để khẳng định rủi ro nguồn cung đã được giải quyết hoặc thị trường đã hình thành xu hướng giảm bền vững.
Bên cạnh đó, hoạt động vận chuyển dầu, dữ liệu tồn kho dầu của Mỹ và những thông tin mới về nguồn cung toàn cầu cũng có thể tác động đáng kể lên giá dầu.
Theo một báo cáo mới đây của Công ty phân tích dữ liệu Kpler, ít nhất 18 tàu đã bị tấn công trong vòng hai tuần qua, điều này khiến phí bảo hiểm rủi ro vẫn được duy trì.
Trong khi đó, lực lượng Houthi tiếp tục tấn công các cơ sở hạ tầng của Saudi Arabia và xuất hiện thêm nhiều thông tin cho biết tàu thuyền tại vùng Vịnh bị tấn công.
Vào ngày 20/10, một cuộc tấn công của lực lượng Houthi vào một trại huấn luyện của lực lượng an ninh chính phủ ở tỉnh Shabwa của Yemen đã khiến 58 người thiệt mạng và hơn 200 người bị thương.
Các cuộc tấn công mới làm gia tăng lo ngại về sự ổn định khu vực, đồng thời cho thấy những rủi ro đối với nguồn cung năng lượng từ Trung Đông vẫn chưa được giải quyết.
Theo các nhà phân tích, giá dầu có thể tiếp tục biến động mạnh trong những ngày tới khi nhà đầu tư theo dõi diễn biến xung đột tại Trung Đông, tiến triển ngoại giao và tình hình nguồn cung dầu.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Theo kế hoạch, liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính sẽ tiến hành điều chỉnh giá xăng dầu trong nước vào chiều mai (22/10).
Giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (21/10) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo kỳ điều hành ngày 15/10, giá xăng E5RON92 hạ 732 đồng/lít, giá bán lẻ không cao hơn 26.971 đồng/lít.
Tương tự, giá xăng E10RON95-III được điều chỉnh giảm tới 1.225 đồng/lít, xuống mức 27.029 đồng/lít.
Trong khi giá dầu diesel 0.05S được điều chỉnh giảm nhẹ 22 đồng/lít, xuống mức giá không cao hơn 29.106 đồng/lít.
Trái lại, giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S tăng 1.043 đồng/kg, lên tối đa 22.135 đồng/kg.
Trong chiều 15/10, Tập đoàn Xăng dầu Việt Nam (Petrolimex) tiến hành giảm thêm 300 đồng/lít hoặc kg đối với các mặt hàng xăng dầu so với mức giá bán tối đa được công bố trong kỳ điều hành 15/10.
Tổng công ty Dầu Việt Nam (PVOIL) cũng giảm 350 đồng/lít đối với hai loại xăng và dầu diesel từ 0h ngày 16/10.
Dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương cho hay, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam hiện ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp với diễn biến thị trường và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: PHP: The three letters that shut down sites all over the internet today
articles.text:
Two bugs found with AI are behind major issues today for 4chan, DeviantArt, Wikipedia, and the blog where the bar around the corner posts pictures of people’s dogs. The “critical vulnerabilities” were discovered in the PHP programming language, which underpins much of the internet, including any site built on WordPress. But it’s far bigger than that. Some Dutch and Finnish government agencies took their sites down as a precaution. The NSA Cybersecurity account on X recommended that organizations take their systems offline if “an immediate update is not feasible,” as did the UK’s National Cyber Security Center. Even Pokémon Home and Pokémon Champions were taken offline, Kotaku reports.
PHP: The three letters that shut down sites all over the internet today
OpenAI is taking credit for finding the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, but now someone has to apply all these patches,
The vulnerability isn’t exactly new. It’s been present in PHP for roughly 20 years, but exploiting it “required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” according to security firm Wiz. However, powerful AI models have made it much easier to turn that kind of obscure bug into dangerous vulnerabilities.
As a casual internet user, you might be wondering what exactly the barrage of jargon like “RCE via OOM corruption” means, how concerned you should be, and how exactly a vulnerability this severe flew under the radar for so long.
What is PHP?
W3Techs, a survey service, says that the PHP programming language is used by “69.3 percent of all the websites whose server-side programming language we know,” including popular sites like Wikipedia and WordPress. The internet security site VirusTotal says its scanner currently registers about 3.8 million sites running PHP with at least one port open.
What happened?
According to OpenAI, an AI security group called Calif identified a “critical” PHP flaw using GPT-5.6 Sol, and Google-owned Wiz independently discovered and reported the vulnerabilities using AI. The PHP Foundation says that an exploit for one of the vulnerabilities “was theorized” in 2024, but “no concrete vectors were found and other concrete issues with clear impact overshadowed these concerns.”
Now the PHP Group says hackers could use the two vulnerabilities for “unauthenticated remote code execution,” like running their own code, changing content, and accessing a site’s stored data without needing an administrator login or password.
RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.
RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.
How serious is it?
Very. The PHP Group says that basically any site running PHP is at risk. OpenAI, which was involved in the vulnerability research, said: “We consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.” And Wiz said it’s “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered … in software history.”
Last night, the CTO of Cloudflare said that it was “seeing early attacks emerging.”
It’s hard to understate just how bad this could get. The vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to take full control of a server. That includes gaining access to passwords, API keys, cryptographic certificates, and databases of sensitive information. They could also execute code on those servers, turning them into vectors to attack other vulnerable servers. And, thanks to AI, it’s relatively trivial for a determined hacker to exploit these flaws now that they have been revealed.
What can I do?
As a user, not much. The vulnerability affects servers running PHP and doesn’t necessarily target users directly, but it could use compromised sites to spread malware and steal other valuable data. If you’re feeling extra cautious, check the social accounts of sites and services you frequently use to see if they’ve posted any updates before visiting.
If you have a website, even a simple blog, it’s time to check what version of PHP your site uses, if any. If you’re using a service like Squarespace or Wix, you’re in the clear, as those don’t support PHP.
Customers of Hostinger, GoDaddy, Bluehost, or other web hosting services should be more cautious. GoDaddy says that any site using PHP should assume it is affected and update to the fixed release as soon as possible. It also says that sites running PHP 8.1 or older should upgrade to a newer version, as they’re no longer supported and there will not be an official fix coming.
Those on a managed hosting service should check with their provider to see when they should expect the fix to be deployed. If you sell products or services or have any sensitive data on your servers at all, it’s best to disable your site until your host patches their version of PHP.

articles.title: German court restricts Google aerial imagery over privacy
articles.text:
A German court has told Google it cannot keep showing people’s homes from above without their permission. The Frankfurt Regional Court ruled on Tuesday that the aerial and satellite views on Google Earth and Google Maps break Germany’s strict privacy laws. It went further, and called the practice “spying”.
A man in Frankfurt brought the case. German courts and media have withheld his name under the country’s privacy rules, as Deutsche Welle reported. He had already forced Google Street View and Apple Look Around to blur photographs of his family’s home. This time he went after the overhead imagery.
The court agreed with him. It said nobody should have to accept Google publishing aerial images of their property worldwide without consent, at least where those areas sit hidden from public view.
“The plaintiff’s personal space extends across the whole of the home’s parcel. The only data to be gleaned here are personal, giving clues to private lifestyle, such as the size and design of the property. Beyond this, potential weak points in the property’s security perimeter are also laid bare,” the court said.
The judges gave two reasons. One was the invasion of privacy. The other was safety. The overhead views, they said, could help burglars find weak spots. The court also ruled that Google must warn property owners before it photographs an area.
Google will appeal
Google rejected the finding and said it would appeal. The company “strongly” disagreed with the ruling, it told Courthouse News. It argued that Google Earth and Maps are a public service, not surveillance.
“The views provided in Google Earth and Google Maps are used for a wide range of purposes, such as urban planning, environmental research and disaster relief, making them a highly valuable service for millions of people,” a Google spokesperson said.
The spokesperson added that the pictures are a mosaic of satellite and aerial shots from several providers, and that similar views appear in other public services. The court did not accept it. It rejected Google’s claim that it was democratising knowledge, and said freedom of information gives it no right to invade private spaces.
Germany’s long fight with the cameras
The ruling lands in a country with little patience for Silicon Valley’s cameras. Germany’s pushback on Google Street View more than a decade ago saw homes blurred, and some camera cars attacked. The decision adds to pressure on Google Earth and its imagery.
It also fits a run of European and US courts reining in big tech. A Frankfurt court recently ruled against Meta over scam ads, and Texas has sued Netflix for alleged spying and addictive design. For now, Google aerial imagery stays online while the company appeals, and an appeals court may yet overturn it.

articles.title: PHP Armageddon: OpenAI, Google's Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation.
PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites. It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress.
The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app.
Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.
So how did two such ubiquitous, decades-old flaws that affect nearly every website on the internet suddenly come to light? AI, naturally, particularly via OpenAI and Google’s Wiz.
Security testing company Calif was engaged in OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative to find flaws in open source software. Using GPT‑5.6 Sol, it found one of the flaws, OpenAI disclosed in a blog post. Separately, the Wiz team also used AI, namely its Wiz Atlas security AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol to find multiple vulnerabilities in PHP.
Both OpenAI and Wiz followed responsible security research practices and worked with PHP on patches before publicly disclosing the flaws. Then they all worked together to flesh out what they found, and test the patches, drawing in a host of others to help.
Wiz thanked Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare, Fastly, Imperva, Microsoft, and Vercel. (While WordPress sites use PHP, WordPress has issued a statement saying that the flaw isn’t WordPress specific, and sites running its CMS must patch their servers and work with their web-hosting companies to ensure their sites are protected.)
OpenAI says that these flaws were found by researchers before hackers discovered them. So there were no reports of exploits in the wild. This is also in part because, before AI, these flaws were too hard for hackers to exploit. “With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts,” Wiz warned in its blog about the flaws.
In other words, this is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented because of AI, but is also a high risk only because of AI.
Now that the issue has been disclosed, hackers are fully in the know. The race is on for the internet to patch tens millions of websites before hackers can attack the unpatched ones. Hence the NSA’s guidance that if you can’t patch your PHP website right away, you’re better off pulling it offline until you can.

articles.title: Ngân hàng giảm lãi suất: Cần giảm thực chất, không “lãi suất ngầm”
articles.text:
“Lãi suất huy động giảm 0,5 điểm phần trăm, lãi vay có thể giảm 2 điểm phần trăm?
Các ngân hàng đang đồng loạt giảm lãi suất huy động và triển khai các chương trình giảm lãi suất cho vay. Tại cuộc họp ngày 19/10 giữa NHNN với lãnh đạo các NHTM, TS. Đào Minh Tú – Phó Chủ tịch kiêm Tổng Thư ký Hiệp hội Ngân hàng Việt Nam thừa nhận, lãi suất cho vay tại các ngân hàng đang cao so với khả năng tạo ra lợi nhuận của doanh nghiệp.
Tuy nhiên, theo ông Tú, lãi suất cao xuất phát từ các yếu tố khách quan. Bản thân các ngân hàng cũng không mong muốn điều này vì có thể ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng tín dụng.
Để giảm lãi suất cho vay, bên cạnh nỗ lực cắt giảm chi phí hoạt động của ngân hàng, điều kiện tiên quyết là lãi suất đầu vào phải thực sự giảm. Đây cũng là lý do ông Lê Ngọc Lâm – Chủ tịch HĐQT BIDV - kêu gọi các ngân hàng giảm thực chất lãi suất huy động khoảng 0,5 điểm phần trăm, nhằm kéo giảm mặt bằng lãi suất cho vay.
Trao đổi với VietNamNet, PGS.TS Nguyễn Văn Phương, Trường Đại học Kinh tế, Đại học Quốc gia Hà Nội, cho rằng giảm lãi suất là chủ trương cần thiết nhằm giảm chi phí tài chính, hỗ trợ sản xuất và ngăn cạnh tranh huy động thiếu lành mạnh giữa các ngân hàng.
Chủ trương này có cơ sở thuận lợi hơn khi áp lực cân đối vốn đã giảm. Tính đến cuối tuần qua, huy động vốn tăng 11,22%, còn tín dụng tăng 11,44%. Như vậy, tốc độ tăng huy động vốn và tín dụng đã khá sát nhau, dù chưa đủ cơ sở để kết luận mọi ngân hàng đều có nguồn vốn dồi dào.
Tuy nhiên, PGS.TS Nguyễn Văn Phương cho rằng, điều quan trọng là giảm lãi suất phải thực chất. Doanh nghiệp giảm được chi phí vốn, được hưởng ưu đãi đủ lâu và không phải bù lại bằng phí hoặc điều kiện phụ.
“Một chương trình công bố rất lớn nhưng giải ngân ít, hoặc chỉ ưu đãi vài tháng đầu, chưa thể xem là thành công”, ông Phương nói.
Theo ông Phương, nguồn vốn ổn định với chi phí hợp lý là điều kiện cần để giảm lãi suất. Để duy trì mức giảm bền vững, ngân hàng còn phải kiểm soát tốt rủi ro và tiết kiệm chi phí vận hành.
“Cần nhìn thẳng vào độ chênh giữa hai mức giảm. Hạ lãi suất huy động mới 0,5 điểm phần trăm không tự động tạo đủ dư địa hạ lãi vay 1,5–2 điểm phần trăm. Tiền gửi đã huy động trước đó vẫn phải trả theo hợp đồng; chi phí vốn bình quân chỉ giảm dần khi nguồn vốn cũ đáo hạn. Phần giảm lãi vay còn lại phải đến từ lợi nhuận ngân hàng, giảm chi phí hoặc giảm rủi ro”.
Ông Phương dẫn chứng, nếu một ngân hàng giảm lãi suất cho vay 1,5 điểm phần trăm đối với 10.000 tỷ đồng dư nợ và duy trì đủ một năm, thu nhập lãi sẽ giảm khoảng 150 tỷ đồng, chưa tính phần chi phí huy động tiết kiệm được. Ví dụ này cho thấy phải xác định rõ quy mô dư nợ được giảm, thời gian áp dụng và nguồn bù đắp, không chỉ cam kết một tỷ lệ.
“Kế hoạch lợi nhuận của ngân hàng là mục tiêu quản trị, không nên được xem là mục tiêu bất di bất dịch để từ chối chia sẻ khó khăn với người vay. Tuy nhiên, cũng không thể buộc ngân hàng giảm thu nhập đến mức suy giảm khả năng trích lập dự phòng và bổ sung vốn. Hội đồng quản trị cần điều chỉnh kỳ vọng lợi nhuận khi cần thiết, đồng thời bảo vệ năng lực tài chính dài hạn”, ông Phương nói.
Về phía cơ quan quản lý, cần giảm rủi ro hoạt động cho vay bằng cách tháo gỡ pháp lý dự án, xử lý công nợ, nâng chất lượng dữ liệu doanh nghiệp và cải thiện bảo lãnh tín dụng. Khi người vay có dòng tiền tốt hơn, ngân hàng mới có thể giảm phần bù rủi ro mà không hạ chuẩn tín dụng.
Làm sao để không còn việc mặc cả lãi suất khi gửi tiền?
Có một thực tế sau một số đợt giảm lãi suất huy động gần đây, các ngân hàng nhanh chóng quay lại cuộc đua tăng lãi suất. Thậm chí, có ngân hàng áp dụng mức lãi suất thực tế cao hơn biểu niêm yết và chỉ thông báo riêng cho khách hàng.
Thực tế này cho thấy ngân hàng không thể duy trì lãi suất thấp chỉ bằng cam kết nếu nhu cầu vốn và nguồn huy động không tương thích. Theo ông Phương, xác định sức ép nằm ở thanh khoản ngắn hạn, nguồn vốn dài hạn hay tốc độ mở rộng tín dụng.
“NHNN cần theo dõi từng nhóm ngân hàng, thay vì chỉ nhìn số bình quân. Ngân hàng thiếu thanh khoản tạm thời cần phải có công cụ hỗ trợ thanh khoản phù hợp. Ngân hàng không thể liên tục tăng lãi suất tiền gửi để duy trì tốc độ mở rộng quy mô tài sản”, PGS.TS Nguyễn Văn Phương nói.
Do đó, cam kết giảm lãi suất của ngân hàng phải đi kèm kế hoạch nguồn vốn theo tháng, quý và các kịch bản ứng phó khi tiền gửi dịch chuyển.
“Các ngân hàng phát triển nguồn tiền gửi ổn định, quản trị kỳ hạn và giữ khách hàng bằng chất lượng dịch vụ có ý nghĩa hơn một đợt giảm mang tính truyền thông”, PGS.TS Nguyễn Văn Phương nói.
Bên cạnh đó, cơ quan quản lý cũng cần đánh giá kết quả định kỳ để theo dõi chi phí huy động có thực sự giảm hay không, tiền gửi có bị rút hoặc chuyển kỳ hạn không, lãi vay thực trả giảm bao nhiêu. Nếu xuất hiện áp lực tỷ giá hoặc lạm phát mới, chính sách phải được giải thích và điều chỉnh minh bạch. Mục tiêu không phải cấm tăng lãi suất trong mọi hoàn cảnh, mà là tránh cuộc đua thiếu lành mạnh, nhưng vẫn cho phép giá vốn phản ánh những thay đổi có thật của thị trường.
Trước tình trạng lãi suất thực tế cao hơn so với lãi suất niêm yết, PGS.TS Nguyễn Văn Phương cho rằng điều này sẽ tạo hệ luỵ lớn là sai lệch thông tin. Cơ quan quản lý cho rằng chi phí huy động đã giảm, nhưng thực tế ngân hàng vẫn “mua” vốn đắt. Người gửi tiền không biết mức lãi suất mình có thể được hưởng; ngân hàng công khai minh bạch chịu bất lợi trong cạnh tranh; nhân viên chịu áp lực chi ngoài và đối mặt với rủi ro tranh chấp. Cuối cùng, những chi phí không được công khai này có thể được chuyển sang người vay, 'lãi suất ngầm'.
Giải pháp là chuẩn hóa công bố tổng lợi ích huy động quy đổi theo năm, gồm lãi hợp đồng và những ưu đãi có giá trị xác định được. Ngân hàng phải báo cáo chi phí thực tế theo sản phẩm, kỳ hạn, nhóm khách hàng; cơ quan thanh tra đối chiếu với sổ kế toán, ngân sách khuyến mại và khoản chi qua đơn vị liên quan”.
PGS.TS Nguyễn Văn Phương nhấn mạnh, muốn chấm dứt “lãi suất ngầm”, phải bảo đảm lãi suất công khai phản ánh đúng lợi ích người gửi tiền được hưởng và các ngân hàng cạnh tranh công bằng. Thành công của đợt giảm lãi suất này không nằm ở số ngân hàng điều chỉnh lãi suất trên bảng niêm yết, mà ở chi phí vốn thực sự giảm, người vay tiếp cận thuận lợi hơn và hệ thống vẫn an toàn.

articles.title: eBay to cut 9% of its staff, its second round of layoffs this year
articles.text:
eBay will cut about 9% of its workforce, around 1,000 jobs, according to an internal memo from CEO Jamie Iannone first reported by Reuters. It follows 800 job cuts in February. eBay says it wants to focus on its fastest-growing areas. It reports results on 28 October.
eBay will cut about 9% of its workforce, its second round of job cuts this year, according to an internal memo from chief executive Jamie Iannone. Reuters first reported the cuts on Wednesday.
Around 1,000 jobs will go, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Affected staff will be told in the coming days, Reuters said.
In the memo, Iannone said “our strategy is working,” but that the next phase “requires us to make thoughtful choices about where we focus and invest.” eBay wants to simplify how it runs and move money to its fastest-growing areas, Reuters said.
The company cut about 800 jobs, or 6% of its staff, in February. It also made cuts in early 2023 and early 2024.
The layoffs come five months after eBay rejected a $56B takeover bid from GameStop, calling it “neither credible nor attractive.” GameStop chief executive Ryan Cohen had promised to find $2B in cost savings within a year of buying eBay. He even gave up a huge pay package to pursue the deal.
Iannone, who has run eBay since 2020, has focused on categories such as luxury goods, refurbished items and collectibles. Earlier this year, eBay bought secondhand fashion app Depop to compete with Vinted, which is expanding in the US.
eBay’s shares rose about 1.2% on Wednesday morning in New York. The company reports quarterly results on 28 October.

articles.title: Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues
articles.text:
As the smoke clears from its outrageous Roadster demo, Tesla reported Q3 earnings on Wednesday — and the cold reality is that revenue has flatlined.
Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues
Flat revenue and a 4 percent profit drop show that no amount of rocket thrusters can disguise Tesla’s troubles.
Tesla said it earned $1.7 billion in net income on $28.0 billion in revenue in the quarter that ended in September 2026. Revenues were flat, while profits dropped 4 percent compared to the third quarter of 2025, when the company earned $1.4 billion in net income on $28.1 billion in revenue. Tesla’s revenue came in above Wall Street expectations of $27.9 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Tesla’s own company-compiled expectations predicted Q3 revenues of $28.3 billion.
The earnings come on the heels of a disappointing Q3 sales report, in which Tesla reported a 2.1 percent drop in customer deliveries compared to the blockbuster third quarter of 2025. (For a direct-to-consumer company like Tesla, deliveries are a proxy for sales.) The drop in sales was widely expected thanks to the expiration of the $7,500 federal tax credit for electric vehicles on September 30, 2025. Elon Musk himself said that the company was in for “a few rough quarters” thanks to the expiring incentive and other macroeconomic factors.
Tesla reported automotive revenues of $20.5 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year — a sign that the company’s car business is floundering after the elimination of the tax credit. But there were troubling signs for Tesla’s other businesses too; the company reported $2.9 billion in energy generation and storage revenue, a staggering 16 percent drop year over year. “Services and other revenue,” such as money the company takes in from EV charging, maintenance, parts, and insurance, was up 33 percent to $4.6 billion – a rare bright spot in an otherwise dour earnings report.
Tesla’s capital spending — also known as capex — soared 110 percent year over year to $4.7 billion this quarter, as the company continue to pour money into AI, autonomous vehicles, and robotics. Musk has said to expect “a massive capex year” of at least $25 billion in capital spending as Tesla continues to transition into an AI and robotics company. But the company only spent $13 billion in the first three quarters of the year, suggesting that Tesla may fall short of that $25 billion target.
Operating expenses — the day to day costs of running Tesla’s business — was up 39 percent year over year to $4.8 billion, while its income from operations — the profit Tesla generates from those day-to-day dealings — was down 56 percent year over year to just $718 million.
On the brighter side, Tesla reported a free cash flow of $1.5 billion, after dipping into negative territory last year. Still, that figure represents a 62 percent drop year over year, a sign that Tesla’s operating revenues were still struggling to cover its capital expenditures.
The possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX merger gained new momentum after Musk’s revelation this week that the two companies had formed special committees to discuss the possibility. Musk said a merger would be a “good idea,” even though he claimed he wouldn’t be involved in the process.
Beyond merger talks, this past quarter also saw the highly anticipated re-reveal of the next-generation Tesla Roadster, nine years after it was initially announced. The demo in Waco, Texas, featured a redesigned two-seat prototype flying and flipping through the air using cold-gas thrusters provided by SpaceX. While the event generated its own cottage industry of online reactions, it did little to assuage skeptics that the vehicle would actually go into production in 2028, as promised.

articles.title: Blacksmith hits unicorn valuation after Sequoia leads Series C | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Blacksmith, a platform that helps companies more efficiently build and test software, including code written by AI, announced Wednesday a $66 million Series C funding round led by Sequoia that values the company at $1 billion.
In announcing the round, Blacksmith co-founder and CEO Aditya Jayaprakash said the company was founded to make continuous integration (CI) — the process of building, testing, merging, and validating code changes — “less painful.” In a blog post, he said that “most companies are struggling to keep up with the volume of CI they need to run,” especially in an era where so much code is written by AI.
“As agents write more of the world’s software, the question that matters is whether it can be trusted,” he added.
The company also announced that its annual recurring revenue has grown 17x and that it has run over 90 million CI jobs, or individual automated code checks. Customers include Mercury and Granola.
The Series C comes just two months after its $45 million Series B, which valued the company at $550 million. A year ago, Blacksmith was valued at $60 million after raising a $10 million Series A. It has raised $125 million to date.

articles.title: Bose acquires Skullcandy to help it reach a wider audience
articles.text:
Bose announced today it has acquired Skullcandy. Although the two companies are competitors in the consumer audio space, Skullcandy recently partnered with its new owner to bring several of Bose’s audio technologies — including its head-tracking spatial audio and excellent active noise cancellation (ANC) — to products like the Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC headphones and Method 360 ANC earbuds.
Bose acquires Skullcandy to help it reach a wider audience
Bose will leverage Skullcandy’s designs and branding to help the company reach new demographics.
Specific details about the deal weren’t shared, but according to a news release, Bose plans to keep Skullcandy a separate brand that will become part of its premium consumer audio business. Skullcandy will remain based in Park City, Utah, where it was founded. The acquisition will help Bose expand the reach of its audio technologies, including its industry-leading noise cancellation, to a wider audience.
“For more than 60 years, Bose has been committed to delivering incredible audio experiences however and wherever people choose to listen. As we work to reach even more people, we’re expanding how we do that, not only through Bose products, but through technology partnerships and a growing portfolio of brands,” Bose CEO Lila Snyder says.
Founded in 2003, Skullcandy hasn’t been around for as long as Bose has, but the company’s distinct product designs and branding that includes “longstanding relationships” with board sports athletes will “present new ways for Bose to meaningfully connect with consumers where it has less presence today,” according to today’s release. Bose’s products are a staple among people who regularly fly and travel for work, but Skullcandy will help the company’s products appeal to consumers who don’t necessarily prioritize the effectiveness of ANC on their headphones.
In 2024, Bose acquired the high-end audio brand McIntosh and its subsidiary Sonus faber, and this year it acquired StreamUnlimited Engineering and FMOD-maker Firelight Technologies. Bose also announced last June it had created an in-house content studio called Bose Studios, as well as its own record label, Bose Records.

articles.title: "A structural failure": the PHP Foundation on a two-year delay
articles.text:
The PHP Foundation has given an unusually frank account of the emergency behind this week’s patches. It said it had found one of the two critical flaws two years ago, in 2024. Then it spent months unable to agree on how to repair it.
The admission came in a blog post from the Foundation on Wednesday. It landed hours after the fix for the two critical PHP flaws known together as PHP2Shell. Both bugs sit in the parts of PHP that almost every request touches: memory management and error handling. That central place made them serious, the Foundation said, and hard to fix without breaking the wider ecosystem.
A core developer first spotted the memory-handling bug in 2024. It surfaced while the team fixed a separate issue from PHP’s first external security audit. Someone theorised a possible exploit at the time. But no one found a concrete way in, and clearer problems took priority.
Then the fix stalled. The security team drew up several competing repairs, the Foundation said. Each carried a cost. One broke backward compatibility. Another added a denial-of-service risk. A third forced changes on thousands of third-party extensions. The small team ran on consensus and feared shipping the wrong choice, so the work stalled and restarted for months.
“We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources,” the Foundation wrote.
Then it leaked
Everything moved faster once the secret slipped. On 20 October at around 15:00 UTC, the two CVE identifiers began circulating on forums and social media. They carried a wrong release time and a wrong severity score of 10.0. The real figure is 9.2. No technical details leaked at that point.
The Foundation brought its announcement forward. It also moved the release up a day, from 22 to 21 October. Distributors were still packaging the fix, it said. Going out at once would have left many users with no easy way to update.
Two more breaks followed. Around 20:00 UTC, Calif, one of the firms that reported the bugs, mistakenly published a video. It showed the firm’s proof of concept working against real targets. Calif deleted it, but copies spread. That sped up the public exploit code that appeared the next day, the Foundation said.
Then a vendor broke the embargo. More than six hours before the release, Chainguard published built images containing the fix. It had been given the patch early, like other distributors, so its users could update at once. But releasing it ahead of time let any attacker study the fix in binary form while everyone else waited.
“This disregarded weeks of work by many parties toward a coordinated disclosure,” the Foundation wrote.
The security team watched the exploit code closely after the leak, it added. It had seen no working exploit by the time of release.
Pay for the plumbing
The post doubled as a plea for money. PHP runs a large share of the web, the Foundation said. That includes government services, online stores and banks. Yet its security work rests on a small group of Foundation-funded developers and a little volunteer help. AI tools now surface bugs faster than ever, for attackers and defenders alike.
The reports keep piling up. The team has published 15 CVEs since the start of July. It worked through more than 100 others that proved invalid or duplicates.
What tools cannot do, the Foundation said, is choose the right fix for a decades-old design decision. Nor can they weigh the compatibility costs. That takes experienced engineers, and it said there are too few of them. It asked the companies, hosting providers and governments that run on PHP to sponsor the work.
Changing how it works
The Foundation has already changed how it operates. It set up an Ecosystem Security Team in May and hired two more engineers over the summer. It is also moving security decisions from consensus to a majority vote. And it has leaned on AI. It scanned PHP earlier this year with Anthropic’s Claude Mythos, and later added OpenAI’s Daybreak to validate reports.
The timing showed how crowded that field has become. Calif began its audit on 30 July, as part of OpenAI’s Patch the Planet programme. Its researcher Ryan A reported the flaw on 11 August. OpenAI reported the same root cause the same day, the Foundation said, independently. It added that it was now confident a flaw stuck on hard trade-offs would reach its leadership far sooner, rather than stalling for months.
We have posted more information about today’s security releases, including the sequence of events that led to the discovery, and what we need from you to continue this critical work.
The PHP Foundation (@ThePHPF) October 21, 2026

articles.title: Waymo starts offering rides at the Las Vegas airport | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Waymo is now shuttling customers to and from the Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas, with pickups and drop-offs happening at dedicated “autonomous vehicle zones” at Terminal 1 and Terminal 3, the company announced Wednesday.
This is the sixth major airport that Waymo is serving. The company already offers rides at Phoenix Sky Harbor, Nashville International, San Antonio International, San Francisco International, and San José International airports.
Waymo only just started offering rides to the public in Las Vegas in September but is already serving a 24-square-mile area in the city. The company said the rides to and from the Las Vegas airport will be limited at first to just a few riders, before opening up to all customers.
Amazon-owned Zoox already offers rides at the Vegas airport, and more robotaxis are coming to Sin City. In August, state regulators approved permits that will allow Tesla and Uber to put thousands of them on the city’s streets in the next year.

articles.title: Intel restarts its stalled US factory push as AI chip demand grows
articles.text:
Intel has started installing equipment at Fab 62, its new chip plant near Phoenix, which is due to open in early 2028. It has also put up the first major roof truss at its long-delayed Ohio site. The progress comes as demand for its data centre processors outpaces supply.
Intel has started installing equipment at Fab 62, its new chip factory near Phoenix, and is moving ahead at its long-delayed Ohio site, Bloomberg reported. Intel manufacturing chief Naga Chandrasekaran shared the update on the company’s website on Wednesday.
Fab 62 sits on Intel’s Ocotillo campus in Arizona, next to Fab 52, which is already running. It is due to start operating in early 2028, Intel said. Filling a plant with tools is the costliest step in getting it ready, as some machines cost hundreds of millions of dollars.
In New Albany, Ohio, workers have installed the first major roof truss for the site’s first factory. Ohio was meant to become the world’s largest chipmaking site, but work stalled. Last year, Intel pushed back its opening to between 2030 and 2031.
Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan, who took over in March 2025, has said projects like Ohio will only go ahead when there is enough work for them. The progress suggests Intel is becoming more confident about demand.
Orders for Intel’s data centre processors, used to run AI services, are growing faster than it can make them. It is also spending $5.7B to make more of its Xeon chips in Ireland. In July, Intel raised its spending plans for this year to more than $20B and said it expects to spend significantly more in 2027.
Intel also wants to make chips for other companies, but it has yet to announce many big customers for that business. Apple was reported in May to be in early talks to use Intel’s factories, and Intel has joined Elon Musk’s Terafab project as a manufacturing partner.
The US government, which holds a stake in Intel, has a lot riding on the plan. In August, Intel also proposed a $15B share sale to raise money. Still, Intel spends far less than rival TSMC, which analysts expect to spend about $60B this year, Bloomberg said.

articles.title: Airbnb bans making guests do dishes and take out the trash
articles.text:
Checking out of your next Airbnb might be less of a hassle now that the company is banning hosts from including time-consuming chores in their house rules. Airbnb’s updated house rules policy, which starts with reservations booked on or after November 20th, says hosts can’t ask guests to “complete tasks that require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner.” According to Airbnb, that includes:
Airbnb bans making guests do dishes and take out the trash
Airbnb’s new rules limit hosts to ‘reasonable’ requests like putting dirty dishes in the sink.
- Dishes: Guests shouldn’t be asked to wash and put away dishes, but you can ask them to put used dishes in the sink.
- Laundry: Guests shouldn’t be asked to remove sheets from the bed or start a load of laundry, but you can ask them to gather used towels.
- Trash: Guests shouldn’t be asked to take garbage off-site, but you can ask them to separate their trash and recycling into designated indoor bins.
- Utilities: Guests shouldn’t be asked to avoid using a listed amenity like air conditioning, but you can ask them to turn it off when they leave.
Airbnb is displaying hosts’ requests more prominently now in a new “rules and requests” section on listings. You might see an “includes cleaning requests” warning if a host leaves chore requests in their listing after the new policy goes into effect. Hosts aren’t allowed to sneak in extra rules in messages to guests or on signs around their property, either.
Some hosts pushed back on the house rules restrictions on Airbnb’s forums, saying they pose health risks and arguing that guests can simply choose not to stay at listings with overly-strict rules. Airbnb says there can be exceptions to the limits on checkout chores, like asking guests to “dispose of trash in an animal-proof container in bear country.”

articles.title: Foursquare co-founder says equity holders saw no returns from the company's acquisition | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Last month, advertising company Infillion acquired location-data platform Foursquare, a once popular social network, at an undisclosed value. Now, in a new blog post, Foursquare co-founder and former CEO Dennis Crowley said that investors didn’t see any returns from the sale.
Crowley referenced a post by an angel investor, inferred that neither preferred nor common stockholders got any value out of the deal, and said he was disappointed by the outcome.
“I was heartbroken by this ending. So many people put so much time and energy and passion and love into building Foursquare — the company, the products, the brand, the culture. If you were part of it (or even close to it), you know exactly what I’m talking about. To our ~1600 former employees over 17 years, I am sorry the Foursquare story ended in such a way that makes it seem like our collective efforts were worth … nothing?” he said in the post.
Crowley said that the company did well after it started focusing on enterprise business and had consecutive years with over $100 million in revenue. In 2019, the company raised capital from a private equity firm and in 2021 brought in the banker who led the raise as CEO. Crowley blamed the final outcome on that transition, saying that the management of the company wasn’t able to preserve or create new value.
Foursquare, which had raised over $411 million in funding according to PitchBook data, eventually shut down its app in 2024.
Several people reacted to Crowley’s post and said that Foursquare was very useful to them in discovering new places in their cities and also gave ideas for new apps. After Foursquare, startups like Zenly and Jagat, along with Instagram and Snapchat, have explored social maps.

articles.title: Inside India newsletter: Asia’s hottest data center market aims to quell concerns over water and power use
articles.text:
Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.
Welcome to the latest edition of "Inside India" — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.
India is touted as one of the hottest markets for data centers, with several U.S. Big Tech companies investing to set up capacity in the country. But of late, some projects have faced public backlash over the use of water and power resources.
Now the Indian government is taking steps to address the situation. Will it work?
Any thoughts on today's newsletter? Share them with the team.
The big story
Several U.S. Big Tech companies that are spending billions to set up digital infrastructure in India are facing growing public anger over resource sharing and environmental concerns, prompting the government to step in and calm tensions.
On Oct. 14, Jitin Prasada, a junior minister for electronics and information technology, announced that India will roll out a policy for data centers, calling the country a "fertile ground for hyperscalers."
The minister reportedly said India wants to avoid a situation where consumers have to pay more for power because they have to compete with data centers for supply.
Globally, data center companies are facing public backlash as communities raise concerns over electricity, water and land use. India is also grappling with similar issues that pose a threat to its ambitions to host the whole world's data.
As per local media reports, Amazon's data center near Mumbai is facing resistance from residents who are worried that the U.S. company's facility would receive priority access to water and electricity during shortages.
Meanwhile, environmental activists have been demanding the cancellation of permissions given to AI data centers in Visakhapatnam, where Google is constructing its $15 billion project.
Amazon told CNBC that it is committed to being a "good and responsible neighbor," and said it is engaging with the community through educational sessions. They denied using water for cooling and added that their data centers "do not draw electricity from the local distribution network that supplies homes, shops and businesses."
The American firm also said it "will be a part of industry consultations with the government to advise on India's data center regulations."
Google did not respond to CNBC's request for comments.
Experts told CNBC that the government plans to roll out a policy directive to pacify local resistance to some projects across the country.
It will also lay down clear approval guidelines that will minimize the risks data center developers face from public pushback and execution challenges, they added.
Policy shift
The proposed policy indicates a shift in direction from "primarily encouraging the data center investment" to now balancing it with infrastructure readiness and sustainability aspects, Jaspreet Singh, partner at Grant Thornton Bharat, told CNBC.
Last week, Niti Aayog, an Indian government think tank, shared a framework for local governments to evaluate data center projects for sustainability and to provide suitable locations, based on grid readiness and water supply availability.
It underscored the need to establish guidelines "before constraints emerge," adding that data centers should get faster approvals only in cases where resource readiness, local safeguards and public value are proven.
Experts who are part of consultations expect the new policy to lay down clear and consistent rules, which will also help the industry overcome challenges around land acquisition and simplify a fragmented approval process.
"India does not have a dedicated national policy for data centers, and it is high time that this gap was addressed," Shobhit Agarwal, chief executive of real estate consultancy ANAROCK Capital, told CNBC.
He explained that projects are currently approved under existing environmental and building rules, and every state has its own "variations and incentives."
While the Indian government has been enthusiastic in welcoming the hyperscalers to invest in data centers in India, even giving them 20-year tax sops, regional governments are the final decision-makers when it comes to providing land, water and power resources.
Nikhil Narendran, a partner for technology at law firm Trilegal, who works with U.S. Big Tech companies, said local governments are proposing data center projects in locations that are already facing constraints in terms of electricity, water and other infrastructure.
He added that state governments need to be encouraged to identify locations where reliable electricity, substantial cooling infrastructure, water availability and high-quality connectivity are available, "rather than simply competing to announce large investments."
Need to know
U.S. eyes refining muscle of Indian billionaire Ambani's Reliance as Rubio visits Jamnagar plant
The U.S. is looking to "work together more closely" with Reliance Industries for refining energy from the "Western Hemisphere," U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in an interview with India's Network 18. 
India's finance minister says market liquidity makes it easier for investors to exit
The high degree of liquidity in India's equity market has provided easier exits to foreign portfolio investors, according to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.
BlackRock, GIC among investors chasing Indian telecom major Jio's IPO as anchor bids top $26 billion
India's Jio Platforms has seen the anchor investor quota for its initial public offering oversubscribed more than 30 times, according to a source familiar with the matter, drawing bids from top asset managers including BlackRock, Capital Group and GIC.
India's rupee forecast to weaken toward 100-per-dollar level even as RBI pushes back
The Reserve Bank of India's measures to slow currency depreciation will provide short-term relief, but strategists said the rupee is expected to weaken toward the end of the year and mid-2027, and a 100 rupee-per-dollar mark could not be ruled out.
Coming up
Oct. 23: HSBC composite Flash PMI for October
Oct. 28: India Industrial output for September

articles.title: AI and jobs: The hot new topic for central bankers
articles.text:
BEIJING — Artificial intelligence is breaking into the realm of central bankers.
High-level gatherings this month in Asia, including the International Monetary Fund-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok last week and the Bund Summit this week in Shanghai, reflected growing scrutiny on the tech, especially as competition for capital sends many government bond yields to multi-decade highs.
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said in Bangkok that AI was a positive economic "shock" that could "fundamentally" change monetary policy. He noted plans for a hearing on productivity and jobs in the Bay Area on Nov. 16 and has a task force focusing on AI.
Three days later in Beijing, People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng spent the last portion of a Financial Street Forum keynote on AI, according to an official transcript. He said the central bank would evaluate the impact of the technology, improve financial support for the AI industry and promote its application in finance.
"The impact of AI on the global economy, on employment, on China, on everything" was at the top of the agenda at the central-banker-heavy Bund Summit, Guo Kai, president of the CF40 Institute think tank, told CNBC on the sidelines of the conference Tuesday.
AI and wages
"AI may be already having an effect on wage demands because workers are concerned" about their jobs, said Donald Kohn, former vice chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. "We have a situation now where the economy is at full employment, demand is pretty strong, and wages, if anything, have continued to come down in the U.S. in nominal terms and in real terms," he told CNBC on the sidelines of the Bund Summit.
During upcoming meetings of central bankers and financial regulators at the Bank for International Settlements in Basel, Switzerland, Kohn expects central bankers will discuss AI's impact on jobs.
Managing spillover
Many Asian economies from Indonesia to China are vulnerable to any downturn in AI demand due to their significant role in the underlying supply chain, Sonali Jain-Chandra, deputy director of the IMF's Asia Pacific Department, said Tuesday during a fund roundtable.
"This is a very important risk for policymakers to pay attention to," she said. "And this is why we also say that now is the time to build buffers, fiscal external buffers to make sure that if there is a downturn ... that policymakers have space to be able to respond."
At the IMF-World Bank meetings and the Bund Summit, there's been "surprise" at how resilient the world economy is, despite debate about how vulnerable it is to a slowdown in AI spend or profitability in the U.S., Adam Posen, president of the Peterson Institute for International Economics, said Tuesday on CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia."
He said even if there's a stock "market correction in the megascalers ... in the near term, we can probably have something more like 1987 or 2000, where the profits just rotate to adjacent industries and the real economy isn't affected much."

articles.title: Stock futures fall as investors digest earnings from Meta and Tesla: Live updates
articles.text:
U.S. equity futures slid late Wednesday after investors digested third-quarter earnings from big tech names including Meta Platforms and Tesla.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures ticked down 0.3%, or 170 points. S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%, and Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 0.7%.
In Asia, markets opened mixed Thursday. South Korea's Kospi fell 0.67%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.19%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was flat.
Shares of Meta gained 2% in extended trading. The Facebook and Instagram parent delivered a revenue beat along with strong guidance for the current quarter. Meanwhile, Tesla reported a better-than-expected top and bottom line for its third-quarter results. Shares of the electric vehicle maker were last off 3%.
"The quarter showed the AI investment paying off in the core," said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives in his post Meta earnings reaction note. Spend is "better controlled than feared," Ives added as Meta narrowed the range for its full-year data center-related capital expenditures.
The action follows a positive day on Wall Street, with the S&P 500 notching a three-day win streak, while the Dow jumped 360 points. The Nasdaq Composite closed 1% higher, catching a tailwind from SpaceX and Tesla.
Blowout quarterly results from SpaceX fueled investors' excitement for the artificial intelligence trade, sending shares of Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices higher. Also fanning the flames was news from Super Micro Computer, which lifted its fiscal first-quarter revenue outlook.
There was also some focus on Nvidia's U.S. supply chain agreements Wednesday. The chip giant announced plans to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform.
Looking ahead to Thursday, there are a host of companies on deck to report results including Procter & Gamble, Lockheed Martin, Valero Energy and Honeywell.
Investors will also be paying attention to the economic calendar with weekly initial jobless claims set to release Thursday morning.

articles.title: Anthropic announces preview of Claude Duet, a personal AI agent to take on Muse, Dots
articles.text:
Anthropic on Wednesday announced a preview of Claude Duet, an artificial intelligence agent that will likely challenge OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse offerings.
Claude Duet is designed for small businesses and professionals, Anthropic said. It can send users daily briefs, keep tabs on connected apps, and carry out a range of tasks like building dashboards, scheduling meetings and creating financial forecasts.
"It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working even when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf," Anthropic said in a blog post.
The debut comes as competing products from Meta and OpenAI have started to show real traction with users. Meta's Muse, which the company touts as a "personal AI agent," launched last month and rocketed to the top of Apple's App Store. OpenAI introduced dots, its "always-on agents," during its annual developer conference weeks later.
Meta has primarily marketed its agent toward consumers, while OpenAI's product straddles both the enterprise and consumer markets. Anthropic said Wednesday that since Claude Duet is primarily designed for the workplace, personal errands, like booking tickets, are not "quite as strong."
Anthropic and OpenAI have long been fierce rivals, and they've spent much of the last year releasing competing models and jockeying for enterprise market share. Meta, meanwhile, has been revamping its AI strategy and pouring billions of dollars into new efforts to compete at the frontier. With the rise of personal agents, Meta is hoping to capitalize on the momentum.
Meta reported third-quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, and CEO Mark Zuckerberg told analysts that more 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada "have set up Muse personal agents" over the past month and a half. The initial success of the Muse helped Meta end September with its best month on Wall Street since 2022.
Anthropic said Wednesday that Claude Duet is still in an early phase, and that it "might misread a thread or miscalibrate what's urgent."
The company opened a waitlist for Claude Duet on Wednesday, and said eligible users will be able to access it through a standalone app or through the Claude website. Claude Duet is available to Pro and Max subscribers during the preview.

articles.title: AIPAC retreats from candidate endorsements and direct giving as political backlash grows
articles.text:
The American Israel Public Affairs Committee, better known as AIPAC, plans to stop endorsing candidates, making direct PAC contributions and earmarking contributions to candidates. The shift reverses a strategy adopted five years ago as the influential pro-Israel group faces mounting political resistance.
The change was disclosed Wednesday in a letter to members obtained by CNBC. AIPAC will continue operating United Democracy Project, its super PAC, while putting greater emphasis on mobilizing individual donors to give directly to candidates, according to the letter.
Jewish Insider first reported the change.
"We're looking to dramatically expand our political involvement as a community and to heighten our activists' direct impact. That will be our focus in the next two years," AIPAC spokesperson Deryn Sousa told CNBC in a statement.
In the letter, however, the group called 2026 "one of the most challenging environments in recent memory" and warned those challenges "will continue to grow."
The overhaul strips away some of AIPAC's most visible political activity while preserving its ability to move large sums of money. It could also make AIPAC's influence harder to see in campaign finance records. Donations routed through the group are currently disclosed as AIPAC-earmarked contributions, while direct donations from its members would not carry the same label.
That distinction matters as AIPAC support has become a liability in some Democratic primaries amid the war in Gaza, with candidates attacking rivals for accepting its support and some lawmakers pledging to reject money tied to the group.
A Pew Research Center survey this year found that 80% of Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents held an unfavorable view of Israel, up from 53% in 2022.
AIPAC has deployed about $105.1 million through its traditional PAC and affiliated super PAC this cycle, according to a CNBC analysis of FEC filings. Its United Democracy Project reported $53.4 million in independent expenditures through the end of September, according to FEC filings.
AIPAC's traditional PAC was the nation's largest PAC contributor to candidates and other political committees in 2025, giving $26.8 million, according to FEC data. That was more than four times the $6.1 million given by the National Association of Realtors' PAC, the next-largest contributor.
AIPAC's biggest intervention of the cycle was also a major defeat. Its United Democracy Project super PAC spent more than $30 million in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary supporting Rep. Haley Stevens and opposing Abdul El-Sayed, according to a CNBC analysis of FEC filings, but El-Sayed narrowly won the nomination.
The super PAC also spent millions in House primaries opposing Democrats Cori Bush and Tom Malinowski and Republican Thomas Massie. According to a CNBC analysis of FEC filings, it spent more than $3 million in the Bush race, roughly $2.3 million against Malinowski and more than $4 million in the Kentucky primary where Massie was defeated.
United Democracy Project will continue operating, according to the letter, preserving AIPAC's ability to raise unlimited sums for independent political spending even as the group ends candidate endorsements, direct PAC contributions and earmarking.

articles.title: CoreWeave’s market confidence erodes as bond yields spike and stock sinks
articles.text:
CoreWeave is facing a crisis of confidence on Wall Street that's playing out in real time among equity and bond investors.
With interest rates spiking and AI build-out concerns mounting, debt-heavy neoclouds like CoreWeave are being viewed by many market participants as the most vulnerable trade in the artificial intelligence space.
"Sentiment is decidedly negative," Andrew Keches, a credit analyst at Barclays, wrote in a note to clients on Tuesday, referring broadly to corporate debt in tech. Keches highlighted the "speed at which AI vibes are shifting on a day-to-day basis."
CoreWeave, which went public in March of last year and reached a peak market cap of about $90 billion three months later, is now valued at roughly $34 billion, with its stock down 29% this month. Its unsecured debt, meanwhile, is sporting a yield of about 15%.
The spread on CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, is up 164% in the past year and 30% in October. It last stood at nearly 1,067 basis points, or 10.67%.
CoreWeave declined to comment.
The story is playing out across the neocloud sector. Shares of Nebius are down 27% this month, while IREN's stock is down 32%. In Australia, shares of data center operator NextDC plunged 40% on Wednesday after the company slashed its annual earnings forecast. Earlier this month, Australian data center company Firmus scrapped its planned initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions.
U.K. neocloud Nscale is now under the microscope as investors wait to see whether the Nvidia-backed company will go through with its IPO. The company filed to go public on the New York Stock Exchange last month.
A representative from Nscale declined to comment.
On hold until midterms
CoreWeave is the biggest of the pack, and is intimately tied to the U.S. AI market. Nvidia is its top institutional investor, with a stake of about 9%, according to FactSet. And more than two-thirds of CoreWeave's revenue last year came from Microsoft.
That's put a spotlight on CoreWeave's financials and its ability to remain viable. The company has about $20.7 billion in debt coming due through 2030 and another $14.9 billion thereafter, with the prospects of higher interest rates on future financing.
Sources on credit desks told CNBC that the high-yield debt market is effectively on hold until after the midterm elections in two weeks given ongoing concerns about the political pushback that data centers are facing. One source, who asked not to be named because of the sensitivity of the matter, said fixed income investors "want permitting and regulatory requirements to be substantially resolved" before they commit financing.
"Given recent turbulence, pausing makes sense," Seth Meyer, global head of client portfolio management at Janus Henderson, said in an interview.
CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator, who co-founded the company in 2017 initially as a crypto-mining venture, sent a memo to employees on Thursday, which CNBC obtained, to try and tamp down concern. Intrator stressed that the company maintains a range of funding options.
"Our financing model combines infrastructure-backed borrowing, corporate debt, equity, and customer prepayments," Intrator wrote. He added that the company has "additional flexibility to raise equity over time as market conditions and our capital needs warrant."
CoreWeave had $5.5 billion of cash and equivalents at the end of the second quarter. The company is expected to report third-quarter results next month. Analysts expect negative free cash flow in the period to swell to $10.1 billion, the highest since the company started reporting quarterly financials, according to FactSet.
One issue being debated heading into the report is how much more capital CoreWeave needs to raise. Rob Oliver, a software analyst at Baird, is estimating roughly $30 billion in 2027.
"Earnings may address financing measures to shore up confidence," Oliver said in an interview. "But they wouldn't need that capital until the first quarter."
Another question is whether Nvidia will step in if necessary?
Nvidia, which supplies the graphics processing units that CoreWeave rents out, invested $2 billion in January for a 10% stake. The purchase price was $87.20 a share. The stock is now trading at $61.82 even after jumping 6% the day of the announcement.
While Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said last week that CoreWeave doesn't need a backstop, some investors say the chip giant's further participation may be necessary if credit conditions continue to worsen.
Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
Analysts at Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase and Barclays have put out bullish notes on the company this week, highlighting the company's GPU-backed loans and its solid list of investment-grade customers like Microsoft and Meta. Goldman analysts emphasized the company's strength in the market relative to many of its neocloud competitors.
"Not all neoclouds are created equal," they wrote, in upgrading their rating to buy from hold. "CoreWeave is likely in the top quartile of neoclouds, if not the top decile, when measured on performance and ability to execute."
— CNBC's Michelle Fox and Jordan Novet contributed to this report.

articles.title: Southwest Airlines cuts 2026 profit forecast on higher fuel
articles.text:
Southwest Airlines became the third major U.S. airline this month to cut its 2026 profit forecast due to higher fuel prices, but CEO Bob Jordan said travelers continue to book despite higher fares.
The carrier expects to earn between $2.60 and $2.85 a share on an adjusted basis this year, down from its forecast in July of between $3.25 to as much as $4.25 a share.
Here's what Southwest reported for third quarter compared with Wall Street expectations, according to consensus estimates from LSEG:
- Earnings per share: 66 cents adjusted vs. 58 cents expected
- Revenue: $8.42 billion adjusted vs. $8.25 billion expected
Southwest forecast per-share adjusted earnings of between 55 cents and 80 cents in the fourth quarter and unit revenue, a gauge of airfare, up as much as 21% from a year earlier. It said it expects to grow capacity by up to 4% year over year.
"Demand remained strong as we lapped last year's bag fee and other commercial initiatives, reinforcing our belief that the earnings power we've built is durable, even with significantly higher fuel costs," Jordan said in an earnings release.
The airline said its average passenger fare was $231.69 in the third quarter, up almost 27% from the same quarter of 2025. A spokesman said that number does not include add-on fees. The number of revenue passengers carried fell 3.2% to 33.47 million people.
Under pressure to grow revenue, Southwest has been remaking its longtime business model over the past several years, scrapping its old policies like two free checked bags per passenger and open seating. In its place, Southwest has started charging for many seat assignments and added a bag fee, similar to major competitors.
For the third quarter, Southwest posted net income of $270 million, or 55 cents a share, up from $54 million or 10 cents a share a year earlier. Revenue rose more than 21% to $8.42 billion.
Adjusting for one-time items, Southwest reported 66 cents a share.
Delta Air Lines and United Airlines also cut their profit outlooks for the rest of the year when they reported third-quarter earnings. Both of those airlines reported top- and bottom-line misses for the third quarter.

articles.title: Trump denies ordering Starlink slowdown in Ukraine, says he doesn't know who did
articles.text:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday insisted he had nothing to do with a slowdown of SpaceX's Starlink in Ukraine and said he does not know if Elon Musk was responsible for speed-capping the critical satellite service.
Trump's latest denial came one day after The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed U.S. officials and people familiar with the matter, reported Musk ordered the slowdown and discussed it with Trump.
"I wasn't involved," Trump told a reporter when asked about the decision as he departed the White House for a campaign rally in South Carolina.
When pressed to answer if Musk, SpaceX's founder and CEO, ordered the slowdown, Trump said, "I don't know who did it, but I was not involved."
The recent disruption of Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, rendered some Ukrainian drones effectively useless, weakening defenses against Russian attacks.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday said his military still faces "speed restrictions on Starlink and Starshield services in different parts of the front."
"No explanation for either of these issues has been provided to Ukraine by the American side," he said.
The Journal reported Tuesday that Musk and Trump discussed the move to throttle Starlink "soon after" the change first became public last week, citing two people familiar with the matter.
One of the people who spoke with the news outlet claimed Musk discussed the matter with multiple senior administration officials, including Trump himself, prior to imposing the Starlink speed cap.
Trump and Musk have both recently ramped up their criticism of Zelenskyy. But neither of them has yet identified who ordered the Starlink disruption.
Musk said on X last week that Starshield systems are "owned and controlled by the US government" and that any speed or usage limits are "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Earlier Wednesday, Zelesnkyy said he and Norwegian Defense Minister Tore Sandvik "discussed in detail launching work on new satellite communication capabilities for our warriors."
"We will involve partners who have the capacity to provide support," Zelenskyy said in an X post.
Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday morning that he does not believe Musk would throttle Starlink without "at least the acquiescence of the White House."

articles.title: IBM beats on top and bottom lines as CEO Krishna touts 'Super Intelligence' traction
articles.text:
IBM shares slipped in extended trading on Wednesday after the technology vendor reported better-than-predicted third-quarter results.
Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus:
- Earnings: $2.95 adjusted vs. $2.86 expected
- Revenue: $17.10 billion vs. $16.82 billion expected
IBM's revenue grew about 5% from a year ago, according to a statement. Net income, at $2.19 billion, or $2.30 per share, increased from $1.74 billion, or $1.84 per share, a year ago. Adjusted earnings exclude acquisition-related adjustments.
"Our clients are now deploying 'Super Intelligence' in ways that transform entire operating models, instead of simply addressing narrow or novel problems," IBM CEO Arvind Krishna was quoted as saying in a statement.
With respect to guidance, IBM called for full-year free cash flow to increase by more than $1 billion. The forecast as of July was a bump of approximately $1 billion. IBM still sees 2026 constant-currency revenue growth between 4% and 5%.
In the third quarter, IBM generated $7.80 billion in software revenue, growing 8% and topping the $7.66 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount.
Consulting revenue, at $5.34 billion, was flat and just below StreetAccount's $5.37 billion consensus.
"AI is increasingly embedded in broader transformations our clients are undertaking, representing about 30% of our consulting revenue in the quarter and 35% of our backlog," Jim Kavanaugh, IBM's finance chief, said on a conference call with analysts.
The consulting unit's 27.4% gross margin narrowed from 28.9% in the second quarter.
"We reinvested productivity gains into digital assets, accelerating our transition towards a services as software model to capture the growing AI opportunity," Kavanaugh said.
Infrastructure revenue came to $3.70 billion. That was up 4% and higher than the $3.57 billion consensus from StreetAccount.
The company's adjusted gross margin, at 58.5%, was narrower than the StreetAccount consensus of 59.1%.
During the quarter, IBM said it agreed to buy Boeing and General Motors' HRL Laboratories, formerly known as Hughes Aircraft's research division, for an undisclosed sum.
As of Wednesday's close, IBM stock has come down 15%, while the S&P 500 index has gained 13%.
"I think the current street estimates for the year are about $32 billion of revenue," Kavanaugh said. "We feel comfortable with that $32 billion of revenue."
